Name.en: Ancient Building Complex in the Wudang Mountains

History_background.cn: 自唐代起为道教中心，明代鼎盛
History_background.en: It was a center of Taoism from the Tang Dynasty onwards, and reached its peak in the Ming Dynasty.

Main_function.cn: 道教活动与宗教研究中心
Main_function.en: Taoist Activities and Religious Studies Center

Brief_intro.cn: 自唐代以来的道教中心，现存53座古建筑和9处遗址，代表了元明清三代建筑艺术和中国道教发展，对明初政治与宗教史研究具有重要价值。
Brief_intro.en: A center of Taoism since the Tang Dynasty, it preserves 53 ancient buildings and 9 archaeological sites, representing the architectural arts of the Yuan, Ming, and Qing dynasties and the development of Chinese Taoism, with significant scholarly value for the study of early Ming political and religious history.

Standard.cn: 武当山的古代建筑代表了近千年来中国艺术和建筑的最高水平。
Standard.en: The ancient architecture of Wudang Mountain represents the highest level of Chinese art and architecture over the past thousand years.

Standard.cn: 武当建筑对中国宗教和公共艺术及建筑的发展产生了巨大的影响。
Standard.en: Wudang architecture has had a tremendous impact on the development of Chinese religious and public art and architecture.

Standard.cn: 武当山宗教建筑群是道教的中心，道教是东方主要宗教之一，对该地区信仰和哲学的发展起到了深远的作用。
Standard.en: The Wudang Mountain religious architectural complex is the center of Taoism, one of the major religions in the East, which has played a profound role in the development of beliefs and philosophy in the region.

Description.cn: 武当山古建筑群坐落于风景秀丽的湖北武当山群峰、沟壑之间。自唐代初期便作为道教中心而建立，部分道教建筑可追溯至公元7世纪。然而，现存建筑则展现了元、明、清三代中国世俗和宗教建筑的艺术成就。武当山古建筑群在明代达到鼎盛时期，拥有9座宫殿、9座寺院、36座尼姑庵和72座庙宇，这得益于朱棣皇帝为巩固其统治而发起的大规模修建工程。如今，53座古建筑和9处建筑遗址保存完好，其中包括建于1307年的金祠和古铜祠（均为青铜预制建筑）；以及建于1419年的石砌紫禁城。紫禁宫始建于12世纪，15世纪重建，19世纪扩建；南阳宫始建于12至13世纪；扶真寺始建于15至17世纪；以及建于1522年的石制智石玄岳门，作为武当山的入口标志。武当山建筑群展现了卓越的建筑艺术和技术，代表了近千年来中国艺术和建筑的最高水平。这些建筑既包括宗教建筑，也包括世俗建筑，与中国道教的发展密切相关，并得到了历代皇帝的慷慨资助。作为规模空前、保存完好的道教建筑群，它是研究明初政治和中国宗教史的重要实物资料。
Description.en: The palaces and temples of the Ancient Building Complex are located amongst the peaks, ravines and gullies of the picturesque Wudang Mountains, Hubei Province. Established as a Taoist centre from the early Tang Dynasty, some Taoist buildings could be traced back to the 7th century. However the surviving buildings exemplify the architectural and artistic achievements of China’s secular and religious buildings of the Yuan, Ming and Qing dynasties. The Ancient Building Complex reached its apogee during the Ming dynasty, with 9 palaces, 9 monasteries, 36 nunneries and 72 temples, following the major building campaign undertaken by Emperor Zhu Di to align his imperial regime with Taoism. Today, 53 ancient buildings and 9 architectural sites survive, including the Golden Shrine and the Ancient Bronze Shrine, which are prefabricated buildings in bronze made in 1307; the stone-walled Forbidden City of 1419; Purple Heaven Palace built originally in the 12th century, rebuilt in the 15th century and extended in the 19th century; the Nanyang Palace of the 12th and 13thcenturies; the Fuzhen Temple of the 15th and 17th centuries and the stone Zhishi-Xuanyue Gateway built to mark the entrance to the Wudang Mountains in 1522.The buildings in the Wudang Mountains exhibit exceptional architectural art and technology and represent the highest level of Chinese art and architecture achieved over a period of nearly 1,000 years. They are examples of religious and secular buildings closely associated with the growth of Taoism in China and lavishly endowed by successive Emperors. As an exceptionally large and well-preserved Taoist building complex it is important material evidence for studying early Ming politics and the Chinese history of religion.

History_background.cn: 始建于14世纪，明清时期代表
History_background.en: Originally built in the 14th century, it is a representative of the Ming and Qing dynasties.

Main_function.cn: 展现汉代城市历史风貌
Main_function.en: Showcasing the historical features of cities in the Han Dynasty

BUilding_use.cn: 古城墙、民居、寺庙等综合用途
BUilding_use.en: ancient city walls, residences, temples and other multi-purpose buildings

Brief_intro.cn: 保存完整，包含古城墙、街道、商铺、民居和寺庙，展现明清时期汉族城市风貌，是研究中国历史文化的重要遗址。
Brief_intro.en: Remarkably well preserved, it encompasses ancient city walls, streets, shops, residences, and temples, showcasing the Han Chinese urban landscape of the Ming and Qing dynasties and serving as an important site for the study of Chinese history and culture.

Standard.cn: 平遥古城的城镇景观出色地反映了五百年来中国古代建筑风格和城镇规划的演变，并融合了不同民族和中国其他地区的贡献。
Standard.en: The urban landscape of Pingyao Ancient City brilliantly reflects the evolution of ancient Chinese architectural styles and urban planning over the past five hundred years, and incorporates contributions from different ethnic groups and other parts of China.

Standard.cn: 平遥古城从19世纪到20世纪初是中国的金融中心。城内的商铺和传统民居是这一时期平遥古城经济繁荣的历史见证。
Standard.en: Pingyao Ancient City was China's financial center from the 19th to the early 20th century. The shops and traditional residences within the city are historical witnesses to the economic prosperity of Pingyao Ancient City during this period.

Standard.cn: 平遥古城是明清时期（14至20世纪）汉族城市的杰出代表，它以非凡的程度保留了所有特征。
Standard.en: Pingyao Ancient City is an outstanding representative of Han Chinese cities during the Ming and Qing Dynasties (14th to 20th centuries), and it has preserved all its features to an extraordinary degree.

Description.cn: 平遥古城是中国保存最完好的县级古城之一。它位于山西省中部平遥县，包括三部分：平遥城墙内的全部区域、位于县城西南6公里处的双林寺以及位于县城东北12公里处的振国寺。平遥古城很好地保留了14至20世纪汉族中原县级城市的历史风貌。平遥古城始建于14世纪，占地225公顷，是一座完整的建筑群，包括古城墙、街道巷弄、商铺、民居和寺庙。其布局完美地体现了汉代城市五百多年来的建筑风格和城市规划发展历程。尤其值得一提的是，从19世纪到20世纪初，平遥古城曾是全国的金融中心。城内现存近4000座气势恢宏、装饰精美的传统民居，见证了平遥一个世纪以来的经济繁荣。双林寺拥有2000多件明清时期的彩绘雕塑，素有“东方彩绘雕塑艺术馆”之称。万佛祠是镇国寺的主殿，始建于五代，是中国现存最早、最珍贵的木结构建筑之一。平遥古城是明清时期（14至20世纪）汉代城市的杰出代表，完整地保留了汉代城市的所有特征，展现了中国历史上文化、社会、经济和宗教发展的完整图景，对于研究社会形态、经济结构、军事防御、宗教信仰、传统思想、传统伦理和居住形式具有重要价值。
Description.en: The Ancient City of Ping Yao is a well-preserved ancient county-level city in China. Located in Ping Yao County, central Shanxi Province, the property includes three parts: the entire area within the walls of Ping Yao, Shuanglin Temple 6 kilometers southwest of the county seat, and Zhenguo Temple 12 kilometers northeast of the county seat. The Ancient City of Ping Yao well retains the historic form of the county-level cities of the Han people in Central China from the 14th to 20th century.Founded in the 14th century and covering an area of 225 hectares, the Ancient City of Ping Yao is a complete building complex including ancient walls, streets and lanes, shops, dwellings and temples. Its layout reflects perfectly the developments in architectural style and urban planning of the Han cities over more than five centuries. Particularly, from the 19th century to the early 20th century, the Ancient City of Ping Yao was a financial center for the whole of China. The nearly 4,000 existing shops and traditional dwellings in the town which are grand in form and exquisite in ornament bear witness to Ping Yao’s economic prosperity over a century. With more than 2,000 existing painted sculptures made in the Ming and Qing dynasties, Shuanglin Temple has been reputed as an “oriental art gallery of painted sculptures”. Wanfo Shrine, the main shrine of Zhenguo Temple, dating back to the Five Dynasties, is one of China’s earliest and most precious timber structure buildings in existence.The Ancient City of Ping Yao is an outstanding example of Han cities in the Ming and Qing dynasties (from the 14th to 20th century). It retains all the Han city features, provides a complete picture of the cultural, social, economic and religious development in Chinese history, and it is of great value for studying the social form, economic structure, military defense, religious belief, traditional thinking, traditional ethics and dwelling form.

Name.cn: 皖南古村落－西递、宏村（2000年）
Name.en: Ancient Villages in Southern Anhui – Xidi and Hongcun

History_background.cn: 14至20世纪安徽村落原始风貌
History_background.en: Original features of Anhui villages from the 14th to the 20th centuries

Main_function.cn: 传统村落，展示徽文化
Main_function.en: Traditional villages showcasing Hui culture

Brief_intro.cn: 以商业活动为主要收入来源，家庭和氏族社会组织，以其区域文化闻名。整体布局、景观、建筑形态、装饰和施工技术均保留了14至20世纪安徽村庄的原始特征。
Brief_intro.en: Supported primarily by commercial activities and organized around family and clan social structures, these villages are renowned for their regional culture. Their overall layouts, landscapes, architectural forms, decorative styles, and construction techniques faithfully preserve the original character of Anhui villages from the 14th to the 20th century.

Standard.cn: 西递村和宏村是封建时期建立在繁荣的贸易经济基础上的人类聚落的典型例子。
Standard.en: Xidi Village and Hongcun Village are typical examples of human settlements built on a prosperous trade economy during the feudal period.

Standard.cn: 安徽南部这两个村庄的建筑和街道格局反映了中国历史上长期定居时期的社会经济结构。
Standard.en: The architecture and street layout of these two villages in southern Anhui reflect the socio-economic structure of China during a long period of settlement in history.

Standard.cn: 中国传统的非城市聚落，在过去一个世纪中很大程度上已经消失，但在西递和宏村的村庄里却保存得异常完好。
Standard.en: Traditional non-urban settlements in China have largely disappeared over the past century, but they have been remarkably well preserved in the villages of Xidi and Hongcun.

Description.cn: 西递和宏村是位于安徽省黄山市义县的两个杰出的传统村落，以商业活动为主要收入来源，社会组织以家族和宗族为基础，并以其独特的地域文化而闻名。其整体布局、景观、建筑形式、装饰和建造技术均保留了14至20世纪安徽村落的原始风貌。西递和宏村深受安徽近代以前传统文化的影响，由功成名就的官员或商人从官府或经商归来后兴建，逐渐发展成为中国传统村落建设的典范。西递群山环绕，依三条东西走向的溪流而建，南面汇聚于惠源桥。宏村则位于山脚下，溪水潺潺流淌，形成两个水池：村中心的月亮池和南面的池塘。村落空间韵律优美，巷道幽静，水源来自风景如画的园林，整体体现了人与自然和谐共生的理念。建筑风格独特而精致，以朴素雅致的色彩为主，山墙雕刻精美雅致，室内陈设雅致考究。森严的父权制度与温和真诚的民俗风情，反映了封建社会士大夫的文化思想，他们对儒家和新儒家思想推崇备至。这些幸存下来的村落拥有六百多年的历史，蕴含着丰富的科学、文化和美学价值，是研究区域历史和文化的宝贵资料。
Description.en: Xidi and Hongcun are two outstanding traditional villages, located in Yi County, Huangshan City in south Anhui Province, with commercial activities as their primary source of income, family and clan-based social organization, and well known for their regional culture. The overall layout, landscape, architectural form, decoration, and construction techniques all retain the original features of Anhui villages between the 14th and 20th centuries.Deeply influenced by the traditional culture of pre-modern Anhui Province, these two villages, Xidi and Hongcun, were built by successful officials or merchants returning home from official appointments and business, and gradually developed into models of conventional Chinese village construction. Xidi is surrounded by mountains and built along and between three streams running east-west, which converge at the Huiyuan Bridge to the south. Hongcun is located at the foot of a hill next to a stream which forms two pools, the Moon Pond in the centre of the village and the other to the south. Characterised by rhythmic space variation and tranquil alleyways; and with water originating from a picturesque garden, the whole reflects the pursuit of coexistence, unity and the harmony of man and nature. The unique and exquisite style of Anhui buildings is conveyed in plain and elegant colors, their gables decorated with delicate and elegant carvings, their interiors filled with tasteful furnishings. The rigid patriarchal system together with gentle and sincere folk customs reflects the cultural ideas of scholar-bureaucrats in feudal society who paid special respect to Confucianism and Neo-Confucianism. These surviving villages bear scientific, cultural and aesthetic values with their 600-plus-year history. They are rich sources for the study of regional histories and cultures.

History_background.cn: 中国新石器时代晚期的早期国家遗址
History_background.en: Early state sites in the late Neolithic period of China

Main_function.cn: 权力和信仰中心
Main_function.en: Center of Power and Faith

Brief_intro.cn: 向人们展示了新石器时代晚期一个以稻作农业为支撑、具有统一信仰的早期区域性国家。该遗址由4个部分组成：瑶山遗址区、谷口高坝区、平原低坝区和城址区。
Brief_intro.en: Revealing a late Neolithic early regional state sustained by rice cultivation and united by a shared belief system, the site comprises four components: the Yaoshan ceremonial area, the highland dam system, the lowland dam system, and the walled city zone.

Standard.cn: 良渚城遗址作为良渚文化的权力和信仰中心，是新石器时代晚期长江下游地区以水稻种植农业为经济基础、社会分化且信仰体系统一的早期区域国家的杰出见证。它为研究中国及该地区新石器时代晚期至青铜时代早期的文化认同、社会政治组织以及社会文化发展提供了无可比拟的证据。
Standard.en: The Liangzhu City site, as the power and belief center of the Liangzhu culture, is outstanding evidence of an early regional state in the lower Yangtze River region during the late Neolithic period, characterized by rice cultivation as its economic foundation, social differentiation, and a unified belief system. It provides unparalleled evidence for the study of cultural identity, socio-political organization, and socio-cultural development in China and the region from the late Neolithic to the early Bronze Age.

Standard.cn: 良渚遗址展现了新石器时代小型社会向具有等级制度、礼仪和工艺的大型综合政治单元的过渡。它包含了早期城市化的杰出范例，体现在土质纪念碑、城市和景观规划、墓葬差异所体现的社会等级、空间组织的社会文化策略以及权力的物质化等方面。它代表了5000多年前中国史前水稻种植文明的伟大成就，也是早期城市文明的杰出典范。
Standard.en: The Liangzhu site showcases the transition from small Neolithic societies to large, integrated political units with hierarchical systems, rituals, and crafts. It contains outstanding examples of early urbanization, manifested in earthen monuments, urban and landscape planning, social hierarchy reflected in burial differences, socio-cultural strategies for spatial organization, and the materialization of power. It represents the great achievements of prehistoric rice-cultivating civilization in China more than 5,000 years ago and is an outstanding example of early urban civilization.

Description.cn: 良渚古城遗址位于中国东南沿海长江流域天目山东麓，地处河流纵横的平原之上，是太湖周边早期区域国家的权力和信仰中心。该地块由四个区域组成：瑶山地块；谷口高坝区；平原低坝区——山前堤道区；以及城市地块。良渚古城遗址展现了中国新石器时代晚期以水稻种植为经济基础的早期区域性国家，以及社会分化和统一的信仰体系。该遗址包含一系列遗址，包括建于公元前3300-2300年左右的城址、功能复杂的周边水利系统和社会等级分明的墓地（包括祭坛），以及出土的象征信仰体系和早期历史的玉器等文物，充分体现了长江流域对中华文明起源的卓越贡献。此外，都城的格局和功能分区，以及良渚文化聚落和外城梯田的特征，都强有力地支撑了该遗址的价值。
Description.en: The Archaeological Ruins of Liangzhu City was the centre of power and belief of an early regional state in the Circum-Taihu Lake Area. It is located on a plain criss-crossed by river networks in the eastern foothills of the Tianmu Mountains in the Yangtze River Basin on the southeast coast of China.The property is composed of four areas: Area of Yaoshan Site; Area of High-dam at the Mouth of the Valley; Area of Low-dam on the Plain – Causeway in Front of the Mountains; and Area of City Site.The Archaeological Ruins of Liangzhu City reveals an early regional state with rice-cultivating agriculture as its economic base, and social differentiation and a unified belief system, which existed in the Late Neolithic period in China. With a series of sites, including the City Site built during ca. 3300-2300 BCE, the Peripheral Water Conservancy System with complex functions and socially-graded cemeteries (including an altar), and the excavated objects represented by series of jade artefacts symbolizing the belief system, as well as its early age, the property represents the remarkable contributions made by the Yangtze River Basin to the origins of Chinese civilization. In addition, the pattern and functional zoning of the capital, together with the characteristics of the settlements of the Liangzhu culture and of the Outer City with the terraces, support strongly the value of the property.

Name.cn: 北京中轴线：中国理想都城秩序的杰作
Name.en: Beijing Central Axis: A Building Ensemble Exhibiting the Ideal Order of the Chinese Capital

History_background.cn: 起源于元代，历经明清修建
History_background.en: Originating in the Yuan Dynasty, and renovated during the Ming and Qing Dynasties

Main_function.cn: 见证北京城市发展与规划
Main_function.en: Witnessing Beijing's Urban Development and Planning

BUilding_use.cn: 皇家宫殿、祭祀与管理设施
BUilding_use.en: Royal palaces, religious and administrative facilities

Brief_intro.cn: 由昔日的皇宫和园林、祭祀建筑以及礼仪和公共建筑组成。它们共同见证了城市的发展历程，展现了中国皇朝制度和城市规划传统的痕迹。
Brief_intro.en: Comprising former imperial palaces and gardens, sacrificial buildings, and ceremonial and public structures, these ensembles collectively bear witness to the city's development and reflect the enduring imprint of China's imperial system and urban planning traditions.

Standard.cn: 北京中轴线对全球城市规划史做出了重要贡献，其独特的特征反映了中国帝制时期发展起来的文化和政治体系。这种城市规划传统影响了其他东亚和东南亚首都的规划。用于城市布局设计的规划原则，包括南北轴线的界定和“中心”的建立，体现了儒家思想，这些思想体现在《高工记》中，旨在通过城市布局的对称与平衡，为社会带来中立与和谐。这种城市规划方法的礼仪维度还要求寺庙的布局与中轴线保持平衡，并与季节性庆典所体现的农业祭祀历法相联系。这种平衡与对称，以及寺庙和中心的具体元素，在遗址中仍然清晰可见，并得到了很好的保存。这种城市规划传统一直延续到帝制结束，此后，它虽然影响深远，但也随着现代实践的演变而发生了转变。尽管如此，与古代农业历法相关的庆祝活动仍在举行，包括组成该轴线的一些寺庙中的仪式。
Standard.en: The central axis of Beijing has made significant contributions to the history of global urban planning, its unique features reflecting the cultural and political system that developed during China's imperial period. This urban planning tradition influenced the planning of other East Asian and Southeast Asian capitals. The planning principles used in urban layout design, including the definition of the north-south axis and the establishment of the "center," embody Confucianism, as reflected in the *Gaogongji* (Record of High Engineers), which aimed to bring neutrality and harmony to society through the symmetry and balance of urban layout. The ritual dimension of this urban planning approach also required temples to be laid out in balance with the central axis and linked to the agricultural sacrificial calendar reflected in seasonal celebrations. This balance and symmetry, along with the specific elements of temples and the center, are still clearly visible and well-preserved in the ruins. This urban planning tradition continued until the end of the imperial period, and although its influence was profound thereafter, it also changed with the evolution of modern practices. Nevertheless, celebrations related to the ancient agricultural calendar are still held, including ceremonies in some of the temples that make up the axis.

Standard.cn: 北京中轴线是保存异常完好的城市群落范例，其发展基于古代城市规划理论，并以儒家思想为基础，将礼仪维度融入城市规划、政治和治理之中。在帝制王朝时期，随着北京的扩张和城市化，考公基的原则在中轴线上得以延续，展现了一种独特的城市格局，代表了世界城市史上一种特殊的类型，这种类型起源于中国帝制王朝体系并得以发展。
Standard.en: The central axis of Beijing is an exceptionally well-preserved example of an urban cluster. Its development is based on ancient urban planning theories and grounded in Confucianism, integrating the dimension of etiquette into urban planning, politics, and governance. During the imperial dynasties, with the expansion and urbanization of Beijing, the principle of "kaogongji" (a system of ceremonial foundations) continued along the central axis, showcasing a unique urban pattern that represents a special type in the history of world cities, originating from and developing within the Chinese imperial dynastic system.

Description.cn: 北京中轴线贯穿北京历史中心，南北贯通。它由昔日的皇家宫殿和园林、皇家祭祀建筑、古代城市管理设施、礼仪和公共建筑以及中轴线道路遗迹构成。这条轴线见证了北京的城市发展历程，展现了中国王朝制度和城市规划传统的精髓。中轴线的位置、布局、城市格局和设计体现了《高工记》中描绘的理想都城模式。《高工记》是一部古代典籍，又称《杂工书》。中轴线起源于元代（1271-1368年），元代将都城大都建于中轴线北段。此外，该区域还包含明代（1368-1644年）建造和清代（1636-1912年）修缮的历史建筑。
Description.en: Beijing Central Axis runs from north to south through the heart of historical Beijing. It is defined by former imperial palaces and gardens, imperial sacrificial buildings, ancient city management facilities, ceremonial and public buildings and Central Axis roads remains. The Axis bears testimony to the evolution of the city exhibiting evidence of the imperial dynastic system and urban planning traditions of China. The location, layout, urban pattern and design of the Axis showcase the ideal capital city paradigm prescribed in the Kaogongji, an ancient text known as the Book of Diverse Crafts. The Central Axis originated in the Yuan Dynasty (1271-1368) that established Dadu, its capital, in what corresponds to the northern section of the Axis. The property also features later historical structures built during the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644) and improved during the Qing Dynasty (1636-1912).

Name.cn: 高句丽王城、王陵及贵族墓葬
Name.en: Capital Cities and Tombs of the Ancient Koguryo Kingdom

Dynast.cn: 周朝(公元前1046年 - 公元前256年)

History_background.cn: 高句丽王国公元前37年建都，至公元7世纪
History_background.en: The Goguryeo Kingdom established its capital in 37 BC and lasted until the 7th century AD.

Main_function.cn: 高句丽时期的都城与王族陵墓
Main_function.en: Capital cities and royal tombs during the Goguryeo period

BUilding_use.cn: 政治、经济、军事和居住中心
BUilding_use.en: Political, economic, military and residential center

Brief_intro.cn: 陵墓遗址包括乌奴山城、国内城、万都山城及40座陵墓，是某文明的重要遗迹，反映了其的城市布局、建筑风格和丧葬文化，对后世有深远影响。
Brief_intro.en: The site encompasses Wunü Mountain City, Guonei City, Wandu Mountain City, and 40 royal tombs, representing the important remains of the Koguryo civilization and reflecting its urban planning, architectural style, and funerary culture, which had a profound and lasting influence on later generations.

Standard.cn: 陵墓的壁画和结构是人类创造性天才的杰作
Standard.en: The murals and structure of the tomb are masterpieces of human creative genius.

Standard.cn: 高句丽王国的都城是早期山地城市的典范，后被邻近文化竞相效仿。墓葬，尤其是其中一座墓葬中的重要石碑和长篇铭文，展现了中国文化对高句丽（他们没有发展出自己的文字）的影响。墓葬中的绘画，虽然展现了高超的艺术技巧和独特的风格，但也体现了其他文化的强烈影响。
Standard.en: The capital of the Goguryeo Kingdom was a model of early mountain cities, later imitated by neighboring cultures. The tombs, especially the important stele and lengthy inscription in one of them, demonstrate the influence of Chinese culture on Goguryeo (who did not develop their own writing system). The paintings in the tombs, while showcasing superb artistic skill and a unique style, also reflect the strong influence of other cultures.

Standard.cn: 古代高句丽王国的都城和陵墓是已消失的高句丽文明的杰出见证。
Standard.en: The capital and tombs of the ancient Goguryeo Kingdom are outstanding testaments to the vanished Goguryeo civilization.

Standard.cn: 国内城和万度山城所代表的都城体系也影响了高句丽政权后来建造的都城；高句丽陵墓为堆石墓和土墓建筑的演变提供了杰出的例证。
Standard.en: The capital city system represented by Gungnae Fortress and Mandosan Fortress also influenced the capital cities later built by the Goguryeo regime; Goguryeo tombs provide excellent examples of the evolution of stone mound tombs and earthen tombs.

Standard.cn: 高句丽王国的都城体现了人类创造与自然的完美融合，无论是与岩石，还是与森林和河流。
Standard.en: The capital of the Goguryeo Kingdom embodies a perfect fusion of human creation and nature, whether in relation to rocks, forests, or rivers.

Description.cn: 位于中国东北的古代高句丽王国都城和陵墓，其历史可追溯至公元前1世纪至公元7世纪，包括三座城市和40座陵墓的考古遗址：辽宁省环人满族自治县的乌奴山城；吉林省吉安市的国内城、万都山城和40座陵墓。高句丽王国自公元前37年起成为一个区域性强国和民族国家，直至公元427年迁都平壤。在王国早期和中期，乌努山城、国内城和万度山城都曾是高句丽的都城。乌努山城始建于公元前37年，是高句丽政权的第一个都城。城墙环绕，设有三座城门，部分城墙由石头砌成，部分则利用悬崖峭壁而建。城内包括宫殿、军营、瞭望塔、民居和仓库。国内城，如今位于集安市内，建于平原之上，同样拥有石砌城墙，宫殿区和民居区分开来。万度山城是高句丽唯一一座以大型宫殿为核心进行整体规划的山城，完美地融合了高句丽文化与自然环境。国内城和万度山城在数百年间一直是高句丽的经济、政治和文化中心。国内城于公元197年高句丽战败时被毁。完度山城则建于公元209年。这两座城市都曾多次在战乱中损毁重建，并交替作为都城。高句丽主都迁至平壤后，国内城成为辅助都城；它是少数几座至今仍保留着石砌城墙的平原城市遗址之一。高句丽古代君主和贵族的陵墓分布在万都山城东沟古墓群。十二座帝王陵呈阶梯金字塔形，由石头砌成，墓室顶部覆盖瓦片。贵族陵墓为石砌墓室，覆以土堆，内壁绘有壁画，描绘了日常生活、运动、狩猎、自然风光、神灵、仙女和龙等场景。公元414年溥台王碑记载了高句丽王朝的建立。这些都城和陵墓是已消失的高句丽文明的珍贵见证。都城的布局和建筑风格影响了后世的城市规划和建设。墓葬壁画是中世纪东北亚罕见的艺术表现形式，与碑刻和铭文一起展现了中国文化对高句丽的影响。
Description.en: Located in northeast China, the Capital Cities and Tombs of the Ancient Koguryo Kingdom dating from the 1st century BCE to the 7th century CE comprise archaeological remains of three cities and 40 tombs: Wunu Mountain City in Huanren Manchu Autonomous County, Liaoning Province; Guonei City, Wandu Mountain City, and the 40 tombs in Ji’an municipality, Jilin Province.The Koguryo kingdom was a regional power and ethnic group from the year 37BCE until the kingdom moved its capital to Pyonyang in 427CE.Wunu Mountain City, Guonei City and Wandu Mountain City served as capitals of Koguryo during the early and middle period of the Kingdom. Wunu Mountain City was built in 37BCE as the first capital of the Koguryo regime. Surrounded by a defensive wall with three gates which was partly built in stone and in other places exploited the cliff face, the city included a palace, military camp, watch tower, houses and warehouses.  Guonei City, now surrounded by the city of Ji’an, was built on the plain with a stone-built defensive wall and had separate palace and residential zones. Wandu Mountain City, the only Koguryo mountain city capital whose general layout was planned with the large palace as its core, created a mountain city that perfectly combined the Koguryo culture with the natural environment. Guonei City and Wandu Mountain City were the economic, political and cultural centers of the Koguryo for hundreds of years. Guonei City was destroyed in the year 197 CE when the Koguryo were defeated by another power. Wandu Mountain City was built in 209 CE. Both cities were damaged in wars and rebuilt several times, serving alternately as the capital. Guonei City played the role of a supporting capital after the main Koguryo capital moved to Pyongyang; it is one of the few plains city sites with stone city walls still standing.The tombs of kings and nobles of the ancient Koguryo Kingdom are distributed in the Donggou Ancient Tombs Area of Wandu Mountain City. The 12 imperial tombs take a stepped pyramid form constructed of stone. The burial chambers within were roofed with clay tiles. The tombs of the nobles have stone chambers covered with earth mounds and are decorated with wall paintings, depicting scenes of daily life, sports, hunting, nature, gods, fairies, and dragons. The stele of King Haotaiwang dating from 414CE, tells the story of the founding of the Koguryo kingdom.The capital cities and tombs are exceptional testimony to the vanished Koguryo civilisation. The layout and construction of the capital cities influenced the city planning and building of later cultures. The tomb paintings represent a rare artistic expression in medieval North-east Asia and together with the stele and inscriptions show the impact of Chinese culture on the Koguryo.

History_background.cn: 苏州园林始于公元前6世纪吴国都城
History_background.en: Suzhou gardens originated in the capital of the Wu Kingdom in the 6th century BC.

Main_function.cn: 都市生活中隐居和赏景之地
Main_function.en: A secluded place for sightseeing in urban life

BUilding_use.cn: 宅邸内模拟自然的园林景观
BUilding_use.en: The mansion features a natural-style garden landscape.

Brief_intro.cn: 中国山水园林典范，以精湛工艺、艺术格调和文化内涵著称，融合建筑、自然景观及诗意，体现了中国古典园林设计“咫尺之内再造乾坤”的理想。
Brief_intro.en: Exemplars of Chinese landscape garden design, renowned for their exquisite craftsmanship, artistic refinement, and cultural depth, these gardens harmonize architecture, natural scenery, and poetic expression, embodying the classical Chinese ideal of recreating the cosmos within a confined space.

Standard.cn: 苏州古典园林深受中国传统工艺和艺术的影响，其精髓最早体现在传统中国绘画的自由笔法中，体现了中国传统文化的精致与优雅。这种艺术上的完美体现，使苏州古典园林赢得了“中国古代最具创意园林杰作”的美誉。
Standard.en: Suzhou's classical gardens are deeply influenced by traditional Chinese craftsmanship and art. Their essence was first embodied in the free brushstrokes of traditional Chinese painting, reflecting the refinement and elegance of traditional Chinese culture. This perfect artistic expression has earned Suzhou's classical gardens the reputation of being "the most creative masterpieces of ancient Chinese gardens."

Standard.cn: 在两千多年的时间跨度内，针对这类特定类型的花园，形成了一种独特而系统的景观设计形式。其规划、设计、建造技术以及艺术效果，对中国乃至世界景观设计的发展都产生了重大影响。
Standard.en: Over a period of more than two thousand years, a unique and systematic landscape design form has developed for this specific type of garden. Its planning, design, construction techniques, and artistic effects have had a significant impact on the development of landscape design in China and even the world.

Standard.cn: 苏州古典园林最初源于古代中国知识分子在修身养性的同时追求与自然和谐相处的愿望，是古代中国知识分子智慧和传统的最佳遗存。
Standard.en: Suzhou's classical gardens originated from the desire of ancient Chinese intellectuals to live in harmony with nature while cultivating their character. They are the best legacy of the wisdom and tradition of ancient Chinese intellectuals.

Standard.cn: 苏州古典园林是11至19世纪长江东三角地区景观园林设计文化的最生动体现。其建筑、园林和手工艺中所蕴含的哲学、文学、艺术和工艺，反映了这一时期社会、文化、科学和技术发展的巨大成就。
Standard.en: The classical gardens of Suzhou are the most vivid embodiment of landscape garden design culture in the Yangtze River Delta region from the 11th to the 19th centuries. The philosophy, literature, art, and craftsmanship embodied in their architecture, gardens, and handicrafts reflect the tremendous achievements of social, cultural, scientific, and technological development during this period.

Standard.cn: 这些经典的苏州园林是传统中国民居与精心设计的自然环境和谐共存的杰出范例。它们展现了11至19世纪长江三角洲东部地区的生活方式、礼仪和习俗。
Standard.en: These classic Suzhou gardens are outstanding examples of the harmonious coexistence of traditional Chinese dwellings and a meticulously designed natural environment. They showcase the lifestyle, etiquette, and customs of the eastern Yangtze River Delta region from the 11th to the 19th centuries.

Description.cn: 中国江苏省苏州的古典园林可追溯至公元前6世纪，当时苏州建城，成为吴国的都城。受吴王所建皇家狩猎园林的启发，私人园林于公元4世纪左右开始兴起，并在18世纪达到鼎盛时期。如今，苏州仍保存着50多座古典园林，其中九座被誉为中国“山水园林”的典范之作，分别是拙政园、留园、网师园、抱美山庄、苍浪阁、狮子林、栽培园、情侣园和静思园。苍浪阁是其中最早的，建于11世纪初，其前身是一座已被毁的园林。这些园林的设计与建造深受中国传统山水画中自由奔放的诗意风格的影响，以其精湛的工艺、优雅的艺术格调和丰富的文化内涵而著称。它们展现了古代中国知识分子如何在都市生活环境中，于隐居的文化氛围中，和谐地融合了美学理念。历代园林大师运用各种技法，巧妙地利用有限的空间，模拟自然，营造出独特的景观。古典苏州园林局限于宅邸之内，旨在成为自然世界的缩影，融合了水、石、植物等基本元素，以及各种具有文学诗意的建筑。这些精美的园林是当时园林大师高超技艺的体现。这些独特的园林设计，既源于自然，又超越了自然概念的局限，对东西方园林艺术的发展产生了深远的影响。这些由建筑、假山、书法、家具和装饰艺术品组成的园林群落，是长江东三角地区艺术成就的杰出代表，也是中国传统文化内涵的精髓所在。
Description.en: The classical gardens of Suzhou, Jiangsu Province, China date back to the 6th century BCE when the city was founded as the capital of the Wu Kingdom. Inspired by these royal hunting gardens built by the King of the State of Wu, private gardens began emerging around the 4th century and finally reached the climax in the 18th century. Today, more than 50 of these gardens are still in existence, nine of which, namely the Humble Administrator’s Garden, Lingering Garden, Net Master’s Garden, the Mountain Villa with Embracing Beauty, the Canglang Pavilion, the Lion Grove Garden, the Garden of Cultivation, the Couple’s Garden Retreat, and the Retreat & Reflection Garden, are regarded as the finest embodiments of Chinese “Mountain and Water” gardens. The earliest of these, the Canglang Pavilionwas built in the early 11th century on the site of an earlier, destroyed garden. Conceived and built under the influence of the unconstrained poetic freehand style originally seen in traditional Chinese landscape paintings, they are noted for their profound merging of exquisite craftsmanship, artistic elegance and rich cultural implications. These gardens lend insight into how ancient Chinese intellectuals harmonized conceptions of aestheticism in a culture of reclusion within an urban living environment.Garden masters from each dynasty adapted various techniques to artfully simulate nature by skillfully adapting and utilizing only the physical space available to them. Limited to the space within a single residence, classical Suzhou gardens are intended to be a microcosm of the natural world, incorporating basic elements such as water, stones, plants, and various types of buildings of literary and poetic significance. These exquisite gardens are a testament to the superior craftsmanship of the garden masters of the time. These unique designs that have been inspired but are not limited by concepts of nature have had profound influence on the evolution of both Eastern and Western garden art. These garden ensembles of buildings, rock formations, calligraphy, furniture, and decorative artistic pieces serve as showcases of the paramount artistic achievements of the East Yangtze Delta region; they are in essence the embodiment of the connotations of traditional Chinese culture.

Name.cn: 红河哈尼梯田文化景观
Name.en: Cultural Landscape of Honghe Hani Rice Terraces

City.cn: 云南省红河哈尼族彝族自治州
City.en: Honghe Hani and Yi Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province

History_background.cn: 哈尼族1300年前迁徙至此开垦梯田
History_background.en: The Hani people migrated here 1,300 years ago and began cultivating terraced fields.

Main_function.cn: 稻田种植与灌溉
Main_function.en: Rice paddy planting and irrigation

Brief_intro.cn: 当地人创造的复杂灌溉稻田系统，展现人与自然的和谐生态，包含森林、梯田和传统村落，体现独特的社会与宗教结构。
Brief_intro.en: A sophisticated irrigated terrace system created by local communities, this cultural landscape demonstrates the ecological harmony between people and nature through its integrated forests, terraced fields, and traditional villages, reflecting a unique social and religious structure.

Standard.cn: 红河-哈尼梯田是精心设计和精细协调的农业、林业和水利分配系统的杰出体现，这些系统得到了长期存在的独特社会经济宗教体系的强化。红米是梯田的主要作物，其种植依赖于一套复杂而综合的农牧系统。在这个系统中，鸭子为幼苗施肥，鸡和猪为成熟植株提供肥料，水牛翻耕田地为来年播种做准备，梯田水中的蜗牛则捕食各种害虫。水稻种植过程依托于一套精细的社会、经济和宗教体系，这套体系通过对土地和更广泛社区的义务，加强了人们与环境的联系，并肯定了自然的圣洁。这种被称为“人神合一社会体系”的双重相互依存体系，以及梯田的形态，共同构成了一种至今仍然鲜活的独特文化传统。
Standard.en: The Honghe-Hani Rice Terraces are a prime example of a meticulously designed and coordinated system of agricultural, forestry, and water management, reinforced by a long-standing and unique socio-economic and religious system. Red rice is the main crop of the terraces, its cultivation relying on a complex and integrated agricultural and pastoral system. In this system, ducks fertilize the seedlings, chickens and pigs provide fertilizer for mature plants, water buffalo plow the fields in preparation for the following year's planting, and snails in the terrace waters prey on various pests. The rice cultivation process is based on a sophisticated social, economic, and religious system that strengthens the connection between people and the environment and affirms the sanctity of nature through obligations to the land and the wider community. This dual interdependence, known as a "human-divine unity social system," together with the form of the terraces, constitutes a unique cultural tradition that remains vibrant to this day.

Standard.cn: 红河哈尼梯田景观以独特的方式反映了人与环境的特殊互动，这种互动是通过综合农业和水资源管理系统实现的，并以社会经济宗教系统为基础，表达了人与神、个人与社群之间的双重关系。这一系统至少持续了一千年，大量的档案资料可以证明这一点。
Standard.en: The Honghe Hani Rice Terraces landscape uniquely reflects the special interaction between humans and the environment. This interaction is achieved through an integrated agricultural and water resource management system, and is based on a socio-economic and religious system, expressing a dual relationship between humans and gods, and between the individual and the community. This system has lasted for at least a thousand years, as evidenced by a wealth of archival materials.

Description.cn: 在云南南部山区，红河南岸，红河哈尼梯田层层叠叠地从哀牢山脉巍峨的山坡上倾泻而下。这些梯田是哈尼族人在过去1300年间，从更西北方向迁徙至此，在茂密的森林中开垦而成。梯田灌溉系统支撑着俯瞰狭窄山谷的稻田。在某些地方，从森林边缘到谷底之间，竟有多达3000层梯田。面对高山、沟壑纵横的狭窄山谷、极高的降雨量（约 1400 毫米）和亚热带山谷气候等环境带来的困难和机遇，哈尼人从茂密的森林中创造出了一个极其复杂的灌溉梯田系统，该系统沿着山脉的轮廓蜿蜒而行。该遗产地占地约1000平方公里。位于马里寨、达瓦泽和阿勐空-格塔三个流域内的巴达、多依树和老虎嘴三个梯田区域，反映了不同的地质特征。巴达梯田坡度平缓，多依树梯田坡度较陡，老虎嘴梯田坡度则非常陡峭。这片土地展现出森林、水源、梯田和房屋四者相互交融的生态系统。山顶森林是梯田的生命之源，它蓄积并维持着灌溉所需的水源。森林分为四种类型：古老的“补给林”、神圣森林、巩固林和村庄林，村庄林为建筑、粮食和柴火提供木材。神圣森林至今仍具有重要的象征意义。村庄上方供奉着村神“昂玛”（村庄的灵魂）和土地守护神“米松”，村民们在此祈求和平、健康和繁荣。岩石缝隙引导雨水流入，花岗岩山脉下的砂岩截留雨水，随后以泉水的形式释放出来。为了将这些水输送到不同山谷及其间的梯田，人们开发了一套复杂的水渠系统。该系统由公共部门维护，包括四条主干渠和392条支渠，总长度达445.83公里。在山顶森林下方梯田之上，建有82个相对较小的村庄，每个村庄约有50至100户人家。传统的民居建筑以夯土、土坯砖或泥石砌成墙体，屋顶高耸，呈四坡状，覆盖着茅草，使房屋呈现出独特的“蘑菇”形状。村庄中至少一半的房屋主要或部分采用传统材料建造。每户人家耕种一到两块梯田。红​​米的生产依赖于一套复杂而综合的农牧系统，其中涉及水牛、牛、鸭、鱼和鳗鱼。这套系统建立在源远流长的传统社会和宗教结构之上，其基础是动植物之间的共生关系，这种关系强化了社群义务和自然的神圣性，并体现了个人与社群、人与神之间相互依存的二元关系。 红河哈尼梯田是韧性土地管理系统的杰出体现，该系统优化了社会和环境资源，在精神、生态和视觉层面展现了人与环境之间非凡的和谐，并基于对自然的精神尊重以及对个人和社区的尊重，通过被称为“人神合一社会系统”的双重相互依存体系得以实现。
Description.en: On the south banks of the Hong River in the mountainous terrain of southern Yunnan, the Honghe Hani Rice terraces cascade down the towering slopes of the Ailao mountains. Carved out of dense forest over the past 1,300 years by Hani people who migrated here from further to the north-west, the irrigated terraces support paddy fields overlooking narrow valleys. In some places there are as many as 3,000 terraces between the lower edges of the forest and the valley floor.Responding to the difficulties and opportunities of their environment of high mountains, narrow valleys criss-crossed by ravines, extremely high rainfall (around 1400mm) and sub-tropical valley climate, the Hani people have created out of dense forest an extraordinarily complex system of irrigated rice terraces that flows around the contours of the mountains.The property extends across an area of some 1,000 square kilometres. Three areas of terraces, Bada, Duoyishu and Laohuzui, within three river basins, Malizhai, Dawazhe and Amengkong-Geta, reflect differing underlying geological characteristics. The gradient of the terraces in Bada is gentle, in Douyishu steeper, and in Laohuzui very steep.The landscape reflects an integrated four-fold system of forests, water supply, terraces and houses. The mountain top forests are the lifeblood of the terraces in capturing and sustaining the water needed for the irrigation. There are four types of forests, the ancient ‘water recharge’ forest, sacred forest, consolidation forests, and village forests for the provision of timber for building, food and firewood. The sacred forests still have strong connotations. Above the village are places for the Village God “Angma” (the soul of the village) and for the Land Protection God “Misong”, where villagers pray for peace, health and prosperity.Clefts in the rocks channel the rain, and sandstone beneath the granite mountains traps the water and then later releases it as springs. A complex system of channels has been developed to spread this water around the terraces in and between different valleys. Four trunk canals and 392 branch ditches which in length total 445.83km are maintained communally.Eighty-two relatively small villages with between 50 and 100 households are constructed above the terraces just below the mountain top forests. The traditional vernacular buildings have walls built of rammed earth, of adobe bricks or of earth and stone under a tall, hipped, roof thatched with straw that gives the houses a distinctive ‘mushroom’ shape. At least half the houses in the villages are mainly or partly of traditional materials.Each household farms one or two ‘plots’ of the rice terraces. Red rice is produced on the basis of a complex and integrated farming and breeding system involving buffalos, cattle, ducks, fish and eels. This system is under pinned by long-standing traditional social and religious structures, based on symbiotic relationships between plants and animals that reinforce communal obligations and the sacredness of nature and reflect a duality of approach between the individual and the community, and between people and gods, one reinforcing the other. The Honghe Hani rice terraces are an exceptional reflection of a resilient land management system that optimises social and environmental resources, demonstrates an extraordinary harmony between people and their environment in spiritual, ecological and visual terms, and is based on a spiritual respect for nature and respect for both the individual and the community, through a system of dual interdependence known as the ‘Man-God Unity social system’.

Name.cn: 普洱景迈山古茶林文化景观
Name.en: Cultural Landscape of Old Tea Forests of the Jingmai Mountain in Pu’er

History_background.cn: 布朗族傣族自10世纪沿袭发展
History_background.en: The Bulang and Dai ethnic groups have continued their traditions since the 10th century.

Main_function.cn: 展示古茶林文化与生态习俗
Main_function.en: Showcasing the culture and ecological customs of ancient tea forests

Brief_intro.cn: 包括古茶林、茶园、森林和传统村落，体现了布朗族和傣族千年传承的土地利用和茶文化传统。
Brief_intro.en: Comprising ancient tea forests, tea gardens, woodlands, and traditional villages, this landscape embodies the millennium-old land-use practices and tea culture traditions transmitted by the Blang and Dai peoples.

Standard.cn: 红河-普洱景迈山古茶林文化景观是林下茶树栽培传统的杰出见证，这种传统促成了不同土地利用方式互补的空间分布，从而形成了既支持古茶林栽培又保障居住在这一有机演化文化景观中的社区福祉的生态系统和微气候。布朗族和傣族人民遵循着部落-政府-宗教的三元社会治理体系，传承了这些传统一千多年。该体系以茶祖信仰为基础，保护了自然资源，并保存了古茶林。传统实践充分考虑了山地气候、地形特征以及当地动植物，展现了重要的地方传统知识，这些知识有助于保护文化和生物多样性。
Standard.en: The Honghe-Puer Jingmai Mountain Ancient Tea Forest Cultural Landscape is an outstanding testament to the tradition of understory tea cultivation. This tradition fostered a complementary spatial distribution of different land uses, creating an ecosystem and microclimate that both supports ancient tea forest cultivation and safeguards the well-being of the communities residing within this organically evolving cultural landscape. The Bulang and Dai peoples have maintained these traditions for over a thousand years through a tribal-government-religious social governance system. Based on the belief in the Tea Ancestor, this system has protected natural resources and preserved the ancient tea forests. Traditional practices, taking into full account the mountain climate, topography, and local flora and fauna, demonstrate important local traditional knowledge that contributes to the preservation of culture and biodiversity.

Standard.cn: 普洱景迈山古茶林文化景观是基于水平和垂直土地利用模式相结合的可持续土地利用系统的杰出范例。该土地利用系统实现了景迈山山区自然资源的互补利用，是布朗族和傣族人民与易受现代化、城市发展和气候变化负面影响的恶劣环境进行互动的一个特殊范例。传统村落的选址和布局以及民居建筑风格体现了布朗族和傣族人民的文化和传统知识。
Standard.en: The Jingmai Mountain Ancient Tea Forest Cultural Landscape in Pu'er is an outstanding example of a sustainable land use system based on a combination of horizontal and vertical land use patterns. This land use system achieves complementary use of the natural resources of the Jingmai Mountain area and is a unique example of the interaction between the Bulang and Dai peoples and a harsh environment vulnerable to the negative impacts of modernization, urban development, and climate change. The site selection and layout of traditional villages, as well as the architectural style of their dwellings, reflect the culture and traditional knowledge of the Bulang and Dai peoples.

Description.cn: 普洱景迈山古茶林文化景观位于中国西南部的云南省普洱市惠民镇。这一有机演化的文化景观由景迈山上的古茶林、茶园、森林和传统村落组成。这片土地利用系统由布朗族和傣族人民沿袭自10世纪的传统习俗发展而来，历经千年。传统的古茶树林下栽培方式，既适应了山地生态系统和亚热带季风气候的特殊条件，又体现了当地原住民独特的治理体系。与茶祖信仰相关的传统仪式和节庆活动，认为茶园、动植物中居住着特殊的精灵，是这一文化传统的核心。
Description.en: The Cultural Landscape of Old Tea Forests of the Jingmai Mountain in Pu’er is located in Huimin Town, Pu’er City, Yunnan Province, in southwestern China. This organically evolved cultural landscape consists of a tea production area of old tea groves, tea plantations, forests, and traditional villages on Jingmai Mountain. This land-use system has been developed over a thousand years by the Blang and Dai peoples following traditional practices that date back to the 10th century. The traditional understorey cultivation of old tea trees is a method that responds to the specific conditions of the mountain ecosystem and subtropical monsoon climate combined with a particular governance system maintained by the Indigenous communities residing in this area. Traditional ceremonies and festivities related to the Tea Ancestor belief that special spirits live in the tea plantations, local fauna, and flora are at the core of this cultural tradition.

History_background.cn: 公元9至13世纪岩刻艺术遗存
History_background.en: Rock carvings dating from the 9th to 13th centuries

Main_function.cn: 宗教活动与文化交流遗址
Main_function.en: Religious Activities and Cultural Exchange Sites

Brief_intro.cn: 分布于多处山坡，包含1万余幅佛教、道教、儒家题材的石刻，展现宗教融合与社会生活，被誉为中国石窟寺庙艺术的巅峰。
Brief_intro.en: Spread across multiple hillside locations, this site contains over 10,000 stone carvings on Buddhist, Taoist, and Confucian themes, illustrating religious synthesis and everyday social life, and is celebrated as a pinnacle of Chinese rock-cave temple art.

Standard.cn: 大足岩刻代表了中国岩画的巅峰之作，其审美品质高，风格和题材多样。
Standard.en: The Dazu Rock Carvings represent the pinnacle of Chinese rock art, boasting high aesthetic quality and diverse styles and themes.

Standard.cn: 印度密宗佛教与中国道教和儒家信仰在大足相遇，创造了一种高度原创且影响深远的精神和谐表现形式。
Standard.en: Indian Tantric Buddhism met with Chinese Taoism and Confucianism in Dazu, creating a highly original and far-reaching expression of spiritual harmony.

Standard.cn: 中国晚期帝国宗教信仰的多元化特点在大足岩画这一杰出的艺术遗产中得到了物质体现。
Standard.en: The pluralistic nature of religious beliefs in late imperial China is materially reflected in the outstanding artistic heritage of the Dazu Rock Paintings.

Description.cn: 重庆附近大足地区的陡峭山坡上，分布着五处非凡的岩刻群，其年代可追溯至公元9至13世纪。其中规模最大的北山岩刻群，沿7至10米高的峭壁绵延约300米，由两组岩刻组成。这些岩刻创作于9世纪末至12世纪中叶，共计1万余幅，描绘了密宗佛教和道教的主题。碑文为了解历史、宗教信仰、年代以及人物身份提供了重要线索。石柱山岩刻群创作于11世纪末的宋代，绵延130多米，以罕见的三元排列方式展现了佛教、道教和儒家的形象。石门山岩刻群创作于12世纪上半叶的宋代，绵延72米，融合了佛教和道教的主题。南山宋代十二世纪的石刻绵延86米，主要描绘道教题材。保顶山U形峡谷的石刻则堪称密宗佛教表现形式的巅峰之作，峡谷内有两组石刻，年代可追溯至十二世纪末至十三世纪中叶，毗邻长寿寺。其中西侧规模最大的一组石刻绵延约500米，由31组雕刻人物组成，内容涵盖密宗佛教主题以及牧民生活和日常生活场景。大足石刻以其宏大的规模、精美的艺术品质、丰富的题材以及完好的保存状态而闻名。作为9至13世纪中国石窟寺庙艺术的巅峰之作，大足石刻不仅彰显了佛教、道教和儒教三大宗教在中国和谐共存的景象，也为石窟寺庙艺术日益反映日常生活提供了实物证据。遗址内大量的石刻和文字资料展现了这一时期中国石窟寺庙艺术和宗教信仰的巨大变迁与发展。
Description.en: The steep hillsides in the Dazu area near Chongqing, contain an exceptional series of five clusters of rock carvings dating from the 9th to 13th centuries. The largest cluster at Beishan contains two groups along a cliff face 7-10m high stretching for around 300m. There are more than 10,000 carvings dating from the late 9th to the mid-12th century which depict themes of Tantric Buddhism and Taoism. Inscriptions give insight to the history, religious beliefs, dating and the identification of historical figures. The late 11thcentury Song dynasty carvings at Shizhuanshan extend over 130m and depict Buddhist, Taoist and Confucian images in a rare tripartite arrangement. The Song dynasty carvings at Shimenshan dating from the first half of the 12th century extend along 72m and integrate Buddhist and Taoist subjects. At Nanshan the Song dynasty carvings of the 12th century extend over a length of 86m and depict mostly Taoist subjects. The culmination in terms of expression of Tantric Buddhism is found in the U shaped gorge at Baodingshan which contains two groups of carvings dating from the late 12th to the mid-13th century near the Holy Longevity Monastery. The very large group to the west stretches for about 500 metres and comprises 31 groups of carved figures depicting themes from Tantric Buddhism as well scenes of herdsmen and ordinary life.The carvings are known for their grand scale, aesthetic quality and rich diversity of subject matter as well as for being well preserved. Standing as an example of the highest level of Chinese cave temple art dating from the 9th to 13th centuries, the Dazu Rock Carvings not only underline the harmonious coexistence in China of three different religions, namely Buddhism, Taoism and Confucianism, but also provide material proof that cave temple art has increasingly shed light on everyday life. Large numbers of carvings and written historical materials within the heritage site show the great changes in and development of cave temple art and religious beliefs in China during that period.

History_background.cn: 建于13至20世纪，反映兴起与发展
History_background.en: Built between the 13th and 20th centuries, reflecting the rise and development of [the site].

Main_function.cn: 防御与聚落居住
Main_function.en: Defense and settlement

Brief_intro.cn: 是中国东南山区最具代表性的土质防御建筑，规模宏大，技术精湛，体现了聚落模式和建筑艺术的非凡成就。
Brief_intro.en: The most representative earthen defensive structures of southeastern China's mountainous regions, these imposing, technically sophisticated buildings represent an extraordinary achievement in settlement organization and architectural tradition.

Standard.cn: 土楼是长期以来用于集体生活的防御性建筑文化传统的杰出见证，反映了复杂的建筑传统以及和谐与合作的理念，这些理念在时间上得到了充分的记录。
Standard.en: Tulou are outstanding testaments to the long-standing tradition of defensive architecture used for communal living, reflecting complex architectural traditions and the concepts of harmony and cooperation, which have been well documented over time.

Standard.cn: 土楼在规模、建筑传统和功能方面都十分特殊，反映了该地区社会对经济和社会历史各个阶段的回应。
Standard.en: Tulou are unique in terms of scale, architectural tradition and function, reflecting the region's society's response to various stages of economic and social history.

Standard.cn: 土楼整体，特别是提名的福建土楼，从形式上看是集体生活和防御需求的独特体现，从与环境的和谐关系上看是人类居住的杰出范例。
Standard.en: The Tulou as a whole, especially the Fujian Tulou mentioned above, is a unique embodiment of the needs for collective living and defense in terms of form, and an outstanding example of human habitation in terms of its harmonious relationship with the environment.

Description.cn: 福建土楼是中国东南山区土楼中最具代表性、保存最完好的典范。这些规模宏大、技术精湛、气势恢宏的土质防御建筑，建于13至20世纪，坐落于肥沃的山谷之中，环境极为敏感，是历经岁月洗礼而形成的聚落模式的非凡体现。土楼及其丰富的相关文献资料，记录了七个世纪以来土楼这一杰出建筑艺术的兴起、创新与发展。土楼内部结构精巧，部分建筑表面装饰华丽，既满足了居住者的物质需求，也满足了他们的精神需求，以一种非凡的方式展现了在偏远且潜在险恶的环境中，一个高度发达的社会是如何形成的。这些宏伟的建筑与周围景观的和谐共生，既体现了风水原则，也体现了对景观之美与和谐的追求。
Description.en: The Fujian Tulou are the most representative and best preserved examples of the tulou of the mountainous regions of south-eastern China. The large, technically sophisticated and dramatic earthen defensive buildings, built between the 13th and 20th centuries, in their highly sensitive setting in fertile mountain valleys, are an extraordinary reflection of a communal response to settlement which has persisted over time. The tulou, and their extensive associated documentary archives, reflect the emergence, innovation, and development of an outstanding art of earthen building over seven centuries. The elaborate compartmentalised interiors, some with highly decorated surfaces, met both their communities’ physical and spiritual needs and reflect in an extraordinary way the development of a sophisticated society in a remote and potentially hostile environment. The relationship of the massive buildings to their landscape embodies both Feng Shui principles and ideas of landscape beauty and harmony.

History_background.cn: 16世纪中叶沦为葡萄牙殖民地，1999年回归中国
History_background.en: It became a Portuguese colony in the mid-16th century and returned to China in 1999.

Main_function.cn: 见证中西交流与多元文化融合
Main_function.en: Witnessing the exchange between China and the West and the integration of diverse cultures

BUilding_use.cn: 住宅、宗教、教育、公共等用途
BUilding_use.en: Residential, religious, educational, public and other uses

Brief_intro.cn: 包括了22座主要建筑和公共空间，保留着葡萄牙和中国风格的古老街道、住宅、宗教和公共建筑，见证了东西方美学、文化、建筑和技术影响力的交融。
Brief_intro.en: Encompassing 22 major buildings and public spaces, the historic centre preserves streets, residences, religious structures, and public buildings in both Portuguese and Chinese styles, bearing witness to the intermingling of Eastern and Western aesthetics, cultures, architectural traditions, and technological influences.

Standard.cn: 澳门在中国领土上的战略位置，以及中国和葡萄牙当局之间建立的特殊关系，促进了几个世纪以来在文化、科学、技术、艺术和建筑等各个领域的重要人类价值观交流。
Standard.en: Macau’s strategic location on Chinese territory, and the special relationship between the Chinese and Portuguese authorities, have fostered the exchange of important human values in various fields such as culture, science, technology, art and architecture for centuries.

Standard.cn: 澳门是西方与中国首次也是持续时间最长的接触的独特见证。从16世纪到20世纪，澳门一直是贸易商、传教士和不同学术领域的中心。这种接触的影响体现在澳门历史核心区多元文化的融合之中。
Standard.en: Macau is a unique witness to the first and longest-lasting contact between the West and China. From the 16th to the 20th centuries, Macau was a center for traders, missionaries, and various academic fields. The impact of this contact is reflected in the fusion of diverse cultures in Macau's historic heartland.

Standard.cn: 澳门是建筑群的杰出范例，它展现了西方文明与中国文明在四个半世纪以来相互交融的发展历程，并通过历史路线、一系列城市空间和建筑群，将古代中国港口与葡萄牙城市连接起来。
Standard.en: Macau is an outstanding example of architectural ensembles that showcase the intertwining development of Western and Chinese civilizations over four and a half centuries, connecting an ancient Chinese port with a Portuguese city through historical routes, a series of urban spaces and architectural complexes.

Standard.cn: 澳门与西方文明在文化、精神、科学和技术等方面的交流密切相关。这些思想直接推动了中国的关键变革，最终结束了帝国封建​​制度，建立了现代共和国。
Standard.en: Macau's exchanges with Western civilization in culture, spirit, science, and technology were closely intertwined. These ideas directly propelled crucial transformations in China, ultimately ending the imperial feudal system and establishing a modern republic.

Description.cn: 澳门曾是发展中国领土国际贸易的重要战略要地，也是一个利润丰厚的港口。16世纪中叶，澳门沦为葡萄牙殖民地，并于1999年回归中国。列入世界遗产名录的澳门历史城区包含22座主要建筑和公共空间，清晰展现了这座古老贸易港口城市的格局。澳门历史城区拥有历史悠久的街道、住宅、宗教和公共建筑，涵盖葡萄牙和中国风格，是东西方美学、文化、宗教、建筑和科技交融的独特见证。它见证了中西之间基于蓬勃发展的国际贸易而建立的首次也是最持久的交流。作为连接中国与西方世界的门户，澳门在世界贸易中扮演着重要的战略角色。不同国籍的人们在此定居，同时，传教士也带来了宗教和文化影响，例如中国最早的西式剧院、大学、医院、教堂和堡垒等，其中许多至今仍在使用。澳门独特的多元文化身份体现在东西方建筑遗产并存的活力之中，这种活力也体现在建筑设计中，例如，中西建筑风格相互融合，将中国设计元素融入西式建筑，反之亦然。例如，在巴洛克风格的圣保罗大教堂外墙上，就巧妙地运用了汉字作为装饰。典型的欧洲港口城市特征也体现在城市肌理结构中，公共广场与狭窄蜿蜒的街道上密集的住宅区融为一体，同时又汲取了其他葡萄牙殖民地的经验，例如连接港口和旧城的“直街”（Rua Direita）。建筑与海景之间的视觉联系反映了澳门作为贸易港口城市的起源；几个世纪以来一直使用的内港，至今仍在发挥作用，也印证了这一点。历史的交融对当地居民的生活方式产生了深远的影响，体现在宗教、教育、医疗、慈善、语言和饮食等各个方面。历史中心的核心价值不仅在于其建筑、城市结构、居民及其习俗，而是所有这些元素的融合。东西方文化底蕴的共存及其鲜活的传统，共同构成了历史中心的精髓。
Description.en: Macao, a lucrative port of strategic importance in the development of international trade in Chinese territory, became a Portuguese settlement in the mid-16th century and returned to Chinese sovereignty in 1999. The inscribed property presents a group of 22 principal buildings and public spaces that enable a clear understanding of the structure of the old trading port city. With its historic streets, residential, religious and public Portuguese and Chinese buildings, the Historic Centre of Macao provides a unique testimony to the meeting of aesthetic, cultural, religious, architectural and technological influences from East and West. It bears witness to the first and most enduring encounter between China and the West, based on the vibrancy of international trade. As a gateway between China and the western world, Macao played a strategic role in world trade. Different nationalities settled in this hub of a complex maritime trading network, along with missionaries who brought with them religious and cultural influences, as illustrated by the introduction of foreign building types (China’s first western-style theatre, university, hospital, churches and fortresses), many still in use. Macao’s unique multicultural identity can be read in the dynamic presence of Western and Chinese architectural heritage standing side by side in the city and the same dynamics often exist in individual building designs, adapting Chinese design features in western style buildings and vice versa, such as the incorporation of Chinese characters as decorative ornaments on the baroque-mannerist church façade of St. Paul’s Ruins. Typical European port city characteristics can also be seen in the urban fabric structure of the settlement with public squares blending into the densely packed lots along narrow, meandering streets, whilst accumulating experiences from other Portuguese settlements, seen in the concept of “Rua Direita” that links the port with old citadel. Visual connections between the property and seascape are attributes that reflect Macao’s origin as a trading port city; the Inner Harbour used over centuries and still functioning today adds to that testimony. Intangible influences of the historic encounter have permeated the lifestyles of the local people, affecting religion, education, medicine, charities, language and cuisine. The core value of the historic centre is not solely its architecture, the urban structure, the people or their customs, but a mixture of all these.  The coexistence of cultural sediments of eastern and western origin, along with their living traditions, defines the essence of the historic centre.

Name.cn: 拉萨布达拉宫历史建筑群
Name.en: Historic Ensemble of the Potala Palace, Lhasa

History_background.cn: 始建于公元7世纪，象征藏传佛教地位
History_background.en: Built in the 7th century AD, it symbolizes the status of Tibetan Buddhism.

Main_function.cn: 宗教活动和行政管理中心
Main_function.en: Religious Activities and Administrative Management Center

BUilding_use.cn: 达赖喇嘛冬夏宫、寺院及历史文物收藏
BUilding_use.en: The Dalai Lama's Summer and Winter Palaces, Monasteries, and Historical Artifacts Collection

Brief_intro.cn: 包含了三大建筑群，是藏传佛教和西藏传统行政的核心，建筑融合多种风格，拥有丰富的文物和艺术价值。
Brief_intro.en: Comprising three major architectural complexes, this ensemble is the heart of Tibetan Buddhism and traditional Tibetan administration. Its buildings integrate multiple architectural styles and contain a rich collection of cultural relics and artistic treasures.

Standard.cn: 布达拉宫历史建筑群是人类想象力和创造力的杰出作品，其设计、装饰以及与壮丽景观的和谐融合都堪称典范。布达拉宫历史建筑群由布达拉宫（宫殿堡垒建筑群）、罗布林卡（花园住宅）和大昭寺（寺庙建筑）三部分组成，各具特色，是藏式传统建筑的杰出代表。
Standard.en: The Potala Palace complex is a masterpiece of human imagination and creativity, with its design, decoration, and harmonious integration with the magnificent landscape serving as a model. The Potala Palace complex comprises three parts: the Potala Palace (a palace and fortress complex), Norbulingka (a garden residence), and Jokhang Temple (a temple), each with its own unique characteristics, representing outstanding examples of traditional Tibetan architecture.

Standard.cn: 布达拉宫历史建筑群的规模和艺术价值，代表了藏族建筑的巅峰，使其成为神权建筑的杰出范例，也是现代世界现存的最后一个此类建筑。
Standard.en: The scale and artistic value of the Potala Palace historical building complex represent the pinnacle of Tibetan architecture, making it an outstanding example of theocratic architecture and the last such building still existing in the modern world.

Standard.cn: 布达拉宫历史建筑群是世俗权威与宗教权威融合的有力而独特的象征。
Standard.en: The Potala Palace complex is a powerful and unique symbol of the fusion of secular and religious authority.

Description.cn: 布达拉宫的白宫、红宫及其附属建筑群，被夯土和石头砌成的厚重城墙、城门和塔楼环绕，耸立于拉萨山谷中心海拔3700米的红山之上。自公元7世纪以来，布达拉宫一直是达赖喇嘛的冬宫，象征着藏传佛教及其在西藏传统行政管理中的核心地位。白宫内设有主殿，供奉着达赖喇嘛的宝座，他的私人寝宫和接见厅则位于顶层。宫殿内藏有698幅壁画、近万幅彩绘卷轴、众多雕塑、地毯、华盖、帷幔、瓷器、玉器以及精美的金银器皿，此外还收藏了大量的经文和重要的历史文献。在西侧更高处的红宫内，安放着历代达赖喇嘛的镀金陵墓。再往西走就是达赖喇嘛的私人寺院——南杰扎仓。大昭寺由拉萨政权于7世纪兴建，旨在弘扬佛教。寺院位于拉萨古城中心，占地2.5公顷，包括入口门廊、庭院和佛殿，四周环绕着僧舍和仓库。建筑以木石为主，是藏传佛教建筑风格的杰出代表，并融合了中国、印度和尼泊尔的建筑风格。寺内供奉着3000多尊佛像、神像和历史人物像，以及众多珍宝和手稿。墙壁上绘满了描绘宗教和历史场景的壁画。罗布林卡是达赖喇嘛的夏宫，建于18世纪，坐落在拉萨河畔，位于布达拉宫以西约2公里处，绿树环绕，环境优美。它由一个大型花园、四座宫殿建筑群、一座寺院以及其他殿堂和亭台楼阁组成，所有建筑都巧妙地融入花园布局，构成了一幅占地36公顷的艺术杰作。罗布林卡与宗教和政治密切相关，曾是人们冥想和签署政治协议的场所。布达拉宫、大昭寺和罗布林卡这三处历史建筑群，通过其选址、布局和建筑风格，体现了西藏神权政府的行政、宗教和象征功能。这三处建筑的精美绝伦和独创性，其丰富的装饰以及与周围壮丽景观的和谐融合，共同造就了它们杰出的普世价值。
Description.en: Enclosed within massive walls, gates and turrets built of rammed earth and stone the White and Red Palaces and ancillary buildings of the Potala Palace rise from Red Mountain in the centre of Lhasa Valley at an altitude of 3,700 metres. As the winter palace of the Dalai Lama from the 7th century CE the complex symbolizes Tibetan Buddhism and its central role in the traditional administration of Tibet. The White Palace contains the main ceremonial hall with the throne of the Dalai Lama, and his private rooms and audience hall are on the uppermost level. The palace contains 698 murals, almost 10,000 painted scrolls, numerous sculptures, carpets, canopies, curtains, porcelain, jade, and fine objects of gold and silver, as well as a large collection of sutras and important historical documents. To the west and higher up the mountain the Red Palace contains the gilded burial stupas of past Dalai Lamas. Further west is the private monastery of the Dalai Lama, the Namgyel Dratshang.The Jokhang Temple Monastery was founded by the regime also in the 7th century, in order to promote the Buddhist religion. Covering 2.5ha in the centre of the old town of Lhasa, it comprises an entrance porch, courtyard and Buddhist hall surrounded by accommodation for monks and storehouses on all four sides. The buildings are constructed of wood and stone and are outstanding examples of the Tibetan Buddhist style, with influences from China, India, and Nepal. They house over 3,000 images of Buddha and other deities and historical figures along with many other treasures and manuscripts. Mural paintings depicting religious and historical scenes cover the walls.Norbulingka, the Dalai Lama's former summer palace constructed in the 18th century, is located on the bank of the Lhasa River about 2km west of the Potala Palace in a lush green environment.  It comprises a large garden with four palace complexes and a monastery as well as other halls, and pavilions all integrated into the garden layout to create an exceptional work of art covering 36ha. The property is closely linked with religious and political issues, having been a place for contemplation and for signing political agreements.The Historic Ensemble of the Potala Palace, Jokhang Temple and Norbulingka embody the administrative, religious and symbolic functions of the Tibetan theocratic government through their location, layout and architecture. The beauty and originality of the architecture of these three sites, their rich ornamentation and harmonious integration in a striking landscape, contribute to their Outstanding Universal Value.

Name.cn: 登封 “天地之中”历史古迹
Name.en: Historic Monuments of Dengfeng in “The Centre of Heaven and Earth”

Dynast.cn: 汉朝(公元前202年 - 公元220年)

History_background.cn: 中国早期都城之一，位置不详
History_background.en: One of the early capitals of China, location unknown.

Main_function.cn: 举行神圣仪式与天文观测
Main_function.en: Performing sacred ceremonies and astronomical observations

BUilding_use.cn: 皇帝下令建造以巩固权力
BUilding_use.en: The emperor ordered its construction to consolidate his power.

Brief_intro.cn: 历来被视为天地中心，是皇帝举行仪式和天文观测的重要场所，周边建筑群多为皇帝所建，巩固了其影响力。
Brief_intro.en: Long regarded as the center of heaven and earth, Dengfeng was an important site for imperial rituals and astronomical observations. The surrounding building complexes, many constructed by emperors, reinforced its singular cultural and religious significance.

Standard.cn: 天地中心的天文观念与皇权观念紧密相连，与在天地中心建立都城的吉利理念，以及嵩山这一自然地标及其相关的礼仪活动息息相关。该系列遗产体现了该地区在威望和赞助方面的重要性。
Standard.en: The astronomical concept of the center of heaven and earth is closely linked to the concept of imperial power, the auspicious idea of establishing a capital city at the center of heaven and earth, and the natural landmark of Mount Song and its associated ceremonial activities. This series of heritage sites reflects the importance of the region in terms of prestige and patronage.

Standard.cn: 登封地区宗教和世俗建筑的集中分布，反映了与圣山相连的天地中心这一强大而持久的传统。这座圣山在1500多年间承受着皇室的祭祀和庇护，在中国文化中具有举足轻重的地位。佛教建筑与圣山之间形成了共生关系。
Standard.en: The concentrated distribution of religious and secular buildings in Dengfeng reflects the powerful and enduring tradition of being connected to the sacred mountain as the center of heaven and earth. This sacred mountain, which received imperial sacrifices and protection for over 1500 years, holds a pivotal position in Chinese culture. A symbiotic relationship has formed between Buddhist architecture and the sacred mountain.

Description.cn: 登封，这座中国早期都城之一，其确切位置已不可考，但如今其名称通常指嵩山两峰少石山和太石山以南的地区。几个世纪以来，登封逐渐与天地中心的概念联系起来——在当时，只有这里天文观测才被认为是准确的。嵩山被视为天地中心的自然象征，皇帝们通过崇拜嵩山来巩固自己的权力。因此，这三种观念在某种程度上是相通的：天文意义上的天地中心被视为建立世俗权力中心的吉地，而嵩山作为天地中心的自然象征，则被用作举行神圣仪式以巩固世俗权力的场所。登封周围的建筑群在建造之初都达到了极高的建筑水准，其中许多都是由皇帝下令建造的。这些建筑因此巩固了登封地区的影响力。提名区域内的一些遗址与这座山密切相关（中岳寺、太史雀和少史雀）；天文台显然与在天地中心进行的天文观测有关，而其余的建筑则建在被认为是天地中心的区域——这赋予了它们相应的地位。
Description.en: For many centuries Dengfeng, one of the early capitals of China whose precise location is unknown, but whose name is now associated with an area to the south of Mount Shaoshi and Mount Taishi, two peaks of Mount Songshan, came to be associated with the concept of the centre of heaven and earth – the only point where astronomical observations were considered to be accurate. The natural attribute of the centre of heaven and earth was seen to be Mount Songshan and worship of Mount Songshan was used by the Emperors as a way of reinforcing their power.The three ideas do therefore converge to some extent: the centre of heaven and earth in astronomical terms is used as a propitious place for a capital of terrestrial power, and Mount Songshan as the natural symbol of the centre of heaven and earth is used as the focus for sacred rituals that reinforce that earthly power. The buildings that clustered around Dengfeng were of the highest architectural standards when built and many were commissioned by Emperors. They thus reinforced the influence of the Dengfeng area.Some of the sites in the nominated area relate closely to the mountain (Zhongyue Temple, Taishi Que and Shaoshi Que); the Observatory is very clearly associated with the astronomical observations made at the centre of heaven and earth, while the remainder of the buildings were built in the area perceived to be the centre of heaven and earth – for the status that this conferred.

Name.cn: 明清故宫（北京故宫、沈阳故宫）
Name.en: Imperial Palaces of the Ming and Qing Dynasties in Beijing and Shenyang

History_background.cn: 明清两代皇帝的皇家住所
History_background.en: Royal residences of emperors of the Ming and Qing dynasties

Main_function.cn: 国家权力中心、皇室居所
Main_function.en: Center of national power, residence of the royal family

BUilding_use.cn: 皇宫、皇家临时住所、祭祀场所
BUilding_use.en: Royal palace, temporary royal residence, and place of worship

Brief_intro.cn: 是明清皇帝的居住和政务中心，见证了中晚期中国封建国家权力与宫廷文化的发展，对建筑艺术和宫廷生活有深远影响。
Brief_intro.en: The residential and administrative centers of the Ming and Qing emperors, these palaces bear witness to the development of imperial power and court culture in middle and late feudal China, and have had a profound influence on architectural art and courtly life.

Standard.cn: 皇家宫殿代表了中国皇家宫殿建筑发展史上的杰作。
Standard.en: The Imperial Palace represents a masterpiece in the history of Chinese imperial palace architecture.

Standard.cn: 皇家宫殿建筑群，特别是沈阳的宫殿建筑群，在17世纪和18世纪表现出传统建筑和中国宫殿建筑的重要交流影响。
Standard.en: The royal palace complexes, especially those in Shenyang, demonstrate significant exchange and influence between traditional architecture and Chinese palace architecture in the 17th and 18th centuries.

Standard.cn: 皇宫是明清时期中国文明的杰出见证，是真正的风景、建筑、家具和艺术品的宝库，也是满族人民几个世纪以来所奉行的萨满教生活传统和习俗的杰出证据。
Standard.en: The Imperial Palace is an outstanding testament to Chinese civilization during the Ming and Qing dynasties, a true treasure trove of landscapes, architecture, furniture, and works of art, and outstanding evidence of the shamanistic traditions and customs practiced by the Manchu people for centuries.

Standard.cn: 皇家宫殿是中国最伟大的宫殿建筑群的杰出范例。它们展现了从清朝到更早的明元时期皇室制度的宏伟，以及满族传统，并提供了17世纪和18世纪此类建筑演变的证据。
Standard.en: Imperial palaces are outstanding examples of China's greatest palace complexes. They showcase the grandeur of the imperial system from the Qing Dynasty to the earlier Ming and Yuan Dynasties, as well as Manchu traditions, and provide evidence of the evolution of such architecture in the 17th and 18th centuries.

Description.cn: 从15世纪到20世纪，明清两代皇帝的皇家住所——北京和沈阳的明清宫殿——是封建晚期中国国家权力的中心。北京的明清宫殿，即紫禁城，由明朝皇帝朱棣于1406年至1420年间建造，在随后的505年间，见证了14位明朝皇帝和10位清朝皇帝的登基。沈阳的清代皇宫建于1625年至1637年间，由努尔加赤为清朝女真/满族先祖建造。清朝于1644年在北京建立都城。该宫殿又称后进宫或圣林宫，此后一直作为第二都城和皇室临时住所，直至1911年。北京皇宫和沈阳皇宫分别于1987年和2004年被列入世界遗产名录。位于北京中心的故宫是古代中国宫殿发展的典范，为了解晚朝时期中国的社会发展，特别是礼仪和宫廷文化，提供了宝贵的资料。故宫的布局和空间安排继承并体现了古代中国城市规划和宫殿建造的传统特征，以中轴线为中心，前后对称，外院在前，内院在后，并借鉴元代城市布局，增设了园林庭院。作为古代建筑等级、建造技术和建筑艺术的典范，故宫对后世清代官邸建筑产生了长达300余年的影响。故宫内的宗教建筑，特别是宫殿内的一系列皇家佛殿，吸收了丰富的民族文化特征，见证了自14世纪以来满汉蒙古藏族建筑的融合与交流。与此同时，超过一百万件珍贵的皇家藏品、皇室成员使用的物品以及大量关于古代工程技术的档案资料，包括文字记录、图纸和模型，都是明清两代宫廷文化和法律法规的佐证。沈阳清宫在遵循中国宫殿建造传统的同时，保留了满族传统民居的典型特征，并融合了汉、满、蒙古三族建筑艺术。宫殿建筑按照满族特有的“八旗”制度布局，这种布局在宫殿建筑中独树一帜。清宫内的祭祀场所也体现了满族数百年来信奉萨满教的习俗。
Description.en: As the royal residences of the emperors of the Ming and Qing dynasties from the 15th to 20th century, the Imperial Palaces of the Ming and Qing dynasties in Beijing and Shenyang were the centre of State power in late feudal China. The Imperial Palace of the Ming and Qing Dynasties in Beijing known as the Forbidden City was constructed between 1406 and 1420 by the Ming emperor Zhu Di and witnessed the enthronement of 14 Ming and 10 Qing emperors over the following 505 years. The Imperial Palace of the Qing Dynasty in Shenyang was built between 1625 and 1637 by Nurgaci for the Nuzhen/Manchu forebears of the Qing Dynasty, which established itself in Beijing in 1644. Also known as Houjin Palace or Shenglin Palace, it was then used as the secondary capital and temporary residence for the royal family until 1911. The Imperial Palaces of Beijing and Shenyang were inscribed on the World Heritage List in 1987 and 2004 respectively.The Forbidden City, located in the centre of Beijing is the supreme model in the development of ancient Chinese palaces, providing insight into the social development of late dynastic China, especially the ritual and court culture. The layout and spatial arrangement inherits and embodies the traditional characteristic of urban planning and palace construction in ancient China, featuring a central axis, symmetrical design and layout of outer court at the front and inner court at the rear and the inclusion of additional landscaped courtyards deriving from the Yuan city layout. As the exemplar of ancient architectural hierarchy, construction techniques and architectural art, it influenced official buildings of the subsequent Qing dynasty over a span of 300 years. The religious buildings, particularly a series of royal Buddhist chambers within the Palace, absorbing abundant features of ethnic cultures, are a testimony of the integration and exchange in architecture among the Manchu, Han, Mongolian and Tibetan since the 14th century. Meanwhile, more than a million precious royal collections, articles used by the royal family and a large number of archival materials on ancient engineering techniques, including written records, drawings and models, are evidence of the court culture and law and regulations of the Ming and Qing dynasties.The Imperial Palace of the Qing Dynasty in Shenyang while following the traditions of palace construction in China retains typical features of traditional folk residences of the Manchu people, and has integrated the architectural arts of Han, Manchu and Mongolian ethnic cultures. The buildings were laid out according to the “eight-banner” system, a distinct social organization system in Manchu society, an arrangement which is unique among palace buildings. Within the Qingning Palace the sacrificial places for the emperors testify to the customs of Shamanism practiced by the Manchu people for several hundred years.

Name.en: Imperial Tombs of the Ming and Qing Dynasties

History_background.cn: 明清两代帝陵建于1368-1915年
History_background.en: The imperial tombs of the Ming and Qing dynasties were built between 1368 and 1915.

Main_function.cn: 皇家陵墓及举行皇家仪式
Main_function.en: Royal tombs and royal ceremonies

Brief_intro.cn: 陵墓为清朝开国皇帝及其祖先建造，遵循传统中国占卜和风水理论的原则。雕像和雕刻华丽，瓷砖上有龙纹图案，展现清朝丧葬建筑的发展历程。
Brief_intro.en: Built for the founding emperors of the Qing dynasty and their ancestors in accordance with traditional Chinese divination and feng shui principles, these tombs feature elaborate statues, carvings, and dragon-patterned tiles, tracing the evolution of Qing imperial funerary architecture.

Standard.cn: 明清皇家陵墓在符合风水原则的自然环境中和谐地融合了杰出的建筑群，使其成为人类创造性天才的杰作。
Standard.en: The imperial tombs of the Ming and Qing dynasties harmoniously integrate outstanding architectural complexes within a natural environment that conforms to feng shui principles, making them masterpieces of human creative genius.

Standard.cn: 这些陵墓代表了一个发展阶段，其中先前的传统融入了明清时期的形式，也成为后来发展的基础。
Standard.en: These tombs represent a stage of development in which earlier traditions were incorporated into the forms of the Ming and Qing dynasties, and became the basis for later developments.

Standard.cn: 这些皇家陵墓是五百多年来主宰世界这一地区的文化和建筑传统的杰出见证。
Standard.en: These royal tombs are outstanding testament to the cultural and architectural traditions that have dominated this region of the world for over five centuries.

Standard.cn: 皇家陵墓的建筑与自然环境完美融合，构成独特的文化景观组合，是中国古代皇家陵墓的杰出范例。
Standard.en: The architecture of the royal tombs blends perfectly with the natural environment, forming a unique combination of cultural landscapes and serving as an outstanding example of ancient Chinese royal tombs.

Standard.cn: 明清陵墓是封建时期中国盛行的风水信仰、世界观和风水理论的生动体现。它们既是显赫人物的陵墓，也是中国历史上重大事件的发生地。
Standard.en: The Ming and Qing imperial tombs vividly embody the prevailing Feng Shui beliefs, worldviews, and theories in feudal China. They are not only the tombs of prominent figures but also the sites of significant events in Chinese history.

Description.cn: 明清两代帝陵建于公元1368年至1915年间，分布于中国北京市、河北省、湖北省、江苏省和辽宁省。其中包括2000年列入世界遗产名录的明代咸陵和清代东陵、西陵；2003年列入世界遗产名录的明代孝陵和北京明代三陵；以及2004年列入世界遗产名录的辽宁沈阳三陵（清代永陵、涪陵和昭陵）。明清两代皇陵选址于精心挑选的地形地貌，遵循风水原则，陵墓建筑群众多，均采用传统建筑风格和装饰。陵墓及建筑群的布局遵循中国等级制度，并设有神圣的道路，道路两旁林立着石碑和雕塑，既用于举行皇家仪式，也用于引导亡灵的通行。这些陵墓体现了明清两代统治者在长达五个世纪的时间里对建造宏伟陵墓的重视，不仅反映了当时人们对来世的普遍信仰，也彰显了统治者的权威。明朝开国皇帝孝陵打破了以往的陵墓设计，为北京后来的陵墓奠定了基本基调。此外，位于钟乡的明代仙陵、清西陵和清东陵也具有类似的意义。位于辽宁省的清代三大陵墓（永陵、涪陵和昭陵）均建于17世纪，为清朝开国皇帝及其先祖而建，融合了前朝的传统和满族文明的新特色。明清两代的皇家陵墓因其与自然环境的有机融合而成为人类创造性天才的杰作，也是14至20世纪中国历史上最后两个封建王朝（明清）文化和建筑传统的独特见证。它们是汉清两代建筑艺术的融合之作。陵墓的选址、规划和设计既体现了风水“人与自然和谐”的哲学理念和社会等级制度的规则，也展现了中国古代社会后期盛行的世界观和权力观念。
Description.en: The Imperial Tombs of the Ming and Qing Dynasties were built between 1368 and 1915 AD in Beijing Municipality, Hebei Province, Hubei Province, Jiangsu Province and Liaoning Province of China. They comprise of the Xianling Tombs of the Ming Dynasty and the Eastern and Western Qing Tombs inscribed on the World Heritage List in 2000; the Xiaoling Tomb of the Ming Dynasty and the Ming Tombs in Beijing added to the inscription in 2003, and the Three Imperial Tombs of Shenyang, Liaoning Province (Yongling Tomb, Fuling Tomb, and Zhaoling Tomb, all of the Qing Dynasty) added in 2004.The Ming and Qing imperial tombs are located in topographical settings carefully chosen according to principles of geomancy (Fengshui) and comprise numerous buildings of traditional architectural design and decoration. The tombs and buildings are laid out according to Chinese hierarchical rules and incorporate sacred ways lined with stone monuments and sculptures designed to accommodate ongoing royal ceremonies as well as the passage of the spirits of the dead. They illustrate the great importance attached by the Ming and Qing rulers over five centuries to the building of imposing mausolea, reflecting not only the general belief in an afterlife but also an affirmation of authority.The tomb of the first Ming Emperor, the Xiaoling Tomb broke with the past and established the basic design for those that followed in Beijing, and also the Xianling Tomb of the Ming Dynasty in Zhongxiang, the Western Qing Tombs and the Eastern Qing Tombs. The Three Imperial Tombs of the Qing Dynasty in Liaoning Province (Yongling Tomb, Fuling Tomb, and Zhaoling Tomb) were all built in the 17th century for the founding emperors of the Qing Dynasty and their ancestors, integrating the tradition inherited from previous dynasties with new features from the Manchu civilization.The Imperial Tombs of the Ming and Qing Dynasties are masterpieces of human creative genius by reason of their organic integration into nature, and a unique testimony to the cultural and architectural traditions of the last two feudal dynasties (Ming and Qing) in the history of China between the 14th and 20th centuries. They are fine works combining the architectural arts of the Han and Manchu civilizations. Their siting, planning and design reflect both the philosophical idea of “harmony between man and nature” according to Fengshui principles and the rules of social hierarchy, and illustrate the conception of the world and power prevalent in the later period of the ancient society of China.

History_background.cn: 融合中西建筑风格的发展
History_background.en: The development of integrating Chinese and Western architectural styles

Main_function.cn: 防御性住宅
Main_function.en: defensive housing

Brief_intro.cn: 现了中西建筑和装饰形式复杂而灿烂的融合，表现了19世纪末及20世纪初开平侨民在几个南亚国家、澳洲以及北美国家发展进程中的重要作用，以及海外开平人与其故里的密切联系。
Brief_intro.en: Displaying a complex and splendid fusion of Chinese and Western architectural and decorative forms, these structures reflect the important role played by the Kaiping diaspora in the development of several South and Southeast Asian countries, Australia, and North America in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, as well as the close ties between overseas Kaiping people and their homeland.

Standard.cn: 碉楼以引人注目的物质形式代表了人类价值观的重要交流——从北美归来的中国人将建筑风格与当地农村传统融合在一起——在世界特定文化区域内。
Standard.en: The watchtowers, in their striking physical form, represent an important exchange of human values—Chinese returning from North America blending architectural styles with local rural traditions—within specific cultural regions of the world.

Standard.cn: 自明代以来，修建防御楼是开平地区应对当地土匪猖獗的传统。入选的碉楼代表了这一传统的最终发展阶段，当时返乡汉人的巨额财富助长了土匪的蔓延，而碉楼的修建则是应对土匪的极端方式。
Standard.en: Since the Ming Dynasty, building defensive towers has been a tradition in the Kaiping area to deal with rampant local bandits. The selected towers represent the final stage of this tradition, when the enormous wealth of returning Han Chinese fueled the spread of bandits, and the construction of towers was an extreme way to deal with them.

Standard.cn: 主塔及其周围环境，以及其炫耀财富的方式，体现了开平移民在 19 世纪末 20 世纪初南亚、澳大拉西亚和北美几个国家的发展中所发挥的重要作用，以及开平社群与这些地区华人社群之间持续的联系。
Standard.en: The main tower and its surroundings, along with the way it flaunts its wealth, reflect the important role played by Kaiping immigrants in the development of several countries in South Asia, Australasia, and North America in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, as well as the ongoing connections between the Kaiping community and Chinese communities in these regions.

Description.cn: 碉楼及其周边村落因其复杂而自信地融合了中西建筑风格，因其最终繁荣发展了当地塔楼建造传统，因其作为防御性住宅的短暂寿命和相对废弃而得以完整保存，以及因其与农业景观的和谐关系，而展现出杰出的普世价值。
Description.en: The Diaolou and their surrounding villages demonstrate Outstanding Universal Value for their complex and confident fusion between Chinese and western architectural styles, for their final flowering of local tower building traditions, for their completeness and unaltered state resulting from their short life span as fortified dwellings and their comparative abandonment and for harmonious relationship with their agricultural landscape.

History_background.cn: 1843年厦门开港，1903年成为国际租界
History_background.en: Xiamen opened as a port in 1843 and became an international concession in 1903.

Main_function.cn: 中外交流与多元文化聚居
Main_function.en: Sino-foreign exchanges and multicultural coexistence

Brief_intro.cn: 随着厦门开港通商成为中外交流的重要窗口，建筑风格多样，包括传统闽南风格、西式古典复兴风格和走廊殖民风格。
Brief_intro.en: As Xiamen opened to trade and foreign commerce, Kulangsu became an important window for Sino-foreign exchange, featuring a diverse range of architectural styles including traditional Southern Fujian, Western classical revival, and veranda colonial forms.

Standard.cn: 鼓浪屿的建筑特色和风格体现了中国、东南亚和欧洲建筑及文化价值观和传统的交融，这种多元性是由定居于此的外国居民或归国华侨所创造的。岛上的聚落不仅反映了定居者从原籍地或先前居住地带来的各种影响，而且融合了一种新的混合风格——所谓的厦门装饰艺术风格。这种风格在鼓浪屿发展起来，并对东南亚沿海地区乃至更广阔的区域产生了影响。由此可见，鼓浪屿的聚落展现了早期亚洲全球化阶段不同价值观的相遇、互动与融合。
Standard.en: The architectural features and styles of Gulangyu Island embody the fusion of Chinese, Southeast Asian, and European architectural and cultural values and traditions. This diversity was created by foreign residents or returned overseas Chinese who settled there. The island's settlements not only reflect the various influences brought by the settlers from their ancestral homes or previous residences, but also integrate a new hybrid style—the so-called Xiamen Art Deco style. This style developed on Gulangyu and influenced the coastal areas of Southeast Asia and even wider regions. Thus, the settlements of Gulangyu demonstrate the encounter, interaction, and integration of different values during the early stages of Asian globalization.

Standard.cn: 鼓浪屿是厦门装饰艺术风格的发源地和最佳代表。厦门装饰艺术风格以厦门本地的闽南语名称“厦门”命名，指的是一种建筑风格和类型，它最初出现在鼓浪屿，融合了当地建筑传统、早期西方（尤其是现代主义）的影响以及福建南部移民文化。基于这些，厦门装饰艺术风格展现了传统建筑类型向新形式的转变，这种转变后来被东南亚各地效仿，并在更广泛的地区流行起来。
Standard.en: Gulangyu Island is the birthplace and best representative of the Xiamen Art Deco style. Named after the local Minnan (Hokkien) name for Xiamen, Art Deco refers to an architectural style and type that originated on Gulangyu Island, blending local architectural traditions, early Western (especially modernist) influences, and the immigrant culture of southern Fujian. Based on these elements, Art Deco showcased the transformation of traditional architectural types into new forms, a transformation that was later imitated throughout Southeast Asia and became popular in a wider area.
