Description.cn: 鼓浪屿位于九龙江入海口，隔着600米宽的庐江海峡与厦门相望。1843年厦门开港，1903年鼓浪屿成为国际租界，这座位于中国南部沿海的岛屿，从此成为中外交流的重要窗口。岛上的历史遗迹丰富多彩，展现了现代聚落的多元融合，拥有931座融合了本土和国际建筑风格的历史建筑、优美的自然风光、纵横交错的历史道路和园林。在当地华人、归国华侨和来自世界各地的外国居民的共同努力下，鼓浪屿发展成为一个文化多元、生活品质现代化的国际化聚居区。它也成为活跃于东亚和东南亚的华侨和精英人士的理想居住地，以及19世纪中期至20世纪中期现代居住理念的体现。鼓浪屿是文化融合的杰出典范，这种融合源于各种文化交流，并体现在其数十年来不断吸收多元文化元素、有机形成的都市肌理之中。而最能体现不同风格融合的，莫过于岛上兴起的全新建筑流派——厦门装饰艺术风格。
Description.en: Kulangsu Island is located on the estuary of Chiu-lung River facing the city of Xiamen across the 600-meter-wide Lujiang Strait. With the opening of Xiamen as a commercial port in 1843, and Kulangsu as an international settlement in 1903, the island of the southern coastal areas of the Chinese empire suddenly became an important window for Sino-foreign exchanges. Its heritage reflects the composite nature of a modern settlement composed of 931 historical buildings of a variety of local and international architectural styles, natural sceneries, a historic network of roads and historic gardens.Through the concerted endeavour of local Chinese, returned overseas Chinese, and foreign residents from many countries, Kulangsu developed into an international settlement with outstanding cultural diversity and modern living quality. It also became an ideal dwelling place for the overseas Chinese and elites who were active in East Asia and South-eastern Asia as well as an embodiment of modern habitat concepts of the period between mid-19th and mid-20th century.Kulangsu is an exceptional example of the cultural fusion, which emerged from these exchanges, which remain legible in an organic urban fabric formed over decades constantly integrating more diverse cultural references. Most exceptional testimony of the fusion of various stylistic influences is a genuinely new architectural movement the Amoy Deco Style, which emerged from the island.

History_background.cn: 北魏至唐代开凿，艺术风格演变
History_background.en: Carved from the Northern Wei to the Tang Dynasty, the artistic style evolved

Main_function.cn: 佛教石窟寺庙及艺术展示
Main_function.en: Buddhist grottoes, temples and art exhibitions

BUilding_use.cn: 供奉佛像、佛教艺术雕刻
BUilding_use.en: Buddhist statues and Buddhist art sculptures

Brief_intro.cn: 由2300多个洞窟，藏有近11万尊佛像组成，是中国重要的佛教石窟艺术遗址。
Brief_intro.en: Comprising over 2,300 caves housing nearly 110,000 Buddhist statues, the Longmen Grottoes represent one of China's most important sites of Buddhist rock-carved art.

Standard.cn: 龙门石窟的雕塑是人类艺术创造力的杰出体现。
Standard.en: The sculptures in the Longmen Grottoes are an outstanding manifestation of human artistic creativity.

Standard.cn: 龙门石窟展现了一种历史悠久的艺术形式的完美，这种艺术形式在亚洲这一地区的文化发展中发挥了极其重要的作用。
Standard.en: The Longmen Grottoes showcase the perfection of a time-honored art form that has played an extremely important role in the cultural development of this region of Asia.

Standard.cn: 唐代中国高度发达的文化水平和社会文明程度体现在龙门石窟杰出的石刻作品中。
Standard.en: The highly developed culture and social civilization of Tang Dynasty China are reflected in the outstanding stone carvings of the Longmen Grottoes.

Description.cn: 龙门石窟位于河南省洛阳古都以南，横跨伊河两岸，绵延1公里，由2300多个洞窟和壁龛组成，开凿于陡峭的石灰岩峭壁之上。石窟内藏有近11万尊佛像、60多座佛塔以及2800多块碑刻。洛阳曾是北魏末唐初期的都城，龙门石窟开凿最为密集的时期是从公元5世纪末到8世纪中叶。西山峭壁上最早开凿的洞窟包括古阳洞和宾阳三洞，均开凿于公元5世纪末至6世纪初，洞内均有大型佛像。药房洞内有140块碑刻，记载着各种疾病的治疗方法。该洞窟的雕刻工程持续了150余年，展现了艺术风格的演变。唐代（7至8世纪）佛教石窟中发现的雕塑风格，特别是奉贤寺石窟的巨型雕塑，是皇家石窟寺庙艺术最具代表性的范例，被各地艺术家竞相模仿。早期的“中原风格”和后期的“大唐风格”两种雕塑艺术风格，在国内乃至世界范围内都产生了深远的影响，并对其他亚洲国家的雕塑艺术发展做出了重要贡献
Description.en: The Longmen Grottoes, located on bothsides of the Yi River to the south of the ancient capital of Luoyang, Henan province, comprise more than 2,300 caves and niches carved into the steep limestone cliffs over a 1km long stretch. These contain almost 110,000 Buddhist stone statues, more than 60 stupas and 2,800 inscriptions carved on steles. Luoyang was the capital during the late Northern Wei Dynasty and early Tang Dynasty, and the most intensive period of carving dates from the end of the 5th century to the mid-8th century. The earliest caves to be carved in the late 5th and early 6th centuries in the West Hill cliffs include Guyangdong and the Three Binyang Caves, all containing large Buddha figures. Yaofangdong Cave contains 140 inscription recording treatments for various diseases and illnesses. Work on the sculpture in this cave continued over a 150 year period, illustrating changes in artistic style. The sculptural styles discovered in the Buddhist caves of the Tang Dynasty in the 7th and 8th centuries, particularly the giant sculptures in the Fengxiansi Cave are the most fully representative examples of the Royal Cave Temples’ art, which has been imitated by artists from various regions. The two sculptural art styles, the earlier “Central China Style” and the later “Great Tang Style” had great influence within the country and throughout the world, and have made important contributions to the development of the sculptural arts in other Asian countries.

History_background.cn: 两千多年吸引众多名人，文化中心
History_background.en: For over two thousand years, it has attracted numerous celebrities and served as a cultural center.

Main_function.cn: 旅游观光、文化教育中心
Main_function.en: Tourism and cultural education center

BUilding_use.cn: 寺庙、书院、别墅等多功能用途
BUilding_use.en: Multifunctional uses such as temples, academies, and villas

Brief_intro.cn: 集自然美景与丰富历史文化于一体，拥有众多历史建筑和寺院，是中国山水文化与中西文化交融的代表性景区。
Brief_intro.en: Combining spectacular natural scenery with rich historical and cultural heritage, Lushan National Park features numerous historic buildings and monasteries, and stands as a representative landscape of Chinese nature culture and the convergence of Eastern and Western cultural traditions.

Standard.cn: 庐山风景名胜区寺庙和教育建筑的建造和布局，形成了从公元前3世纪末汉代到20世纪初漫长时期内价值观交流的文化景观。
Standard.en: The construction and layout of temples and educational buildings in the Lushan Scenic Area formed a cultural landscape of value exchange over a long period from the late 3rd century BC (Han Dynasty) to the early 20th century.

Standard.cn: 庐山山水激发了哲学和艺术的灵感。将优质文化遗产有选择、有意识地融入这片山水之中，充分体现了中国人对自然美景与文化和谐共生的欣赏。
Standard.en: The landscape of Mount Lu has inspired philosophy and art. The selective and conscious integration of high-quality cultural heritage into this landscape fully reflects the Chinese people's appreciation for the harmonious coexistence of natural beauty and culture.

Standard.cn: 白鹿洞书院的古建筑群是中国传统书院建筑的典范。观音桥是一座榫卯结构的石拱桥，在中国桥梁建造史上占有举足轻重的地位。现代别墅群则见证了19世纪末至20世纪中叶西方文化对中国内陆地区的渗透。
Standard.en: The ancient architectural complex of Bailudong Academy is a model of traditional Chinese academy architecture. Guanyin Bridge is a stone arch bridge with mortise and tenon joints, holding a pivotal position in the history of Chinese bridge construction. The modern villa complex bears witness to the penetration of Western culture into inland China from the late 19th to the mid-20th century.

Standard.cn: 慧远在庐山东林寺创立净土宗，开启了佛教在中国本土化的时代。朱熹重振白鹿洞书院，使其成为宋明儒家唯心主义思想普及的典范，以及书院教育的典范。他的影响在宋代之后持续了七百余年。朱熹诠释的儒家唯心主义思想及其教育模式远播日本、韩国、印度尼西亚等地，在全球教育史上扮演了极其重要的角色。
Standard.en: Huiyuan founded the Pure Land School at Donglin Temple on Mount Lu, ushering in an era of Buddhism's localization in China. Zhu Xi revitalized the White Deer Grotto Academy, making it a model for the popularization of Song-Ming Confucian idealism and a paradigm of academy education. His influence lasted for over seven hundred years after the Song Dynasty. Zhu Xi's interpretation of Confucian idealism and his educational model spread to Japan, Korea, Indonesia, and other places, playing an extremely important role in the history of global education.

Description.cn: 庐山位于江西省九江市。庐山国家公园总面积30200公顷，最高峰汉阳峰海拔1474米。庐山北临长江，南濒鄱阳湖，江、山、湖三景浑然一体，两千多年来，其秀丽风光吸引着无数精神领袖、学者、艺术家和作家。庐山国家公园内拥有200多座历史建筑，这些经多次重建和扩建的寺院群，构成了一个持续至今的学习和宗教中心。其中包括始建于公元386年的慧远东林寺；始建于公元730年左右的西林塔；唐代建造的清静寺曾是道教经典的存放地；白鹿洞书院始建于公元940年，后于12世纪末宋代朱熹时期复兴，朱熹大力弘扬孔子的政治伦理思想。此后，该建筑群不断扩建，直至19世纪，囊括了众多寺庙、书院和图书馆。其他重要景点还包括建于公元1015年的单跨石桥——观音桥，以及遍布悬崖峭壁和石碑的900余处碑文。此外，19世纪末20世纪初，随着该地区成为热门度假胜地，中国和外国游客在此建造了约600座别墅。20世纪30年代至40年代，这里曾是中华民国的官方避暑胜地。这些别墅风格各异，布局也符合当时盛行的西方规划理念。庐山在中国历史文化中占有举足轻重的地位。它是中国山水文化的杰出代表，也是中国书院教育的典范，更是中西文化交融的汇聚点，曾是中国南方的文化中心。庐山历史上发生的重大文化发展和政治事件，对中国历史进程产生了深远的影响。庐山的自然美景与历史建筑和特色完美融合，形成独具特色的文化景观，蕴含着卓越的审美价值，与中国的精神文化生活紧密相连。庐山自然与文化的交融，代表着中华民族精神，是中华文化生活的缩影。
Description.en: Mount Lushan is located in Jiujiang City, Jiangxi Province. The property area of Lushan National Park occupies a total area of 30,200 hectaresand its highest Peak, Hanyang Peak, is 1,474 meters above sea level. Bordered on the north by the Yangtze River and on the south by Poyang Lake, Mount Lushan presents an integral scene of river, hills and lake, the beauty of which has attracted spiritual leaders, scholars, artists and writers for over 2,000 years. More than 200 historic buildings are located in the Lushan National Park; complexes of prayer halls that have been rebuilt and extended many times to create an ongoing centre for study and religion. These include the Buddhist East Grove Temple complex begun by Huiyuan in 386 CE; the West Grove Pagoda begun around 730 CE; the Temple of Simplicity and Tranquility built during the Tang dynasty as the repository of Taoist scriptures, and the White Deer Cave Academy originally established in 940 CE and revived in the late 12th century during the Song dynasty when Zhu Xi instigated the spread of Confucius’ political and ethical teaching. This complex continued to be extended up to the 19th century to include many temples, study halls and libraries. Other important features include the stone single-span Guan Ying Bridge of 1,015 CE and more than 900 inscriptions on cliffs and stone tablets. In addition there are around 600 villas built by Chinese and foreign visitors in the late 19th and 20th centuries, when the area became a popular resort and was, during the 1930s and 40s the official Summer Capital of the Republic of China.  The villas reflect various architectural fashions and are laid out within the landscape in accordance with Western planning concepts prevalent at the time.Mount Lushan has an important place in Chinese history and culture. It is an outstanding representative of Chinese landscape culture, as well as a remarkable model of Chinese academy-based education, and a focal point for the integration of Chinese and Western cultures, once acting as the cultural center of southern China. The significant cultural developments and political events occurring over the course of Lushan’s history have influenced the course of Chinese history.The natural beauty of Lushan is perfectly integrated with its historic buildings and features, creating a unique cultural landscape which embodies outstanding aesthetic value powerfully associated with Chinese spiritual and cultural life. Combining nature and culture, Mount Lushan represents the Chinese national spirit and epitomizes its cultural life.

Name.en: Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor

Dynast.cn: 秦朝(公元前221年 - 公元前206年)

History_background.cn: 秦始皇统一中国后修建的陵墓
History_background.en: The mausoleum built by Qin Shi Huang after unifying China

Main_function.cn: 秦始皇的帝王陵墓
Main_function.en: Qin Shi Huang's Imperial Mausoleum

BUilding_use.en: Imperial burial sites and funerary objects

Brief_intro.cn: 中国历史上规模最大的帝王陵墓，内有大量陶俑和珍贵文物，展示了秦朝的强盛与艺术成就。
Brief_intro.en: The largest imperial mausoleum in Chinese history, it contains vast numbers of terracotta figures and precious artifacts that showcase the might and artistic achievements of the Qin dynasty.

Standard.cn: 由于其卓越的技术和艺术品质，陶俑和陶马以及青铜葬车是汉代以前中国雕塑史上的重要作品。
Standard.en: Due to their superior technical and artistic quality, terracotta figurines, terracotta horses, and bronze funerary chariots are important works in the history of Chinese sculpture before the Han Dynasty.

Standard.cn: 这组雕像群为战国时期（公元前475-221年）和短暂存在的千代帝国时期（公元前221-210年）的中国军事组织提供了独特的见证。出土文物（长矛、刀剑、斧头、戟、弓箭等）的直接证据显而易见。这组高度写实的雕塑，从战士的服饰、武器到马匹的缰绳，每一个细节都刻画得淋漓尽致，其文献价值极其巨大。此外，从这些雕像中还蕴含着关于陶工和青铜工匠工艺和技术的宝贵信息。
Standard.en: This group of sculptures provides unique evidence of Chinese military organization during the Warring States period (475-221 BC) and the short-lived Thousand Generations Empire (221-210 BC). The direct evidence from unearthed artifacts (spears, swords, axes, halberds, bows and arrows, etc.) is readily apparent. The highly realistic sculptures, depicting every detail from the warriors' clothing and weapons to the horse reins, possess immense documentary value. Furthermore, these sculptures contain invaluable information about the craftsmanship and techniques of potters and bronze artisans.

Standard.cn: 秦始皇陵是中国现存最大的遗址。它是一座独特的建筑群，其布局呼应了秦都咸阳的城市规划：皇宫被城墙环绕，城墙本身又被其他城墙所包围。这座秦都（今西安所在地先后成为汉、隋、唐三朝的都城）是秦始皇意图统一的“中央”的缩影（他推行了全国统一的文字、货币、度量衡制度），同时也是为了抵御可能来自四面八方的蛮族入侵（守卫皇帝的军队面向陵墓外侧）。
Standard.en: The Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor is the largest existing archaeological site in China. It is a unique architectural complex whose layout echoes the urban planning of Xianyang, the Qin capital: the palace is surrounded by city walls, which in turn are encircled by other city walls. This Qin capital (located in present-day Xi'an, which subsequently served as the capital of the Han, Sui, and Tang dynasties) is a microcosm of Qin Shi Huang's intention to unify the country into a "centralized" system (he implemented a unified system of writing, currency, and weights and measures), and also served to defend against potential invasions from barbarian tribes from all directions (the army guarding the emperor faces outwards from the mausoleum).

Standard.cn: 秦始皇陵与一件具有普遍意义的事件有关：公元前 221 年，一位绝对君主建立了一个中央集权国家，首次统一了中国领土。
Standard.en: The Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor is associated with an event of universal significance: in 221 BC, an absolute monarch established a centralized state and unified the territory of China for the first time.

Description.cn: 秦始皇陵位于陕西省西安市东北35公里处的梨山北麓，是秦始皇皇帝的陵墓。秦始皇于公元前3世纪建立了中国历史上第一个统一的帝国。陵墓始建于公元前246年，至今仍保存完好，其土墩高51.3米，呈南北走向的矩形双层围墙结构。陵墓周围有近200个陪葬坑，出土了数千尊真人大小的陶俑、陶马、青铜战车和兵器——这是举世闻名的考古发现。此外，陵墓内还有墓葬和建筑遗迹，总遗址超过600处，占地56.25平方公里。据史学家司马迁（约公元前145-95年）记载，为了在这座巨大的土墩内建造一座地下城，帝国各省的工匠们一直辛勤劳作，直到秦始皇于公元前210年驾崩。作为统一中国的第一位皇帝的陵墓，它是中国历史上规模最大的陵墓，拥有独特的风格和布局，以及大量精美的陪葬品。它见证了第一个统一帝国——秦朝的建立。公元前3世纪，秦朝拥有空前的政治、军事和经济实力，并极大地提升了帝国的社会、文化和艺术水平。
Description.en: Located at the northern foot of Lishan Mountain, 35 kilometers northeast of Xi'an, Shaanxi Province, Qinshihuang Mausoleum is the tomb of Emperor Qinshihuang, founder of the first unified empire in Chinese history during the 3rd century BCE. Begun in 246 BCE the grave mound survives to a height of 51.3 meters within a rectangular, double-walled enclosure oriented north-south. Nearly 200 accompanying pits containing thousands of life-size terra cotta soldiers, terra cotta horses and bronze chariots and weapons - a world-renowned discovery - together with burial tombs and architectural remains total over 600 sites within the property area of  56.25 square kilometers. According to the historian Sima Qian (c. 145-95 BCE), workers from every province of the Empire toiled unceasingly until the death of the Emperor in 210 in order to construct a subterranean city within a gigantic mound.As the tomb of the first emperor who unified the country, it is the largest in Chinese history, with a unique standard and layout, and a large number of exquisite funeral objects. It testifies to the founding of the first unified empire- the Qin Dynasty, which during the 3rd BCE, wielded unprecedented political, military and economic power and advanced the social, cultural and artistic level of the empire.

History_background.cn: 始建于公元366年，佛教艺术宝库
History_background.en: Built in 366 AD, a treasure trove of Buddhist art

Main_function.cn: 保存和展示佛教艺术
Main_function.en: Preservation and display of Buddhist art

BUilding_use.cn: 佛教石窟寺庙和艺术保存
BUilding_use.en: Buddhist cave temples and art preservation

Brief_intro.cn: 世界最大佛教艺术宝库，拥有492窟，壁画面积约4.5万平方米，彩塑2000余件，是中国佛教艺术的巅峰代表。
Brief_intro.en: The world's largest repository of Buddhist art, the Mogao Caves encompass 492 grottoes, approximately 45,000 square meters of murals, and over 2,000 painted sculptures, representing the highest pinnacle of Chinese Buddhist artistic achievement.

Standard.cn: 莫高窟石窟群在空间组织上独具特色，共有 492 个洞窟，分五层建造；此外，还创作了 2000 多件彩绘雕塑和约 45000 平方米的壁画，其中不乏中国艺术杰作。
Standard.en: The Mogao Grottoes are unique in their spatial organization, comprising 492 caves built in five layers. In addition, more than 2,000 painted sculptures and murals covering approximately 45,000 square meters were created, including many masterpieces of Chinese art.

Standard.cn: 从北魏时期（386-534 年）到蒙古统治的元朝时期（1276-1386 年），莫高窟在长达 1000 年的时间里，在中国、中亚和印度之间的艺术交流中发挥了决定性作用。
Standard.en: From the Northern Wei Dynasty (386-534 AD) to the Yuan Dynasty under Mongol rule (1276-1386 AD), the Mogao Caves played a decisive role in the artistic exchange between China, Central Asia, and India for a period of 1,000 years.

Standard.cn: 莫高窟的绘画是隋、唐、宋时期中国古代文明的杰出见证。
Standard.en: The paintings in Mogao Grottoes are outstanding evidence of ancient Chinese civilization during the Sui, Tang, and Song dynasties.

Standard.cn: 千佛洞是佛教岩画圣地的杰出范例。
Standard.en: The Thousand Buddha Caves are an outstanding example of a sacred site of Buddhist rock paintings.

Standard.cn: 莫高窟岩画群由敦煌文物研究所管理，自 19 世纪末至 1930 年一直由佛教僧侣居住，保存了传统僧侣聚落的范例。
Standard.en: The Mogao Grottoes rock paintings are managed by the Dunhuang Cultural Relics Research Institute. From the late 19th century to 1930, they were inhabited by Buddhist monks, preserving an example of a traditional monastic settlement.

Standard.cn: 敦煌石窟与跨大陆交流的历史以及佛教在亚洲的传播密切相关。几个世纪以来，丝绸之路两条支线在此分岔，敦煌绿洲一直是重要的中转站，不仅商品在此交易，思想也在此交流，石窟中发现的汉字、藏文、粟特文、和田文、维吾尔文甚至希伯来文手稿便是明证。
Standard.en: The Dunhuang Grottoes are closely related to the history of transcontinental exchanges and the spread of Buddhism in Asia. For centuries, the two branches of the Silk Road diverged here, and the Dunhuang oasis was an important transit point. Not only were goods traded here, but ideas were also exchanged, as evidenced by the Chinese, Tibetan, Sogdian, Khotanese, Uyghur, and even Hebrew manuscripts found in the grottoes.

Description.cn: 莫高窟位于甘肃省敦煌绿洲东南部，开凿于大川河畔的峭壁之上，是世界上规模最大、藏品最丰富、使用时间最长的佛教艺术宝库。它始建于公元366年，代表了公元4世纪至14世纪佛教艺术的巅峰成就。现存492窟，壁画总面积约4.5万平方米，彩绘雕塑超过2000件。隋代302窟描绘了丝绸之路上文化交流的场景，生动展现了当时典型的商队骆驼拉车的景象，是现存最古老、最生动的丝绸之路文化交流场景之一。唐代第23窟和第156窟分别描绘了田间劳作的工人和一队武士；宋代第61窟描绘了著名的五台山风景，这是中国早期艺术地图的典范，其中没有遗漏任何东西——山脉、河流、城市、寺庙、道路和商队都被描绘了出来。作为中国西北地区佛教艺术发展历程的见证，莫高窟具有无可比拟的历史价值。这些作品生动地展现了中世纪中国西部地区的政治、经济、文化、艺术、宗教、民族关系以及日常生活等方方面面。敦煌艺术独特的风格不仅融合了汉族艺术传统以及从古印度和犍陀罗文化中吸收的元素，更吸收了突厥、古藏族和其他少数民族的艺术。其中许多杰作都出自无与伦比的艺术天才之手。1990年莫高窟书窟的发现，以及其中出土的数万件手稿和文物，被誉为世界古代东方文化最伟大的发现。这一重要的文化遗产为研究古代中国和中亚的复杂历史提供了宝贵的参考资料。
Description.en: Carved into the cliffs above the Dachuan River, the Mogao Caves south-east of the Dunhuang oasis, Gansu Province, comprise the largest, most richly endowed, and longest used treasure house of Buddhist art in the world. It was first constructed in 366AD and represents the great achievement of Buddhist art from the 4th to the 14th century. 492 caves are presently preserved, housing about 45,000 square meters of murals and more than 2,000 painted sculptures. Cave 302 of the Sui dynasty contains one of the oldest and most vivid scenes of cultural exchanges along the Silk Road, depicting a camel pulling a cart typical of trade missions of that period. Caves 23 and 156 of the Tang dynasty show workers in the fields and a line of warriors respectively and in the Song dynasty Cave 61, the celebrated landscape of Mount Wutai is an early example of artistic Chinese cartography, where nothing has been left out – mountains, rivers, cities, temples, roads and caravans are all depicted.As evidence of the evolution of Buddhist art in the northwest region of China, the Mogao Caves are of unmatched historical value. These works provide an abundance of vivid materials depicting various aspects of medieval politics, economics, culture, arts, religion, ethnic relations, and daily dress in western China. The unique artistic style of Dunhuang art is not only the amalgamation of Han Chinese artistic tradition and styles assimilated from ancient Indian and Gandharan customs, but also an integration of the arts of the Turks, ancient Tibetans and other Chinese ethnic minorities. Many of these masterpieces are creations of an unparalleled aesthetic talent.The discovery of the Library Cave at the Mogao Caves in 1990, together with the tens of thousands of manuscripts and relics it contained, has been acclaimed as the world’s greatest discovery of ancient Oriental culture. This significant heritage provides invaluable reference for studying the complex history of ancient China and Central Asia.

Name.en: Mount Qingcheng and the Dujiangyan Irrigation System

Dynast.cn: 汉朝(公元前202年 - 公元220年)

History_background.cn: 都江堰始建于公元前256年，道教于青城山创立于公元142年。
History_background.en: The Dujiangyan Irrigation System was first built in 256 BC, and Taoism was founded on Mount Qingcheng in 142 AD.

Main_function.cn: 防洪、灌溉、输水和日常用水
Main_function.en: Flood control, irrigation, water conveyance and daily water use

BUilding_use.cn: 水利工程和道教活动场所
BUilding_use.en: Water conservancy projects and Taoist activity sites

Brief_intro.cn: 古代水利工程奇迹，至今灌溉平原数十万万公顷。同时也是道教发源地，保存多座古道观，体现川西传统建筑风格。
Brief_intro.en: A marvel of ancient hydraulic engineering that continues to irrigate hundreds of thousands of hectares of plains today, this site is also a cradle of Taoism and preserves numerous ancient Taoist temples representing the traditional architectural style of western Sichuan.

Standard.cn: 都江堰灌溉系统始于公元前2世纪，是水利管理和技术发展史上的一个重要里程碑，至今仍在完美地发挥其功能。
Standard.en: The Dujiangyan Irrigation System, which originated in the 2nd century BC, is an important milestone in the history of water conservancy management and technological development, and it continues to function perfectly to this day.

Standard.cn: 都江堰灌溉系统生动地展现了古代中国在科学技术方面取得的巨大进步。
Standard.en: The Dujiangyan Irrigation System vividly demonstrates the tremendous progress made by ancient China in science and technology.

Standard.cn: 青城山寺庙与道教的创立密切相关，道教是东亚历史上最具影响力的宗教之一。
Standard.en: The temples of Qingcheng Mountain are closely related to the founding of Taoism, one of the most influential religions in East Asian history.

Description.cn: 都江堰灌溉系统位于成都平原西部，地处四川盆地与青藏高原交界处，是一项生态工程奇迹，始建于公元前256年左右。历经唐、宋、元、明四代的改造扩建，该系统利用自然地形和水文特征，在不筑坝的情况下，解决了引水灌溉、排沙、防洪和流量控制等问题。如今，该系统由两部分组成：位于海拔726米、距都江堰市1公里处（成都平原最高点）的堰坝工程，以及灌溉区。堰坝工程的三大关键工程——鱼嘴绕流堤、飞沙堰闸和宝坪口引水渠——控制着岷江上游河谷的水流。连同白丈堤、二王寺水渠和V形堤等辅助堤坝和水道，这些工程设施确保了成都平原的稳定供水。该系统在防洪、灌溉、输水和日常用水等方面都取得了显著成效。始建于2250多年前，如今灌溉面积达66.87万公顷。青城山雄踞都江堰水利系统南侧的成都平原，在中国历史上享有盛名。公元142年，哲学家张陵在此创立了中国道教。金唐时期，青城山上兴建了一系列道观，道教的教义也由此传播开来，并融入了道教文化的精髓。17世纪，青城山再次成为道教的学术和精神中心。山上至今仍保留着十一座重要的道观，它们体现了川西地区的传统建筑风格，其中包括二王寺、福隆寺、张陵讲经之地的长道寺以及建府宫（原张仁寺）。
Description.en: The Dujiangyan irrigation system, located in the western portion of the Chengdu flatlands at the junction between the Sichuan basin and the Qinghai-Tibet plateau, is an ecological engineering feat originally constructed around 256 BC. Modified and enlarged during the Tang, Song, Yuan and Ming dynasties, it uses natural topographic and hydrological features to solve problems of diverting water for irrigation, draining sediment, flood control, and flow control without the use of dams. Today the system comprises two parts: the Weir Works, located at an altitude of 726m, the highest point of the Chengdu plain 1km from Dujiangyan City, and the irrigated area. Three key components of the Weir Works control the water from the upper valley of the Minjiang River: the Yuzui Bypass Dike, the Feishayan Floodgate, and the Baopingkou Diversion Passage. Together with ancillary embankments and watercourses including the Baizhang Dike, the Erwang Temple Watercourse and the V-Shaped Dike, these structures ensure a regular supply of water to the Chengdu plains. The system has produced comprehensive benefits in flood control, irrigation, water transport and general water consumption. Begun over 2,250 years ago, it now irrigates 668,700 hectares of farmland.Mount Qingcheng, dominating the Chengdu plains to the south of the Dujiangyan Irrigation System, is a mountain famous in Chinese history as the place where in 142 CE the philosopher Zhang Ling founded the doctrine of Chinese Taoism. Most of the essential elements of Taoism culture are embodied in the teachings of Taoism that emanated from the temples that were subsequently built on the mountain during the Jin and Tang dynasties. The mountain resumed its role as the intellectual and spiritual centre of Taoism in the 17th century. The eleven important Taoist temples on the mountain reflect the traditional architecture of western Sichuan and include the Erwang Temple, the Fulong Temple, the Changdao Temple built over the place where Zhang Ling preached his doctrines, and the Jianfu Palace (formerly the Zhangren Temple).

Dynast.cn: 汉朝(公元前202年 - 公元220年)

History_background.cn: 自北魏起即为佛教圣地
History_background.en: It has been a Buddhist holy site since the Northern Wei Dynasty.

Main_function.cn: 佛教朝圣与文化传承中心
Main_function.en: Buddhist Pilgrimage and Cultural Heritage Center

BUilding_use.cn: 佛教寺庙、藏书和朝圣活动场所
BUilding_use.en: Buddhist temples, libraries and pilgrimage sites

Brief_intro.cn: 中国佛教四大圣山之一，拥有丰富寺院群，历史悠久，是文殊菩萨信仰中心，至今吸引众多朝圣者。
Brief_intro.en: One of the four sacred mountains of Chinese Buddhism, Mount Wutai possesses a rich concentration of ancient monasteries and is the central site of Manjushri Bodhisattva veneration, continuing to attract pilgrims from across the world.

Standard.cn: 五台山的整体宗教寺庙景观，包括其佛教建筑、雕像和宝塔，反映了思想的深刻交流，这座山成为了神圣的佛教场所，拥有反映尼泊尔和蒙古思想的寺庙，进而影响了中国各地的佛教寺庙。
Standard.en: The overall religious temple landscape of Mount Wutai, including its Buddhist architecture, statues, and pagodas, reflects a profound exchange of ideas. The mountain became a sacred Buddhist site, home to temples reflecting Nepalese and Mongolian thought, which in turn influenced Buddhist temples throughout China.

Standard.cn: 五台山是寺院林立、宗教山地文化传统的杰出代表。它曾是亚洲各地朝圣者的中心，这一文化传统至今依然延续。
Standard.en: Mount Wutai is an outstanding representative of the numerous temples and religious mountain culture traditions. It was once a center for pilgrims from all over Asia, and this cultural tradition continues to this day.

Standard.cn: 五台山的景观和建筑群整体上体现了1000年来皇室赞助的非凡效果，山地景观被建筑、雕像、绘画和碑文所装饰，以庆祝其对佛教徒的圣洁。
Standard.en: The landscape and architectural complex of Mount Wutai as a whole reflects the extraordinary effects of 1,000 years of royal patronage. The mountain landscape is decorated with buildings, sculptures, paintings and inscriptions to celebrate its sanctity to Buddhists.

Standard.cn: 五台山完美地体现了自然景观与佛教文化、自然景观中的宗教信仰与中国哲学中人与自然和谐的思想的融合。五台山的影响深远：在韩国、日本以及中国其他地区，如甘肃、山西、河北、广东等省份，都有与五台山相似的山峰以它命名。
Standard.en: Mount Wutai perfectly embodies the fusion of natural landscape and Buddhist culture, the religious beliefs within the natural landscape and the Chinese philosophical concept of harmony between humanity and nature. Mount Wutai's influence is far-reaching: similar peaks are named after it in South Korea, Japan, and other parts of China, such as Gansu, Shanxi, Hebei, and Guangdong provinces.

Description.cn: 五台山拥有五座平坦的山峰，是中国佛教四大圣山之一，也是全球佛教文殊菩萨崇拜的中心。山上共有五十三座寺院，其中包括佛光寺东殿，殿内有真人大小的泥塑，是唐代现存最高的木结构建筑；还有明代的舒祥寺，寺内有五百尊悬空佛像，以立体山水图景展现佛教故事。这些寺院与山地景观密不可分。五台山山峰巍峨，常年积雪，遍布茂密的松树、杉树、杨树和柳树，草地葱郁，其美景至少从唐代起就为艺术家们所赞颂——敦煌石窟便是其中的代表。两千年的寺庙建设，造就了五台山丰富的寺院群，展现了佛教建筑的发展历程，以及它对中国乃至亚洲部分地区宫殿建筑的影响。自北魏时期（471-499年）起，一千年间，九位皇帝十八次前往五台山朝拜菩萨，这些事迹被铭刻于碑文之上。由皇帝开创的五台山朝圣传统至今依然盛行。五台山寺院藏书丰富，汇集了历代皇帝和学者的大量藏书，至今仍是佛教文化的重要宝库，吸引着来自亚洲各地的朝圣者。
Description.en: Mount Wutai with its five flat peaks is one of the four sacred Buddhist mountains in China. It is seen as the global centre for Buddhist Manjusri worship. Its fifty-three monasteries, include the East Main Hall of Foguang Temple, with life size clay sculptures, the highest ranking timber building to survive from the Tang Dynasty, and the Ming Dynasty Shuxiang Temple with a huge complex of 500 ‘suspension’ statues, representing Buddhist stories woven into three dimensional pictures of mountains and water. The temples are inseparable from their mountain landscape. With its high peaks, snow covered for much of the year, thick forests of vertical pines, firs, poplar and willow trees and lush grassland, the beauty of the landscape has been celebrated by artists since at least the Tang Dynasty – including in the Dunhuang caves. Two millennia of temple building have delivered an assembly of temples that present a catalogue of the way Buddhist architecture developed and influenced palace building over a wide part of China and part of Asia. For a thousand years from the Northern Wei period (471-499) nine Emperors made 18 pilgrimages to pay tribute to the bodhisattvas, commemorated in stele and inscriptions. Started by the Emperors, the tradition of pilgrimage to the five peaks is still very much alive. With the extensive library of books collected by Emperors and scholars, the monasteries of Mount Wutai remain an important repository of Buddhist culture, and attract pilgrims from across a wide part of Asia.

Name.cn: 承德避暑山庄及其周围寺庙
Name.en: Mountain Resort and its Outlying Temples, Chengde

History_background.cn: 清朝皇帝修建的夏宫和行政据点
History_background.en: Summer palaces and administrative outposts built by Qing Dynasty emperors

Main_function.cn: 皇家避暑、处理政务、民族交流
Main_function.en: Royal summer retreat, handling of government affairs, and ethnic exchanges

BUilding_use.cn: 宫殿、园林及寺庙的集合体
BUilding_use.en: A collection of palaces, gardens and temples

Brief_intro.cn: 中国现存最大的皇家宫殿、园林和寺庙建筑群，融合汉、蒙、藏建筑艺术，是中国园林和建筑艺术的杰作。
Brief_intro.en: The largest surviving complex of imperial palaces, gardens, and temples in China, this mountain resort integrates Han, Mongolian, and Tibetan architectural traditions and stands as a masterpiece of Chinese landscape and architectural art.

Standard.cn: 山地度假区及其外围寺庙的景观是中国将建筑融入自然环境的杰出范例，对景观设计产生了深远的影响，并且这种影响至今仍在持续。
Standard.en: The landscape of the mountain resort and its surrounding temples is an outstanding example of how architecture can be integrated into the natural environment in China. It has had a profound influence on landscape design, and this influence continues to this day.

Standard.cn: 山地度假区及其外围寺庙以物质形式代表了中国封建社会的最终繁荣。
Standard.en: The mountain resort and its surrounding temples represent, in material form, the ultimate prosperity of Chinese feudal society.

Description.cn: 承德宫园及其外围寺庙群是中国现存最大的皇家宫殿、园林和寺庙建筑群，总面积达611.2公顷。承德宫园始建于1703年至1792年间，是清朝皇帝在距北京350公里木兰狩猎场附近的一座独立夏宫，也是加强边疆行政管理的重要据点。12座外围寺庙分布在宫殿和园林区域以外的东、北山丘上，部分寺庙采用了少数民族建筑风格，这些寺庙促进了与少数民族的关系，并有助于保卫承德宫园。每年夏秋两季，包括康熙和乾隆在内的清朝皇帝都会在此处理政务，接见少数民族领袖和外国使节，并从这里北上举行木兰秋猎。清朝时期许多重要的历史事件都发生在这里，历史遗迹和文物见证了中国作为一个统一的多民族国家的巩固和发展。承德山庄及其外寺是中国宫殿建筑、园林艺术和宗教建筑的经典杰作。山庄依山傍水，依地势而建，是中国自然景观园林和宫殿的杰出典范，传承并发扬了中国皇家园林传统。外寺融合了汉、蒙、藏三族建筑艺术与文化元素，体现了中国建筑发展进程中不同民族文化交流与融合的成果。山地度假区及其外围寺庙的人工景观与承德独特的自然环境（如丹霞地貌）完美融合。其自然和谐的布局，是中国传统风水文化的成功实践。作为中国古代园林设计的代表，它曾对欧洲产生影响，并在18世纪世界园林设计史上扮演了重要角色。
Description.en: The Mountain Resort of palaces and gardens at Chengde with its Outlying Temples is the largest existing imperial palace-garden and temple complex in China, covering a total area of 611.2ha. Built between 1703 and 1792 as the Qing emperors’ detached summer palace near the imperial Mulan hunting ground 350 kilometres from Beijing, it was a base from which to strengthen administration in the border regions. The 12 outlying imperial temples, some built in the architectural styles of the ethnic minorities, are distributed across the eastern and northern hills outside the palace and garden area. They fostered relations with the ethnic minorities and helped to safeguard the Mountain Resort. Every summer and autumn, emperors of the Qing dynasty including Kangxi and Qianlong handled military and government affairs of the country and received leaders of ethnic minority groups and diplomatic envoys from foreign countries here, and went north from here to hold the Mulan Autumn Hunting. Important historical events of the Qing dynasty took place here, and the historical sites and objects have witnessed the consolidation and development of China as a unitary multi-ethnic state.The Mountain Resort and its Outlying Temples, Chengde is a classic masterpiece of Chinese palace architecture, gardening art and religious architecture.The landscape of the Mountain Resort is designed following the topography of natural hills and water. As an outstanding example of Chinese natural landscape gardens and palaces, it inherits and carries forward China’s imperial gardening tradition. By integrating elements of Han, Mongolian and Tibetan architectural art and culture the Outlying Temples crystallize the achievements of cultural exchanges and integration among different ethnic groups in the course of development of Chinese architecture.The manmade landscape of the Mountain Resort and its Outlying Temples perfectly integrates with the special natural environment of Chengde, such as the danxia landform. Its natural and harmonious layout is a successful practice of the traditional Chinese geomantic culture (fengshui). As a representative of ancient Chinese garden design, it once exerted influence in Europe, and has played an important role in the history of 18th century landscape garden design worldwide.

History_background.cn: 明代始建，宋元时期扩展
History_background.en: It was first built in the Ming Dynasty and expanded during the Song and Yuan Dynasties.

Main_function.cn: 商业中心及居住区
Main_function.en: Business centers and residential areas

BUilding_use.cn: 政府办公、民居、宗教活动
BUilding_use.en: Government offices, residences, and religious activities

Brief_intro.cn: 融合汉藏建筑和纳西族文化，是人类居住的杰出典范。
Brief_intro.en: Integrating Han and Tibetan architectural traditions with the indigenous Naxi culture, the Old Town of Lijiang is an outstanding example of human settlement and land use.

Standard.cn: 自12世纪起，丽江古城成为四川、云南、西藏三国贸易的重要货物集散地，也是南方丝绸之路与古代茶马道的交汇点。丽江古城逐渐发展成为纳西族、汉族、藏族、白族等各民族经济文化交流的重要中心。过去800年间的文化和技术交流，造就了丽江古城独特的建筑、艺术、城市规划、景观、社会生活、风俗习惯、工艺美术等文化特征，这些特征既融合了汉族、白族、藏族等民族的精髓，又展现出鲜明的纳西族特色。尤其值得一提的是，宗教建筑及其他建筑中的壁画，体现了儒、道、佛三教和谐共存的景象。
Standard.en: Since the 12th century, Lijiang Old Town has been an important distribution center for goods traded between Sichuan, Yunnan, and Tibet, and a crossroads of the Southern Silk Road and the ancient Tea Horse Road. Lijiang Old Town gradually developed into a vital center for economic and cultural exchange among various ethnic groups, including the Naxi, Han, Tibetan, and Bai. The cultural and technological exchanges over the past 800 years have shaped the unique cultural characteristics of Lijiang Old Town, including its architecture, art, urban planning, landscape, social life, customs, and arts and crafts. These characteristics not only integrate the essence of Han, Bai, and Tibetan cultures but also showcase the distinct features of the Naxi people. Particularly noteworthy are the murals in religious and other buildings, which reflect the harmonious coexistence of Confucianism, Taoism, and Buddhism.

Standard.cn: 丽江古城分为三个部分：大雁古城（包括黑龙潭）、白沙住宅区和束河住宅区，充分体现了不同时期的社会、经济和文化特征，顺应山水自然地形，形成了纳西族、汉族、白族和藏族居住传统的杰出聚落。
Standard.en: Lijiang Old Town is divided into three parts: Dayan Old Town (including Black Dragon Pool), Baisha Residential Area and Shuhe Residential Area. These areas fully reflect the social, economic and cultural characteristics of different periods and, in accordance with the natural terrain, have formed outstanding settlements inhabited by the Naxi, Han, Bai and Tibetan ethnic groups.

Standard.cn: 丽江古城将山水、树木和建筑融为一体，营造出人与自然和谐共生的宜居环境。古城北临绵延至平原的群山，东、南接平原，几何关系合理，生态布局均衡。发源于雪山的支流水系蜿蜒流经村落和农田，黑龙潭及散布的水井、泉眼构成完整的水系，满足城镇的消防、生活和生产需求。水在古城独特的建筑风格、城市布局和景观中扮演着重要角色，主干道和小巷临河而建，部分建筑和众多桥梁横跨河道。作为人与自然和谐共生的典范，丽江古城是人类土地利用智慧的杰出代表。
Standard.en: Lijiang Old Town seamlessly integrates mountains, water, trees, and architecture, creating a livable environment where humans and nature coexist harmoniously. The old town is bordered by mountains stretching to the north, extending into the plains, and bordered by plains to the east and south, resulting in a rational geometric relationship and balanced ecological layout. Tributaries originating from the snow-capped mountains meander through villages and farmland, with Black Dragon Pool and scattered wells and springs forming a complete water system that meets the town's needs for fire fighting, daily life, and production. Water plays a vital role in the old town's unique architectural style, urban layout, and landscape; main roads and alleys are built along the rivers, and some buildings and numerous bridges span the waterways. As a model of harmonious coexistence between humans and nature, Lijiang Old Town is an outstanding example of human wisdom in land use.

Description.cn: 丽江古城位于中国云南省西南部的丽江平原，海拔2400米，四周群山环抱，战略要道纵横交错。西北部的玉龙雪山是众多河流和泉水的源头，滋养着平原，并汇入黑龙潭。黑龙潭的水道汇入纵横交错的运河和水渠，为丽江古城供水。丽江古城由三部分组成：大雁古城（包括黑龙潭）、白沙和束河住宅区。大雁古城始建于明代，是重要的商业中心，城内有丽江郡政府办公楼、原木家宅院遗留下来的义子阁和瓜壁楼，以及黑龙潭公园内的玉泉建筑群。众多两层瓦顶木结构房屋，融合了汉藏建筑元素，拱形门廊、屏风墙、庭院和雕花屋梁等装饰风格体现了纳西族文化，并沿山势成排排列。木构件上精雕细琢着陶器、乐器、花鸟等生活及文化元素。白沙民居群始建于宋元时期，位于大雁古城以北8公里处。这里的房屋围绕着中央的阶梯式广场呈南北走向排列。宗教建筑群内有殿堂和亭台楼阁，收藏着40余幅创作于13世纪初的绘画作品，描绘了佛教、道教以及纳西族人的生活，并融入了白族文化元素。白沙民居群与位于大雁古城西北4公里处的束河民居群一样，依山傍水，共同展现了几个世纪以来当地文化、民俗和传统的交融。生机勃勃的城市空间、充满活力的水利系统、和谐的建筑群、大小适宜的舒适住宅、宜人的环境以及风格独特的民间艺术，共同构成了人类居住的杰出典范。
Description.en: The Old Town of Lijiang is located on the Lijiang plain at an elevation of 2,400 meters in southwest Yunnan, China, where a series of strategic passes give access through the surrounding mountains. The Yulong Snow Mount to the north-west is the source of the rivers and springs which water the plain and supply the Heilong Pool (Black Dragon Pond), from where waterways feed into a network of canals and channels to supply the town. The Old Town of Lijiang comprises three component parts: Dayan Old Town (including the Black Dragon Pond), Baisha and Shuhe housing clusters. Dayan Old Town was established in the Ming dynasty as a commercial centre and includes the Lijiang Junmin Prefectural Government Office; the Yizi pavilion and Guabi Tower remaining from the former Mujia compound and the Yuquan architectural structures in the Heilongtan Park. Numerous two-storeyed, tile-roofed, timber-framed houses combining elements of Han and Zang architecture and decoration in the arched gateways, screen walls, courtyards and carved roof beams are representative of the Naxi culture and are disposed in rows following the contours of the mountainside. Wooden elements are elaborately carved with domestic and cultural elements - pottery, musical instruments, flowers and birds.The Baisha housing cluster established earlier during the Song and Yuan dynasties is located 8km north of the Dayan Old Town. Houses here are arranged on a north-south axis around a central, terraced square. The religious complex includes halls and pavilions containing over 40 paintings dating from the early 13th century, which depict subjects relating to Buddhism, Taoism and the life of the Naxi people, incorporating cultural elements of the Bai people. Together with the Shuhe housing cluster located 4km north-west of Dayan Old Town, these settlements nestling in mountains and surrounded by water reflect the blend of local cultures, folk customs and traditions over several centuries.The vivid urban space, the vigorous water system, the harmonious building complexes, the comfortable residences of appropriate size, the pleasant environment, and the folk art of unique style combine to form an outstanding example of human habitat.

History_background.cn: 发现了多时期古人类化石遗址
History_background.en: Fossil sites from multiple periods of ancient humans have been discovered.

Main_function.cn: 古人类遗址考古与研究
Main_function.en: Archaeology and Research of Paleolithic Sites

Brief_intro.cn: 是亚洲重要古人类遗址，出土了多时期人类化石、石器和用火遗迹，对人类演化研究具有重要意义。
Brief_intro.en: A major paleoanthropological site in Asia, Zhoukoudian has yielded human fossils, stone tools, and evidence of fire use spanning multiple prehistoric periods, providing crucial insights into the study of human evolution.

Standard.cn: 周口店遗址见证了从中更新世到旧石器时代亚洲大陆的人类社群，说明了演化的过程。
Standard.en: The Zhoukoudian site bears witness to human communities on the Asian continent from the Middle Pleistocene to the Paleolithic period, illustrating the process of evolution.

Standard.cn: 20世纪20年代和30年代，周口店发现的古人类遗骸及其后续研究引起了全世界的关注，颠覆了此前普遍接受的人类历史年表。因此，周口店遗址的发掘和科学工作在世界考古史上具有重要价值，并在世界科学史上也发挥了重要作用。
Standard.en: The discovery of ancient human remains at Zhoukoudian in the 1920s and 30s, and subsequent research there, attracted worldwide attention, overturning previously accepted chronologies of human history. Therefore, the excavation and scientific work at the Zhoukoudian site are of great value in the history of world archaeology and have also played a significant role in the history of world science.

Description.cn: 周口店北京猿人遗址是位于华北平原的一处更新世古人类遗址。该遗址位于北京西南约42公里处，地处华北平原与燕山山脉的交界处。该地区充足的水源和天然石灰岩洞穴为早期人类提供了理想的生存环境。目前，该遗址的科学研究仍在进行中。迄今为止，科学家已在遗址内的23个地点发现了距今500万年至1万年前的古代人类化石、文化遗存和动物化石。其中包括生活在中更新世（距今70万至20万年前）的北京直立人（ Homo erectus pekinensis ）遗骸、生活在距今约20万至10万年前的早期智人（Homo sapiens）遗骸以及生活在距今3万年前的现代智人（ Homo sapiens sapiens）遗骸。与此同时，人们发现了数百种动物的化石、超过 10 万件石器以及北京猿人使用火的证据（包括火塘、灰烬沉积物和烧焦的骨头）。周口店遗址是亚洲大陆发现的重要人类遗骸遗址，展现了人类文化演化的序列，因此在全球范围内具有重要意义。它不仅是亚洲大陆史前人类社会的杰出见证，也揭示了人类演化的进程，对早期人类历史的研究和重建具有重要价值。
Description.en: Peking Man Site at Zhoukoudian is a Pleistocene hominid site on the North China Plain. This site lies about 42 km south-west of Beijing and is at the juncture of the North China Plain and the Yanshan Mountains. Adequate water supplies and natural limestone caves in this area provided an optimal survival environment for early humans. Scientific work at the site is still under way. So far, ancient human fossils, cultural remains and animal fossils from 23 localities within the property dating from 5 million years ago to 10,000 years ago have been discovered by scientists. These include the remains of Homo erectus pekinensis, who lived in the Middle Pleistocene (700,000 to 200,000 years ago), archaic Homo sapiens of about 200,000–100,000 years ago and Homo sapiens sapiens dating back to 30,000 years ago. At the same time, fossils of hundreds of animal species, over 100,000 pieces of stone tools and evidence (including hearths, ash deposits and burnt bones) of Peking Man using fire have been discovered.As the site of significant hominid remains discovered in the Asian continent demonstrating an evolutionary cultural sequence, Zhoukoudian is of major importance within the worldwide context. It is not only an exceptional reminder of the prehistoric human societies of the Asian continent, but also illustrates the process of human evolution, and is of significant value in the research and reconstruction of early human history.

Name.cn: 泉州：宋元中国的世界海洋商贸中心
Name.en: Quanzhou: Emporium of the World in Song-Yuan China

History_background.cn: 宋元时期泉州为世界贸易中心
History_background.en: Quanzhou was a world trade center during the Song and Yuan dynasties.

Main_function.cn: 展示泉州古代贸易繁荣
Main_function.en: Showcasing the prosperity of ancient trade in Quanzhou

Brief_intro.cn: 宋元时期东亚和东南亚贸易网络的海上枢纽，全球贸易中心和重要商业枢纽。
Brief_intro.en: A maritime hub at the center of East and Southeast Asian trade networks during the Song and Yuan dynasties, Quanzhou served as a global trading center and a vital commercial nexus.

Standard.cn: 泉州，宋元时期的世界贸易中心，通过其组成部分，出色地展现了其地域一体化的结构，以及在公元10至14世纪亚洲海上贸易高度繁荣时期，使其成为全球贸易中心和重要商业枢纽的关键制度、交通、生产、营销和社会文化因素。该遗产体现了泉州对东亚和东南亚经济文化发展的巨大贡献。
Standard.en: Quanzhou, a world trade center during the Song and Yuan dynasties, brilliantly showcases its integrated regional structure through its constituent parts. It also highlights the key institutional, transportation, production, marketing, and socio-cultural factors that made it a global trade center and important commercial hub during the period of great prosperity in Asian maritime trade from the 10th to the 14th centuries. This heritage reflects Quanzhou's significant contribution to the economic and cultural development of East and Southeast Asia.

Description.cn: 位于中国东南沿海的系列展品“泉州：宋元时期的世界贸易中心”以独特的方式展现了泉州在公元10至14世纪作为东亚和东南亚贸易网络海上枢纽的崛起和繁荣，以及将生产、运输和市场营销融为一体的空间结构，并揭示了促成泉州崛起和繁荣的关键制度、社会和文化因素。宋元时期的泉州贸易体系以位于江海交汇处的城市为中心和动力，东南临海，与世界相连；西北远眺群山，为生产提供了充足的资源；水陆交通网络则将两者紧密连接起来。该遗产的组成部分和要素包括行政建筑和构筑物遗址、宗教建筑和雕像、文化纪念遗址和纪念碑、陶瓷和铁器生产遗址，以及由桥梁、码头和宝塔组成的交通网络，这些设施曾为航海者指引方向。它们全面反映了宋元泉州独特的海洋领土、社会文化和贸易结构。
Description.en: Located on the southeast coast of China, the serial property Quanzhou: Emporium of the World in Song–Yuan China reflects in an exceptional manner the spatial structure that combined production, transportation and marketing and the key institutional, social and cultural factors that contributed to the spectacular rise and prosperity of Quanzhou as a maritime hub of the East and South-east Asia trade network during the 10th – 14th centuries AD. The Song-Yuan Quanzhou emporium system was centred and powered by the city located at the junction of river and sea, with oceans to the south-east that connected it with the world, with mountains to the far north-west that provided for production, and with a water-land transportation network that joined them all together.The component parts and contributing elements of the property include sites of administrative buildings and structures, religious buildings and statues, cultural memorial sites and monuments, production sites of ceramics and iron, as well as a transportation network formed of bridges, docks and pagodas that guided the voyagers. They comprehensively reflect the distinguishing maritime territorial, socio-cultural and trade structures of Song-Yuan Quanzhou.

Name.cn: 丝绸之路：长安—天山廊道的路网
Name.en: Silk Roads: the Routes Network of Chang'an-Tianshan Corridor

Dynast.cn: 汉朝(公元前202年 - 公元220年)

History_background.cn: 公元前2世纪贸易量大增
History_background.en: Trade volume increased significantly in the 2nd century BC

Main_function.cn: 促进东西方贸易和文化交流
Main_function.en: Promote trade and cultural exchange between East and West

BUilding_use.cn: 遗址多为贸易、宗教、军事用途
BUilding_use.en: The sites were mostly used for trade, religion, and military purposes.

Brief_intro.cn: 连接中国与中亚、西亚等地的重要古代贸易通道，促进了经济、文化和宗教的发展，沿线分布有驿站、寺庙、城镇等遗址，见证了多种文明的交流与融合。
Brief_intro.en: An important ancient trade route connecting China with Central and West Asia, these roads facilitated economic, cultural, and religious exchange. Relay stations, temples, and town sites along the route bear witness to the meeting and merging of multiple civilizations.

Standard.cn: 大陆路线网络的庞大、超长的使用时间、遗产遗迹的多样性及其动态的相互联系、它们所促进的文化交流的丰富性、它们所连接和穿越的各种地理环境，清楚地表明了公元前 2 世纪至公元 16 世纪欧亚大陆上各个文化区域，特别是游牧草原和定居的农业/绿洲/畜牧文明之间发生的广泛互动。
Standard.en: The vastness and long period of use of the continental route network, the diversity of its heritage sites and their dynamic interconnections, the richness of cultural exchanges they facilitated, and the various geographical environments they connected and traversed clearly demonstrate the extensive interactions that occurred between different cultural regions of Eurasia from the 2nd century BCE to the 16th century CE, particularly between nomadic steppe and settled agricultural/oasis/pastoral civilizations.

Standard.cn: 天山走廊见证了公元前 2 世纪至公元 16 世纪欧亚大陆经济和文化交流的传统以及社会发展。
Standard.en: The Tianshan Corridor bears witness to the traditions of economic and cultural exchange and social development across Eurasia from the 2nd century BC to the 16th century AD.

Standard.cn: 天山走廊是高价值长途贸易促进城镇发展的杰出范例，这些城镇发展得益于精心设计的复杂水利系统，该系统从河流、水井和地下泉水收集水，供居民、旅行者和农作物灌溉使用。
Standard.en: The Tianshan Corridor is an outstanding example of how high-value long-distance trade promotes urban development, which benefits from a sophisticated and well-designed water system that collects water from rivers, wells, and underground springs for use by residents, travelers, and crops.

Standard.cn: 天山走廊与张骞西域之行直接相关，这是欧亚大陆人类文明史和文化交流史上的一个里程碑事件。它也深刻地反映了佛教对古代中国的实际影响，而佛教对东亚文化产生了重大影响。此外，天山走廊还促进了景教（公元500年传入中国）、摩尼教、琐罗亚斯德教和早期伊斯兰教的传播。走廊沿线的许多城镇也以独特的方式体现了沿途传播的思想的影响，包括水力利用、建筑和城市规划等方面。
Standard.en: The Tianshan Corridor is directly related to Zhang Qian's journey to the Western Regions, a milestone in the history of human civilization and cultural exchange across Eurasia. It also profoundly reflects the actual influence of Buddhism on ancient China, and Buddhism's significant impact on East Asian culture. Furthermore, the Tianshan Corridor facilitated the spread of Nestorianism (introduced to China around 500 AD), Manichaeism, Zoroastrianism, and early Islam. Many towns along the corridor also uniquely reflect the influence of the ideas spread along the way, including in areas such as water management, architecture, and urban planning.

Description.cn: 丝绸之路是一张环环相扣的路线网络，连接着亚洲、次大陆、中亚、西亚和近东的古代社会，促进了世界众多伟大文明的发展。它是世界上最杰出的长途交通网络之一，直线距离约7500公里，而沿特定路线延伸超过35000公里。虽然其中一些路线已经使用了数千年，但到了公元前2世纪，贸易量大幅增长，东西方之间高价值商品的长途贸易也日益频繁。这些贸易活动的政治、社会和文化影响对所有与之相关的社会都产生了深远的影响。这些路线主要用于运输原材料、食品和奢侈品。一些地区垄断了某些材料或商品，尤其是中国，它向中亚、次大陆、西亚和地中海地区供应丝绸。许多高价值的贸易商品需要长途运输——通过驮畜和船只——而且很可能是由许多不同的商人经手的。天山走廊是庞大的丝绸之路网络的一部分。它绵延约5000公里，包含着一个复杂的贸易路线网络，总长约8700公里。该网络于公元前2世纪至公元1世纪发展起来，连接中国中部的长安和中亚腹地。当时，中国和罗马帝国之间，特别是丝绸等高价值商品的长途贸易开始兴起。天山走廊在公元6世纪至14世纪期间蓬勃发展，并一直作为一条重要的贸易路线使用到16世纪。沿途极端的地理环境生动地展现了长途贸易所面临的挑战。这些路线最低海拔低于海平面154米，最高海拔达7400米，途经大河、高山湖泊、坚硬的盐滩、广袤的沙漠、白雪皑皑的山峰和肥沃的草原。气候也从极端干旱到半湿润不等；植被覆盖范围广泛，包括温带森林、温带沙漠、温带草原、高山草原和绿洲。天山走廊的路线始于汉唐时期中国的中心都城长安，位于黄土高原之上。这条路线向西延伸，途经河西走廊，翻越秦岭和祁连山，到达敦煌的玉门关。从楼兰/哈密出发，路线继续沿着天山南北两麓行进，穿过隘口，最终抵达中亚哲特地区的伊犁、楚河和塔拉斯河谷，连接起丝绸之路贸易的两大强权中心。长城走廊沿线共有33处遗址，包括各帝国和汗国的都城宫殿群、贸易定居点、佛教石窟寺、古道、驿站、关隘、烽火台、长城残段、防御工事、陵墓和宗教建筑。中华帝国建立的驿站和烽火台体系促进了贸易，而哲特苏地区各诸侯国设立的堡垒、驿站和中转站体系也发挥了重要作用。长安及其周边地区一系列宫殿反映了中华帝国1200多年来的权力中心地位；而楚河谷的城市则见证了9至14世纪哲特苏地区的权力中心及其对长途贸易的组织。从西部的库车（今库车县）到东部的洛永，一系列佛教宝塔和大型精美的石窟寺庙绵延分布，记录了佛教经喀喇昆仑从印度向东传播的过程，也展现了佛塔设计在吸收当地文化理念后的演变。这些建筑的精美程度反映了地方政府和中国中央政府的资助、富商的捐赠，以及沿途僧侣的影响——许多僧侣的游历记录可追溯至公元前2世纪。其他宗教建筑则反映了走廊沿线多种宗教（以及多个民族）的共存，包括琐罗亚斯德教（哲特苏地区粟特人的主要宗教）、摩尼教（楚河谷、柘河谷、高梭城和洛永）、景教（高梭城、新疆周边地区和长安）以及伊斯兰教（布拉那）。大规模的贸易活动催生了繁荣昌盛的大型城镇，这些城镇也以多种方式反映了定居社群与游牧社群之间的互动：例如，在哲特苏地区，游牧民族与农民以及不同民族（如突厥人和粟特人）之间存在着相互依存的关系；在天山地区，游牧社群逐渐转变为定居社群，形成了独特的建筑和规划，例如半地下建筑；在和西走廊，公元前1世纪之后，这条绵延1000英里的走廊作为农业要塞，经过规划扩张，最终发展成为定居农业社群。多样化的大型水利系统对于促进城镇、贸易定居点、堡垒和商队驿站的发展以及支撑这些发展所需的农业至关重要，例如，在极其干旱的吐鲁番盆地，许多坎儿井地下水渠至今仍在使用，为高朝城供水，而雅尔城内的深井则作为补充水源。沿河西走廊分布着规模宏大的明渠和沟渠网络，将河水引至居民点，其中在锁阳市附近仍保留着 90 公里；而在哲州地区，河水通过运河和管道进行分配，并被收集到水库中。除了作为货物和人员的运输通道外，这些路线还促进了思想、信仰和技术创新（例如与建筑和城市规划相关的创新）的非凡流动，这些创新在许多根本方面塑造了城市空间和人们的生活。
Description.en: The Silk Roads were an interconnected web of routes linking the ancient societies of Asia, the Subcontinent, Central Asia, Western Asia and the Near East, and contributed to the development of many of the world's great civilizations. They represent one of the world’s preeminent long-distance communication networks stretching as the crow flies to around 7,500 km but extending to in excess of 35,000 km along specific routes. While some of these routes had been in use for millennia, by the 2nd century BC the volume of exchange had increased substantially, as had the long distance trade between east and west in high value goods, and the political, social and cultural impacts of these movements had far-reaching consequences upon all the societies that encountered them.The routes served principally to transfer raw materials, foodstuffs, and luxury goods. Some areas had a monopoly on certain materials or goods: notably China, who supplied Central Asia, the Subcontinent, West Asia and the Mediterranean world with silk. Many of the high value trade goods were transported over vast distances – by pack animals and river craft – and probably by a string of different merchants.The Tian-shan corridor is one section or corridor of this extensive overall Silk Roads network. Extending across a distance of around 5,000 km, it encompassed a complex network of trade routes extending to some 8,700 km that developed to link Chang’an in central China with the heartland of Central Asia between the 2nd century BC and 1st century AD, when long distance trade in high value goods, particularly silk, started to expand between the Chinese and Roman Empires. It flourished between the 6th and 14th century AD and remained in use as a major trade route until the 16th century.The extremes of geography along the routes graphically illustrate the challenges of this long distance trade. Falling to 154 metres below sea level and rising to 7,400 metres above sea level, the routes touch great rivers, alpine lakes, crusty salt flats, vast deserts, snow-capped mountains and ‘fecund’ prairies. The climate varies from extreme drought to semi-humid; while vegetation covers temperate forests, temperate deserts, temperate steppes, alpine steppes and oases.Starting on the Loess plateau at Chang’an, the central capital of China in the Han and Tang Dynasties, the routes of the Tian-shan corridor passed westwards through the Hosi Corridor across the Qin and Qilian Mountains to the Yumen Pass of Dunhuang. From Loulan/Hami, they continued along the northern and southern flanks of the Tian-shan Mountain and then through passes to reach the Ili, Chuy and Talas valleys in the Zhetysu Region of Central Asia, linking two of the great power centres that drove the Silk Roads trade.Thirty-three sites along the corridor include capital cities palace complexes of various empires and Khan Kingdoms, trading settlements, Buddhist cave temples, ancient paths, posthouses, passes, beacon towers, sections of the Great Wall, fortifications, tombs and religious buildings. The formal system of posthouses and beacon towers provided by the Chinese Empire facilitated trade, as did the system of forts, caravanserai and way stations operated by states in the Zhetysu region. In and around Chang’an, a succession of palaces reflect the power centre of the Chinese Empire over 1,200 years; while the cities of the Chuy valley are witness to the power centre of the Zhetysu region from the 9th to the 14th centuries and their organisation of the long distance trade.The series of Buddhist pagodas and large, elaborate cave temples extending from Kucha (now Kuqa County) in the west to Luoyong in the east, record the eastward transmission of Buddhism from India via Karakorum, and demonstrate an evolution in the design of stupas as local ideas were absorbed. Their elaboration reflects the sponsorship of local authorities and the central Chinese imperial government as well as donations of wealthy merchants, and the influence of monks that travelled the routes, many of whose journeys were documented from 2nd century BC onwards. Other religious buildings reflect the co-existence of many religions (as well as many ethnic groups) along the corridor including Zoroastrianism, the main religion of the Sogdians of Zhetysu region, Manichaeism in the Chuy and Talas valleys and in Qocho city and Luoyong, Nestorian Christianity also in Qocho city, around Xinjiang and in Chang’an, and Islam in Burana.The massive scale of the trading activities fostered large, prosperous and thriving towns and cities that also reflect the interface between settled and nomadic communities in a variety of ways: the mutual inter-dependence of nomads and farmers and different peoples such as between Turks and Sogdians in the Zhetysu region; the transformation of nomadic communities to settled communities in the Tian-shan mountains, resulting in highly distinctive construction and planning such as semi-underground buildings; and in the Hosi corridor the planned agricultural expansion of the 1,000 mile corridor after the 1st century BC as an agricultural garrison and its transformation to settled agricultural communities. Diverse and large scale water management systems were essential to facilitate the growth of towns, trading settlements, forts, and caravanserai and the agriculture necessary to support them, such as the extensive Karez underground water channels of the extremely arid Turpan basin, many still in use, that supplied water to Qocho city, and were supplemented by deep wells inside Yar city;  the grand scale of the network of open canals and ditches along the Hosi corridor that drew river water to the settlements, 90 km of which survive around Suoyang city; and in the Zhetsyu region, river water  distribution through canals and pipes and collection in reservoirs.As well as conduits for goods and people, the routes allowed the exceptional flow of ideas, beliefs and technological innovations such as those related to architecture and town planning that shaped the urban spaces and peoples’ lives in many fundamental ways.

City.cn: 内蒙古自治区锡林郭勒盟
City.en: Xilin Gol League, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region

History_background.cn: 曾为忽必烈汗都城和元朝夏都
History_background.en: It was once the capital of Kublai Khan and the summer capital of the Yuan Dynasty.

Main_function.cn: 元朝都城和文化交流中心
Main_function.en: Yuan Dynasty capital and cultural exchange center

BUilding_use.cn: 宫殿、皇城、皇家狩猎场等
BUilding_use.en: Palaces, imperial city, royal hunting grounds, etc.

Brief_intro.cn: 见证了北亚游牧与农业文明的融合，是元朝都城和藏传佛教传播地，城市规划独具特色，享有盛名。
Brief_intro.en: A witness to the fusion of nomadic and agricultural civilizations in northern Asia, the Site of Xanadu served as the summer capital of the Yuan dynasty and a center for the spread of Tibetan Buddhism, distinguished by its unique and celebrated urban planning.

Standard.cn: 上都遗址的地理位置和环境体现了蒙古族和汉族价值观及生活方式的双重影响。该遗址的城市规划模式体现了两个民族的融合。元朝正是凭借蒙古族和汉族思想及制度的融合，才得以将其统治范围扩展到当时已知世界的极大区域。上都遗址是不同民族社群融合的城市规划的独特典范。
Standard.en: The geographical location and environment of the Shangdu site reflect the dual influence of Mongol and Han Chinese values and lifestyles. The site's urban planning model embodies the fusion of these two ethnic groups. It was precisely through the integration of Mongol and Han Chinese thought and systems that the Yuan Dynasty was able to expand its rule to the vastest areas of the known world at that time. The Shangdu site is a unique example of urban planning that integrates different ethnic communities.

Standard.cn: 上都遗址是元朝征服者忽必烈汗至高统治、被征服者文化和政治制度的同化和转变，以及征服者坚持和维护原有文化传统的决心和努力的杰出见证。
Standard.en: The Shangdu site is an outstanding testament to the supreme rule of Kublai Khan, the conqueror of the Yuan Dynasty, the assimilation and transformation of the conquered people's culture and political system, and the conqueror's determination and efforts to uphold and maintain the original cultural traditions.

Standard.cn: 上都遗址的选址和环境，以及其城市格局，体现了游牧文化与农业文化的共存与融合。上都将汉代城市规划与元代蒙古族生活方式所需的园林景观相结合，造就了杰出的城市布局范例，展现了人类历史上的一个重要阶段。
Standard.en: The site selection and environment of Shangdu, as well as its urban layout, reflect the coexistence and integration of nomadic and agricultural cultures. Shangdu combined Han Dynasty urban planning with the garden landscape required for the lifestyle of the Yuan Dynasty Mongols, creating an outstanding example of urban layout and showcasing an important stage in human history.

Standard.cn: 13 世纪，上都城举办了佛教与道教之间的大辩论，这一事件导致了藏传佛教在东北亚的传播。
Standard.en: In the 13th century, a great debate between Buddhism and Taoism was held in Shangdu, an event that led to the spread of Tibetan Buddhism in Northeast Asia.

Description.cn: 上都遗址是一座典型的草原都城，体现了文化融合的特色，见证了北亚游牧文明与农业文明之间的冲突与相互融合。它位于蒙古高原东南边缘，曾是忽必烈汗的第一个都城（1263-1273年），后又成为元朝的夏都（1274-1364年）。城址及相关陵墓群坐落于草原之上，其南北走向符合中国传统风水原则，北倚群山，南临河流。从上都出发，忽必烈汗的骑兵统一了中国的农业文明，并在一定程度上吸收了后者的文化，同时将元朝帝国的版图扩张至整个北亚。上都的城市规划，包括宫殿和皇城，部分被外城环绕，外城内保留着游牧民族营地和皇家狩猎场的遗迹，是这种文化融合的独特例证。铁番干运河的遗迹，便是当年为保护城市而修建的大型水利工程的见证。上都不仅是忽必烈汗崛起之地，也是他举行宗教辩论、接待外国旅行者的地方，这些旅行者的著作在后世留下了深刻的印记。上都因此在世界范围内享有盛名，也是藏传佛教传播的发源地。
Description.en: The Site of Xanadu is the site of a grassland capital characteristic of cultural fusion, witnessing clashes and mutual assimilation between the nomadic and agrarian civilisations in northern Asia. Located on the southeast edge of the Mongolian plateau, it was the first capital (1263-1273) of Kublai Khan and later the summer capital (1274-1364) of the Yuan Dynasty. The city site and associated tombs are located on the grassland steppe with a north south axis determined by traditional Chinese feng shui principles, backed by mountains to the north and a river to the south.From Xanadu, the mounted warriors of Kublai Khan unified the agrarian civilisations of China, and partly assimilated to the latter’s culture, while extending the Yuan empire right across North Asia. The plan of Xanadu, with Palace and Imperial cities enclosed partly by the Outer City containing evidence of the nomadic encampments and royal hunting enclosure, comprises a unique example of this cultural fusion. Evidence of large water control works instigated to protect the city exists in the form of remains of the Tiefan’gan Canal. As the place where Kublai Khan rose to power, hosted religious debates and entertained foreign travellers whose writings gave inspiration down the centuries, it has achieved legendary status in the rest of the world and is the place from where Tibetan Buddhism expanded.

Name.en: Summer Palace, an Imperial Garden in Beijing

History_background.cn: 始建于清乾隆年间，后多次修复
History_background.en: Originally built during the reign of Emperor Qianlong of the Qing Dynasty, it has been repaired several times since.

Main_function.cn: 皇家园林与休闲场所
Main_function.en: Royal gardens and leisure areas

BUilding_use.en: Royal residence, political affairs and entertainment

Brief_intro.cn: 是中国园林设计艺术的杰出代表，融合政治、居住、娱乐等功能，现为著名公共公园，园内有众多古建筑和自然景观。
Brief_intro.en: An outstanding example of Chinese landscape garden design, the Summer Palace integrates political, residential, and recreational functions and today serves as a renowned public park, home to numerous historic buildings and natural scenery.

Standard.cn: 北京颐和园是中国园林设计艺术的杰出代表，将人类的杰作与自然融为一体。
Standard.en: The Summer Palace in Beijing is an outstanding representative of Chinese garden design art, integrating human masterpieces with nature.

Standard.cn: 颐和园体现了中国园林设计的理念和实践，对整个东方这种文化形式的发展起到了关键作用
Standard.en: The Summer Palace embodies the concepts and practices of Chinese garden design and has played a key role in the development of this cultural form throughout the East.

Standard.cn: 以颐和园为代表的中国皇家园林是世界主要文明之一的有力象征。
Standard.en: Chinese imperial gardens, exemplified by the Summer Palace, are a powerful symbol of one of the world's major civilizations.

Description.cn: 北京颐和园由众多传统殿堂亭台楼阁组成，其前身是清朝乾隆皇帝于1750年至1764年间构想的“清澈涟漪园”。颐和园以昆明湖（元朝都城昆明的蓄水池）和万寿山为基本框架，将政治行政、居住、精神生活和休闲娱乐等功能融于湖光山色之中，体现了中国“人与自然和谐共生”的哲学理念。颐和园在19世纪50年代的第二次鸦片战争中遭到破坏，后由光绪皇帝重建，供慈禧太后使用，并更名为颐和园。1900年义和团运动期间，颐和园再次遭到破坏，后经修复，并于1924年成为一座公共公园。行政区的核心建筑——仁寿殿，可通过雄伟的东宫门进入。相连的住宅区由三座建筑群组成：长寿幸福殿、玉涟和绫云，均依长寿山而建，可俯瞰湖泊美景。这些建筑群通过有顶走廊相连，东侧连接大舞台，西侧连接长廊。长寿幸福殿前设有木制码头，供皇室成员水路前往住所。昆明园其余90%的面积用于观景和冥想，园内点缀着佛香塔、转卷阁、五方阁、宝云铜阁和辟云殿等园林建筑。昆明湖中有三个大岛，对应着中国传统山水园林的象征元素，其中南岛通过十七拱桥与东堤相连。西堤是昆明园的一大特色，沿堤建有六座风格各异的桥梁。其他重要景观还包括位于长寿山北侧的汉藏式寺庙和修道院，以及东北侧的和悦园
Description.en: The Summer Palace in Beijing integrates numerous traditional halls and pavilions into the Imperial Garden conceived by the Qing emperor Qianlong between 1750 and 1764 as the Garden of Clear Ripples. Using Kunming Lake, the former reservoir of the Yuan dynasty’s capital and Longevity Hill as the basic framework, the Summer Palace combined political and administrative, residential, spiritual, and recreational functions within a landscape of lakes and mountains, in accordance with the Chinese philosophy of balancing the works of man with nature. Destroyed during the Second Opium War of the 1850s, it was reconstructed by Emperor Guangxu for use by Empress Dowager Cixi and renamed the Summer Palace. Although damaged again during the Boxer Rebellion in 1900 it was restored and has been a public park since 1924. The central feature of the Administrative area, the Hall of Benevolence and Longevity is approached through the monumental East Palace Gate. The connecting Residential area comprises three building complexes: the Halls of Happiness in Longevity, Jade Ripples and Yiyun, all built up against the Hill of Longevity, with fine views over the lake. These are linked by roofed corridors which connect to the Great Stage to the east and the Long Corridor to the West. In front of the Hall of Happiness in Longevity a wooden quay gave access by water for the Imperial family to their quarters.The remaining 90% of the garden provides areas for enjoying views and spiritual contemplation and is embellished with garden buildings including the Tower of the Fragrance of Buddha, the Tower of the Revolving Archive, Wu Fang Pavilion, the Baoyun Bronze Pavilion, and the Hall that Dispels the Clouds. Kunming Lake contains three large islands, corresponding to the traditional Chinese symbolic mountain garden element, the southern of which is linked to the East Dike by the Seventeen Arch Bridge. An essential feature is the West Dike with six bridges in different styles along its length. Other important features include temples and monasteries in Han and Tibetan style located on the north side of the Hill of Longevity and the Garden of Harmonious Pleasure to the north-east.As the culmination of several hundred years of Imperial garden design, the Summer Palace has had a major influence on subsequent oriental garden art and culture.

Name.en: Temple and Cemetery of Confucius and the Kong Family Mansion in Qufu

Dynast.cn: 周朝(公元前1046年 - 公元前256年)

History_background.cn: 始建于公元前478年，纪念孔子
History_background.en: It was first built in 478 BC to commemorate Confucius.

Main_function.cn: 纪念孔子并向他献祭
Main_function.en: Commemorating Confucius and offering sacrifices to him

BUilding_use.cn: 孔庙为祭祀场所，孔府为后裔居住
BUilding_use.en: The Temple of Confucius is a place for worship, while the Confucius Mansion is where his descendants reside.

Brief_intro.cn: 主要目的是纪念孔子，拥有丰富的历史文物和珍贵档案，是东方建筑和文化遗产的代表。
Brief_intro.en: Dedicated primarily to the commemoration of Confucius, this complex houses a wealth of historical artifacts and precious archives, and is a representative example of Eastern architectural and cultural heritage.

Standard.cn: 曲阜的纪念性建筑群具有杰出的艺术价值，因为两千多年来中国皇帝都给予了它们支持，确保了最优秀的艺术家和工匠参与了献给孔子的建筑和景观的建造和重建。
Standard.en: The monumental architectural complex in Qufu has outstanding artistic value because it has been supported by Chinese emperors for over two thousand years, ensuring that the finest artists and craftsmen participated in the construction and reconstruction of the buildings and landscapes dedicated to Confucius.

Standard.cn: 曲阜建筑群是一个杰出的建筑群，它展现了中国物质文化在相当长一段时间内的演变。
Standard.en: The Qufu architectural complex is an outstanding architectural complex that showcases the evolution of Chinese material culture over a considerable period of time.

Standard.cn: 孔子对东方国家两千年来以及18、19世纪欧洲和西方的哲学和政治学说的贡献，是现代思想和政府发展演变中最深刻的因素之一。
Standard.en: Confucius's contributions to the philosophy and political thought of Eastern countries over the past two thousand years, as well as to Europe and the West in the 18th and 19th centuries, are among the most profound factors in the development and evolution of modern thought and government.

Description.cn: 孔子是中国古代著名的哲学家、政治家和教育家，他所创立的涵盖哲学、政治和伦理的信仰体系（后世称为儒家思想）对中国文化产生了深远的影响。他被中国历代皇帝尊为“万代圣师”。孔庙位于孔子的出生地——中国山东省曲阜市，始建于公元前478年，旨在纪念孔子并向他献祭。历经数个世纪的损毁和重建，如今的孔庙占地14公顷，拥有104座从晋代到清代的建筑，包括大成殿、奎文阁和星坛等，以及1250余棵古树。寺内藏有不同时期制作的一千余块碑刻，以及汉代石刻浮雕、描绘孔子生平的雕刻画、明清石龙等珍贵文物。该寺在布局和风格上，堪称东亚和东南亚各国众多孔庙的典范。孔子墓位于曲阜市北面1100米处，占地183公顷，内有孔子的陵墓以及其后裔的10万多座坟墓。孔家府位于孔庙东侧，最初是与孔庙相连的一处小型民居，后来发展成为孔子男性直系后裔居住和工作的贵族府邸。14世纪，孔庙毁于火灾后，按照皇家宫殿的样式重建，并筑起围墙。孔家府也在距离孔庙不远的地方重建。此后，府邸不断扩建，后又毁于火灾，于19世纪末重建。如今，府邸占地7公顷，共有约170座建筑。府内收藏超过10万件文物，其中最著名的包括商周时期的十件礼器、不同时期孔子的画像以及明清时期的服饰和帽子。此外，府内收藏的明清两代6万余份文件和档案，不仅为府内400多年来的各种活动提供了可靠的记录，而且对于研究明清历史具有很高的价值。这些建筑的设计和建造都严格遵循儒家关于各部分等级布局的理念。明代许多杰出的艺术家和工匠参与了寺庙的装饰，而清代则委派皇家工匠建造了大成殿、大成门和秦殿，这两座建筑被认为是清代艺术和建筑的巅峰之作。儒家思想不仅在中国，而且在朝鲜、日本和越南的封建社会也产生了深远的影响，并对18世纪欧洲的启蒙运动产生了积极的影响。孔庙、孔子墓和孔家宅邸不仅是东方建筑技艺的杰出代表，而且具有深厚的历史内涵，是人类文化遗产的重要组成部分。
Description.en: Confucius, a renowned philosopher, politician and educator in ancient China whose system of belief involving philosophy, politics and ethics (subsequently known as Confucianism) has exerted profound influence on Chinese culture, was revered as the Sacred Model Teacher for Ten Thousand Generations by Chinese emperors. Located in his birthplace, Qufu City of Shandong Province, China, the Temple of Confucius was built to commemorate and offer sacrifices to Confucius in 478 BC. Having been destroyed and reconstructed over the centuries, it now covers 14 hectares, with 104 buildings dating from the Jin to Qing dynasties including the Dacheng Hall, Kuiwen Pavilion and Xing Altar, and over 1,250 ancient trees. The Temple houses more than 1,000 stelae made at different times, and precious objects such as Han stone reliefs, carved pictures depicting the life of Confucius, and the stone dragon carvings of the Ming and Qing dynasties. The Temple is the prototype and model for all the Confucius temples widely distributed in countries in East Asia and Southeast Asia, particularly in terms of layout and style.Located 1,100 meters to the north of Qufu City, the Cemetery of Confucius covers an area of 183 hectares. It contains Confucius’ tomb and more than 100,000 graves of his descendants.Lying to the east of the Temple, the Kong Family Mansion developed from a small family house linked to the temple into an aristocratic mansion in which the male direct descendants of Confucius lived and worked.Following a fire and rebuilding of the temple with an enclosure wall on the model of an imperial palace in the 14th century, the mansion was rebuilt a short distance from the temple. Subsequently expanded, then destroyed again by fire and rebuilt in the late 19th century, it now covers 7 hectares with a total of some 170 buildings. Over 100,000 collections are kept in the Mansion; among them the ten ceremonial utensils of the Shang and Zhou dynasties, the portraits of Confucius made in different periods and clothes and caps dating to the Ming and Qing dynasties are the most famous. Furthermore, the more than 60,000 files and archives of the Ming and Qing dynasties collected in the Mansion not only provide a credible record of all kinds of activities in the Mansion for more than 400 years, but are highly valuable for studying the history of the Ming and Qing period.The buildings were designed and built with meticulous care according to the ideas of Confucianism regarding the hierarchy of disposition of the various components. In the Ming period many outstanding artists and craftsmen applied their skills in the adornment of the temple, and in the Qing period imperial craftsmen were assigned to build the Dacheng Hall and Gate and the Qin Hall, considered to represent the pinnacle of Qing art and architecture.Confucianism has exerted a profound influence not only in China but also on the feudal societies of Korea, Japan and Vietnam and had a positive influence on the Enlightenment of 18th century Europe. The Temple of Confucius, the Cemetery of Confucius, and the Kong Family Mansion are not only outstanding representatives of oriental architectural skills, but they also have a deep historical content and are an important part of the cultural heritage of mankind.

Name.en: Temple of Heaven: an Imperial Sacrificial Altar in Beijing

History_background.cn: 明永乐十八年建成，嘉靖年间改为天坛
History_background.en: Built in the 18th year of the Yongle reign of the Ming Dynasty, it was converted into the Temple of Heaven during the Jiajing reign.

Main_function.cn: 皇家祭天祈福场所
Main_function.en: Royal site for offering sacrifices and prayers

BUilding_use.cn: 供皇帝祭天、斋戒、管理祭祀
BUilding_use.en: Used by the emperor for offering sacrifices to Heaven, fasting, and managing sacrificial rites.

Brief_intro.cn: 现存最完整、世界最大规模的皇家祭祀建筑群，明清皇帝在此祭天祈福，建筑布局独特，融合古代天人思想，历史悠久，文化价值极高。
Brief_intro.en: The most complete and largest surviving royal sacrificial complex in the world, the Temple of Heaven served as the site where Ming and Qing emperors offered sacrifices to heaven and prayed for good harvests. Its unique architectural layout embodies the ancient concept of the unity of heaven and humanity.

Standard.cn: 天坛是建筑和景观设计的杰作，它以简洁而形象的方式阐释了宇宙起源，这对世界伟大文明之一的演进具有重要意义。
Standard.en: The Temple of Heaven is a masterpiece of architecture and landscape design. It interprets the origin of the universe in a simple and vivid way, which is of great significance to the evolution of one of the world's great civilizations.

Standard.cn: 天坛的象征性布局和设计对远东地区的建筑和规划产生了深远的影响，这种影响持续了数个世纪。
Standard.en: The symbolic layout and design of the Temple of Heaven had a profound influence on architecture and planning in the Far East that lasted for centuries.

Standard.cn: 两千多年来，中国一直由一系列封建王朝统治，天坛的设计和布局象征着这些王朝的合法性。
Standard.en: For more than two thousand years, China has been ruled by a series of feudal dynasties, and the design and layout of the Temple of Heaven symbolizes the legitimacy of these dynasties.

Description.cn: 天坛呈轴线式布局，南侧为圆形土丘祭坛，敞开于天际；北侧紧邻圆顶天坛，穹顶呈锥形。天坛通过一条高架圣道与更北侧的三层圆顶祈年殿相连。明清两代的皇帝在此作为人间与天界的沟通桥梁，向天庭献祭，祈求五谷丰登。西侧是斋殿，皇帝献祭后在此斋戒。整个建筑群被双层围墙环绕，四周遍植松树。西侧内外围墙之间是神乐管理殿和祭祀牲畜的马厩。整个建筑群共有92座古建筑，600间房间。它是中国现存最完整的皇家祭祀建筑群，也是世界上现存最大的祭祀建筑群。天地坛位于紫禁城南侧，永内大街东侧，原先与紫禁城同时建成于明永乐十八年（1420年）。嘉靖九年（1530年），决定分别祭祀天地，因此在正殿南侧修建了圆丘坛，专门用于祭祀天。嘉靖十三年（1534年），天地坛更名为天坛。如今占地273公顷的天坛建筑群，是清乾隆和光绪皇帝于1749年重建后形成的。天坛的选址、规划和建筑设计，以及祭祀仪式和相关音乐，都基于古代将数字和空间布局与天界信仰及其与人间关系联系起来的教义，而皇帝作为“天子”则代表着这种信仰。其他朝代也曾建造祭坛来祭祀天界，但北京的天坛是古代中国文化的杰作，也是中国众多祭祀建筑中最具代表性的作品。
Description.en: The Temple of Heaven is an axial arrangement of Circular Mound Altar to the south open to the sky with the conically roofed Imperial Vault of Heaven immediately to its north. This is linked by a raised sacred way to the circular, three-tiered, conically roofed Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests further to the north. Here at these places the emperors of the Ming and Qing dynasties as interlocutors between humankind and the celestial realm offered sacrifice to heaven and prayed for bumper harvests. To the west is the Hall of Abstinence where the emperor fasted after making sacrifice. The whole is surrounded by a double-walled, pine-treed enclosure. Between the inner and outer walls to the west are the Divine Music Administration hall and the building that was the Stables for Sacrificial Animals. Within the complex there are a total of 92 ancient buildings with 600 rooms. It is the most complete existing imperial sacrificial building complex in China and the world's largest existing building complex for offering sacrifice to heaven.Located south of the Forbidden City on the east side of Yongnei Dajie, the original Altar of Heaven and Earth was completed together with the Forbidden City in 1420, the eighteenth year of the reign of the Ming Emperor Yongle. In the ninth year of the reign of Emperor Jiajing (1530) the decision was taken to offer separate sacrifices to heaven and earth, and so the Circular Mound Altar was built to the south of the main hall for sacrifices particularly to heaven. The Altar of Heaven and Earth was thereby renamed the Temple of Heaven in the thirteenth year of the reign of Emperor Jiajing (1534). The current arrangement of the Temple of Heaven complex covering 273ha was formed by 1749 after reconstruction by the Qing emperors Qianlong and Guangxu.The siting, planning, and architectural design of the Temple of Heaven as well as the sacrificial ceremony and associated music were based on ancient tenets relating numbers and spatial organisation to beliefs about heaven and its relationship to people on earth, mediated by the emperor as the ‘Son of Heaven’. Other dynasties built altars for the worship of heaven but the Temple of Heaven in Beijing is a masterpiece of ancient Chinese culture and is the most representative work of numerous sacrificial buildings in China.

History_background.cn: 始建于公元前5世纪，隋朝统一修建
History_background.en: Originally built in the 5th century BC, it was unified and constructed during the Sui Dynasty.

Main_function.cn: 帝国内陆交通与物资运输
Main_function.en: Imperial Inland Transportation and Material Transport

BUilding_use.en: Inland waterway shipping and grain transport

Brief_intro.cn: 是世界最大古代土木工程，连接南北，保障经济繁荣与国家统一。
Brief_intro.en: The largest ancient civil engineering project in the world, the Grand Canal connects north and south China and has long served to underpin economic prosperity and national unity.

Standard.cn: 大运河是人类历史上最伟大的水利工程杰作，其历史悠久，规模宏大，历经岁月洗礼不断发展演变，并不断适应环境变化。它充分展现了人类的智慧、决心和勇气。大运河是人类创造力的杰出典范，体现了源自古代中国的庞大农业帝国在技术能力和水文方面的造诣。
Standard.en: The Grand Canal is one of the greatest hydraulic engineering masterpieces in human history. With a long history and grand scale, it has continuously evolved and adapted to environmental changes over time. It fully demonstrates human wisdom, determination, and courage. The Grand Canal is an outstanding example of human creativity, reflecting the technological capabilities and hydrological expertise of the vast agricultural empire originating from ancient China.

Standard.cn: 大运河见证了草运体系独特的运河管理文化传统，包括其起源、兴盛、对历代朝代及其都城的适应，以及最终在20世纪的消亡。它构成了帝国对粮食、盐和铁的运输和储存的垄断，以及一套税收体系。它促进了农民经济、皇室以及民众和军队粮食供应之间的根本联系。它历来是中华帝国稳定的因素。大运河沿线的经济和城市发展见证了伟大农业文明的核心运作，以及水路网络发展在其中发挥的决定性作用。
Standard.en: The Grand Canal bears witness to the unique canal management culture of the grassland transport system, including its origins, prosperity, adaptation to successive dynasties and their capitals, and its eventual demise in the 20th century. It constituted the empire's monopoly on the transport and storage of grain, salt, and iron, as well as a tax system. It fostered fundamental links between the peasant economy, the imperial court, and the food supply for the people and the army. It was historically a factor in the stability of the Chinese empire. The economic and urban development along the Grand Canal testifies to the core operations of a great agricultural civilization and the decisive role played in the development of waterway networks.

Standard.cn: 大运河是世界上最长、最古老的运河。它见证了水利工程早期卓越的发展。它是工业革命前一项重要的技术成就。大运河在应对复杂的自然条件方面堪称典范，其众多建筑都充分适应了各种复杂多样的环境。它充分展现了东方文明的技术能力。大运河包含了重要的、创新的、尤其是早期的水利技术实例。它还体现了建造堤坝、堰和桥梁方面的特殊技艺，以及对石材、夯土等材料的独创性和精湛运用，以及对粘土和稻草等混合材料的巧妙运用。
Standard.en: The Grand Canal is the world's longest and oldest canal. It bears witness to the remarkable development of early hydraulic engineering and represents a significant technological achievement before the Industrial Revolution. The Grand Canal is exemplary in its ability to cope with complex natural conditions, with many of its structures perfectly adapted to diverse environments. It fully demonstrates the technological capabilities of Eastern civilization. The Grand Canal contains important, innovative, and especially early examples of hydraulic engineering. It also embodies special skills in constructing dams, weirs, and bridges, as well as the originality and exquisite use of materials such as stone and rammed earth, and the ingenious application of mixtures such as clay and straw.

Description.cn: 京杭大运河在中国东北和中东部平原形成了一个庞大的内河水系，贯穿中国现今的八个省份。它北起首都北京，南至浙江省。大运河始建于公元前5世纪，分段修建，并于公元7世纪隋朝首次被构想为帝国统一的交通要道。这催生了一系列规模宏大的工程，使其成为工业革命前世界上规模最大、范围最广的土木工程项目。历代朝代不断完善和维护，京杭大运河成为帝国内陆交通系统的骨干。长期以来，曹运制度确保了运河的高效管理。曹运是帝国垄断粮食和战略物资运输、征税和交通管制的机构。该制度保障了粮食供应，满足了民众的粮食需求，实现了领土的统一管理，并便于军队的调动。大运河在13世纪（元朝）达到鼎盛时期，形成了一个由2000多公里人工水道组成的统一内河航运网络，连接了包括黄河和长江在内的中国五大流域。时至今日，它仍然是重要的国内交通要道，在漫长的历史中为保障中国的经济繁荣与稳定发挥了重要作用。
Description.en: The Grand Canal forms a vast inland waterway system in the north-eastern and central eastern plains of China, passing through eight of the country’s present-day provinces. It runs from the capital Beijing in the north to Zhejiang Province in the south. Constructed in sections from the 5th century BC onwards, it was conceived as a unified means of communication for the Empire for the first time in the 7th century AD (Sui Dynasty). This led to a series of gigantic worksites, creating the world’s largest and most extensive civil engineering project ensemble prior to the Industrial Revolution. Completed and maintained by successive dynasties, it formed the backbone of the Empire’s inland communications system. Its management was made possible over a long period by means of the Caoyun system, the imperial monopoly for the transport of grain and strategic raw materials, and for the taxation and control of traffic. The system enabled the supply of rice to feed the population, the unified administration of the territory, and the transport of troops.
