The Grand Canal reached a new peak in the 13th century (Yuan Dynasty), providing a unified inland navigation network consisting of more than 2,000 km of artificial waterways, linking five of the most important river basins in China, including the Yellow River and the Yangtze. Still a major means of internal communication today, it has played an important role in ensuring the economic prosperity and stability of China over the ages.

Dynast.cn: 秦朝(公元前221年 - 公元前206年)

History_background.cn: 自公元前3世纪起建设的防御工程
History_background.en: Defensive works built since the 3rd century BC

Main_function.cn: 军事防御与保护边境安全
Main_function.en: Military defense and border security

BUilding_use.cn: 抵御外敌入侵，传递军事信息
BUilding_use.en: Resisting foreign invasion and transmitting military information

Brief_intro.cn: 中国北部边境历代王朝修建的伟大军事防御工程，东起山海关，西至嘉峪关，全长逾两万公里，是中国古代卓越军事建筑的代表。
Brief_intro.en: A great military defensive structure built across successive dynasties along China's northern frontier, the Great Wall stretches over 20,000 kilometers from Shanhaiguan in the east to Jiayuguan in the west, and is the preeminent symbol of China's ancient military architecture.

Standard.cn: 明长城不仅工程规模宏大，而且建造工艺精湛，堪称绝对的杰作。它是地球上唯一一座从月球上都能看到的由人类建造的建筑，在广袤的大陆尺度上，完美地诠释了建筑与自然景观的和谐统一。
Standard.en: The Ming Great Wall is not only a massive engineering project but also a masterpiece of exquisite craftsmanship. It is the only man-made structure on Earth that can be seen from the moon, perfectly embodying the harmonious unity of architecture and natural landscape on a vast continental scale.

Standard.cn: 春秋时期，中国人将自身的建筑模式和空间组织方式应用于北部边境防御工事的建设。长城修建所引发的人口迁移，进一步加剧了汉文化的传播。
Standard.en: During the Spring and Autumn Period, the Chinese applied their architectural styles and spatial organization methods to the construction of defensive fortifications along the northern border. The population migration triggered by the construction of the Great Wall further accelerated the spread of Han culture.

Standard.cn: 长城作为古代中国文明的杰出见证，不仅体现在甘肃省保存完好的西汉夯土防御工事中，也体现在明代令人赞叹、举世闻名的石砌建筑中。
Standard.en: The Great Wall, as an outstanding testament to ancient Chinese civilization, is not only reflected in the well-preserved rammed earth defensive works of the Western Han Dynasty in Gansu Province, but also in the admirable and world-renowned stone architecture of the Ming Dynasty.

Standard.cn: 这座复杂且历时性的文化遗产是一个杰出而独特的军事建筑群范例，它在 2000 年的时间里服务于单一的战略目的，但其建造历史体现了防御技术的不断进步以及对不断变化的政治环境的适应。
Standard.en: This complex and historically significant cultural heritage is an outstanding and unique example of a military architectural complex that served a single strategic purpose for 2,000 years, but whose construction history reflects the continuous advancement of defensive technology and adaptation to an ever-changing political environment.

Standard.cn: 长城在中国历史上具有无可比拟的象征意义。它的目的不仅在于保护中国免受外敌侵略，也在于保护中国文化免受外来蛮夷风俗的侵蚀。由于长城的修建饱含苦难，因此它成为中国文学中的重要典范，例如陈麟（约公元200年）的《兵士辞》、杜甫（712-770年）的诗歌以及明代通俗小说中都有关于长城的记载。
Standard.en: The Great Wall holds unparalleled symbolic significance in Chinese history. Its purpose was not only to protect China from foreign invasion but also to safeguard Chinese culture from the erosion of barbarian customs. Because the construction of the Great Wall was fraught with hardship, it became an important model in Chinese literature, with accounts of it found in works such as Chen Lin's (c. 200 AD) "Soldier's Ode," Du Fu's (712-770 AD) poems, and popular novels of the Ming Dynasty.

Description.cn: 长城是中国历代王朝自公元前3世纪至公元17世纪在北部边境不断修建的伟大军事防御工程，总长度超过2万公里。长城东起河北省山海关，西至甘肃省嘉峪关。其主体由城墙、马道、烽火台、棚屋等组成，沿途还建有要塞和关隘。长城反映了古代中国农业文明与游牧文明之间的碰撞与交流。它为古代中国中央王朝高瞻远瞩的政治战略思维和强大的军事防御力量提供了重要的实物证据，也是古代中国卓越军事建筑、技术和艺术的杰出代表。作为维护国家和人民安全的象征，长城具有无可比拟的意义。
Description.en: The Great Wall was continuously built from the 3rd century BC to the 17th century AD on the northern border of the country as the great military defence project of successive Chinese Empires, with a total length of more than 20,000 kilometers. The Great Wall begins in the east at Shanhaiguan in Hebei province and ends at Jiayuguan in Gansu province to the west. Its main body consists of walls, horse tracks, watch towers, and shelters on the wall, and includes fortresses and passes along the Wall.The Great Wall reflects collision and exchanges between agricultural civilizations and nomadic civilizations in ancient China. It provides significant physical evidence of the far-sighted political strategic thinking and mighty military and national defence forces of central empires in ancient China, and is an outstanding example of the superb military architecture, technology and art of ancient China. It embodies unparalleled significance as the national symbol for safeguarding the security of the country and its people.

History_background.cn: 13世纪起的土司世袭统治遗迹
History_background.en: Remains of Tusi hereditary rule from the 13th century onwards

Main_function.cn: 展示土司治理体系和民族融合
Main_function.en: Showcasing the Tusi governance system and ethnic integration

BUilding_use.cn: 行政管理、居住和防御用途

Brief_intro.cn: 多处遗址共同展现了13至20世纪初中国西南地区土司制度下的行政管理、民族融合和文化特色。
Brief_intro.en: These sites collectively illustrate the administrative governance, ethnic integration, and cultural characteristics of the Tusi chieftain system in southwestern China from the 13th century to the early 20th century.

Standard.cn: 老寺城、唐雅和海龙屯堡垒的土司遗址清楚地展现了中国西南地区地方民族文化与通过中央政府结构表达的国家认同之间的人文价值观的交流。
Standard.en: The Tusi sites of Laosicheng, Tangya, and Hailongtun clearly demonstrate the exchange of humanistic values between the local ethnic cultures of Southwest China and the national identity expressed through the structure of the central government.

Standard.cn: 老寺城、唐雅和海龙屯遗址是中国西南地区土司政权的证明，因此对这种源于中国早期少数民族行政制度的政权形式，以及元、明、清时期的中华文明，具有特殊的见证意义。
Standard.en: The Laosicheng, Tangya, and Hailongtun sites are evidence of the Tusi regime in southwestern China, and therefore have special significance in witnessing this form of regime that originated from the early administrative system of ethnic minorities in China, as well as the Chinese civilization during the Yuan, Ming, and Qing dynasties.

Description.cn: 在中国西南山区，散布着一些部落领地的遗迹。这些领地的首领由中央政府任命为“土司”，自13世纪至20世纪初，土司世袭统治着各自的领地。这种行政管理体系旨在统一国家行政，同时又允许少数民族保留其习俗和生活方式。老寺城、唐崖和海龙屯三处遗址构成一个系列，共同展现了这一治理体系。老寺城土司领地和海龙屯的考古遗址及现存遗迹代表了最高等级土司的领地；唐崖土司领地的牌坊、行政区遗址、围墙、沟渠和墓葬则代表了较低等级土司的领地。这些遗址融合了地方民族特色和中央汉族文化特征，体现了价值观的交融，也反映了中国古代的行政管理方式，同时又保留了与少数民族文化传统的联系，例如老寺城土家族社区的文化传统和习俗。
Description.en: Distributed around the mountainous areas of south-west China are the remains of tribal domains whose leaders were appointed by the central government as ‘Tusi’, hereditary rulers of their regions from the 13th to the early 20th century. This system of administrative government was aimed at unifying national administration while simultaneously allowing ethnic minorities to retain their customs and way of life. The three sites of Laosicheng, Tangya and the Hailongtun Fortress combine as a serial property to represent this system of governance. The archaeological sites and standing remains of Laosicheng Tusi Domain and Hailongtun Fortress represent domains of highest ranking Tusi; the Memorial Archway and remains of the Administration Area, boundary walls, drainage ditches and tombs at Tangya Tusi Domain represent the domain of a lower ranked Tusi. Their combinations of local ethnic and central Chinese features exhibit an interchange of values and testify to imperial Chinese administrative methods, while retaining their association with the living cultural traditions of the ethnic minority groups represented by the cultural traditions and practices of the Tujia communities at Laosicheng.

Name.en: West Lake Cultural Landscape of Hangzhou

History_background.cn: 自唐代以来为文人墨客所赞颂
History_background.en: It has been praised by literati since the Tang Dynasty.

Main_function.cn: 展现人与自然和谐统一的文化景观
Main_function.en: Cultural landscape showcasing harmony between humanity and nature

Brief_intro.cn: 湖中有岛屿、堤道、寺庙、宝塔等，体现中国山水美学理念，对园林设计有深远影响，是人与自然和谐统一的代表。
Brief_intro.en: With its islands, causeways, temples, and pagodas, West Lake embodies Chinese aesthetic ideals of landscape beauty, has exerted a profound influence on garden design, and stands as a symbol of the harmonious unity between humanity and nature.

Standard.cn: 西湖景观的改善体现了从印度传入中国的佛教理念，例如“佛教的宁静”和“自然如画”，进而对东亚的园林设计产生了重大影响。其堤岸、岛屿、桥梁、寺庙、宝塔以及清晰的景致被广泛效仿，尤其在北京颐和园和日本等地得到体现。十个诗意名胜的理念在中国流传了七个世纪，并在16世纪后随着朝鲜文人雅士游西湖而传播到朝鲜半岛。
Standard.en: The improvement of the West Lake landscape reflected Buddhist concepts introduced to China from India, such as "Buddhist tranquility" and "picturesque nature," which in turn had a significant influence on East Asian garden design. Its embankments, islands, bridges, temples, pagodas, and clear views were widely imitated, especially in places like the Summer Palace in Beijing and Japan. The concept of ten poetic scenic spots circulated in China for seven centuries and spread to the Korean Peninsula after the 16th century when Korean literati visited West Lake.

Standard.cn: 西湖景观是改善景观以创造一系列“画卷”的独特文化传统的杰出体现，这些“画卷”反映了人与自然完美融合的理念，这一传统在唐宋时期发展起来，并延续至今。经过“改造”的西湖，拥有众多人工堤道、岛屿、桥梁、花园、宝塔和寺庙，与周围郁郁葱葱的山峦交相辉映，堪称这一传统的杰出体现。
Standard.en: The West Lake landscape is an outstanding example of the unique cultural tradition of improving the landscape to create a series of "pictures" that reflect the concept of perfect harmony between man and nature. This tradition developed during the Tang and Song dynasties and continues to this day. The "renovated" West Lake boasts numerous artificial causeways, islands, bridges, gardens, pagodas, and temples, which complement the surrounding lush mountains, making it a prime example of this tradition.

Standard.cn: 唐宋时期，人们注重通过美化景观来展现人与自然的和谐，创造优美的自然景观，这种理念被艺术家捕捉、被诗人赋予名字。西湖山水便是这一理念的鲜明体现，其岛屿、堤道、寺庙、宝塔和观赏植物等景观元素均体现了这一理念。这一传统在西湖传承了七个世纪，并传播到中国各地、日本和韩国，成为具有重要意义的文化遗产。
Standard.en: During the Tang and Song dynasties, people emphasized showcasing the harmony between humanity and nature through landscape beautification, creating beautiful natural scenery. This concept was captured by artists and given names by poets. The landscape of West Lake is a vivid embodiment of this concept, with its islands, causeways, temples, pagodas, and ornamental plants all reflecting this idea. This tradition has been passed down in West Lake for seven centuries and spread to other parts of China, Japan, and Korea, becoming a significant cultural heritage.

Description.cn: 西湖三面环云，一面与杭州城接壤。自唐代（公元618-907年）以来，其美景便为文人墨客所赞颂。为了使其更加美丽，人们在湖中的岛屿、堤道以及山坡上增建了众多寺庙、宝塔、亭台楼阁、园林和观赏树木，与周围的农田景观融为一体。西湖的主要人工元素——两条堤道和三座岛屿——是在9至12世纪间通过反复疏浚而成的。自南宋（13世纪）以来，人们将十处诗意盎然的风景名胜认定为理想化的经典景观，它们完美地诠释了人与自然的和谐统一。西湖正是这一文化景观的杰出代表，它清晰地展现了唐宋时期文人墨客所阐述的中国山水美学理念。西湖的景观对中国乃至更远地区的园林设计产生了深远的影响，各地的湖泊堤岸纷纷效仿西湖的和谐与美丽。西湖的核心要素至今仍能激发人们“将情感投射于景观之上”的灵感。从杭州眺望，这座广袤的园林景观轮廓清晰，与周围山峦的脊线相接。
Description.en: West Lake is surrounded on three sides by 'cloud-capped hills' and on the fourth by the city of Hangzhou. Its beauty has been celebrated by writers and artists since the Tang Dynasty (AD 618-907). In order to make it more beautiful, its islands, causeways and the lower slopes of its hills have been 'improved' by the addition of numerous temples, pagodas, pavilions, gardens and ornamental trees which merge with farmed landscape. The main artificial elements of the lake, two causeways and three islands, were created from repeated dredgings between the 9th and 12th centuries. Since the Southern Song Dynasty (thirteenth century) ten poetically named scenic places have been identified as embodying idealised, classic landscapes - that manifest the perfect fusion between man and nature. West Lake is an outstanding example of a cultural landscape that display with great clarity the ideals of Chinese landscape aesthetics, as expounded by writers and scholars in Tang and Song Dynasties. The landscape of West Lake had a profound impact on the design of gardens not only in China but further afield, where lakes and causeways imitated the harmony and beauty of West Lake. The key components of West Lake still allow it to inspire people to 'project feelings onto the landscape'. The visual parameters of this vast landscape garden are clearly defined, rising to the ridges of the surrounding hills as viewed from Hangzhou.

Dynast.cn: 商朝(约公元前1600年 - 公元前1046年)

History_background.cn: 商朝潘庚迁都于此，历经255年
History_background.en: Pan Geng of the Shang Dynasty moved the capital here, a period that lasted 255 years.

Main_function.cn: 古都城遗址，展示商代文明
Main_function.en: Ancient capital city ruins showcase Shang Dynasty civilization

BUilding_use.cn: 宫殿、祠堂、陵墓、祭祀场所
BUilding_use.en: Palaces, ancestral halls, mausoleums, and sacrificial sites

Brief_intro.cn: 中国最早的都城遗址，包含宫殿、祠堂和陵墓区，出土甲骨文、青铜器等，是中国早期文明的重要见证。
Brief_intro.en: The earliest known capital city site in China, Yin Xu encompasses palace, ancestral shrine, and royal tomb precincts, and has yielded oracle bone inscriptions and bronze artifacts that are among the most important material witnesses to early Chinese civilization.

Standard.cn: 殷叙，商朝晚期的都城，展现了中国古代青铜文化的重要影响交流和最高发展水平，包括文字体系。
Standard.en: Yinxu, the capital of the late Shang Dynasty, showcases the significant influence and highest level of development of ancient Chinese bronze culture, including its writing system.

Standard.cn: 殷旭遗址的文化遗存为商代晚期的文化传统提供了非凡的证据，并见证了许多科学技术成就和创新，例如太阳历和阴历系统，以及甲骨文中最早的系统性汉字书写证据。
Standard.en: The cultural remains at the Yinxu site provide remarkable evidence of the cultural traditions of the late Shang Dynasty and bear witness to many scientific and technological achievements and innovations, such as the solar and lunar calendar systems, as well as the earliest systematic evidence of Chinese character writing in oracle bone inscriptions.

Standard.cn: 殷旭的宫殿、祠堂和皇家陵墓是早期中国建筑的杰出代表，对确立中国宫殿建筑和皇家陵墓建筑群的早期原型具有重要意义。
Standard.en: Yin Xu's palaces, ancestral halls, and royal tombs are outstanding representatives of early Chinese architecture and are of great significance in establishing the early prototypes of Chinese palace architecture and royal tomb complexes.

Standard.cn: 殷旭遗址发现的物质遗存为中国文字和语言体系的早期历史、古代信仰、社会制度和重大历史事件提供了有形的证据，具有突出的普遍意义。
Standard.en: The material remains discovered at the Yinxu site provide tangible evidence for the early history of Chinese writing and language systems, ancient beliefs, social systems, and major historical events, and have outstanding universal significance.

Description.cn: 殷叙遗址位于中国中部河南省安阳市西北，环河两岸，距今已有1300年历史。遗址包括宫殿及皇家祠堂区和皇家陵寝区两部分，总面积414公顷，另有720公顷的缓冲区。历史文献、甲骨文和考古发掘均证实，殷叙是中国历史上最早的都城。公元前1300年左右，商朝第二十位君主潘庚将都城从燕迁至殷（今安阳市小屯村一带），建立了一座长久稳定的都城。殷叙历经255年，十二位君主，八代人，缔造了辉煌灿烂的殷商文明，其历史、艺术和科学价值无可估量。殷叙是最早拥有文明迹象的遗址，包括80多处夯土房屋地基及木结构遗迹、祖先祠堂和祭坛，这些遗址被防御壕沟环绕，壕沟也兼具防洪功能。宫殿区内众多坑穴中出土了刻有文字的甲骨文，被认为是已知最早的汉字证据。地势较高的皇家陵墓区内有祭祀坑，坑内有战车和被认为是祭祀牺牲者的遗骸。陪葬品包括装饰精美的青铜礼器、玉雕、骨雕和陶瓷器。作为中国早期最重要的都城之一，殷叙的规划布局对后世都城的建设和发展产生了深远的影响。殷叙王陵区是中国现存最早的大型皇家陵墓群，也是中国皇家陵寝体系的起源；甲骨文是中国已知最早的成熟文字，是商代历史的有力佐证，有助于追溯近千年前的中国历史；殷叙遗址则展现了商代晚期的社会生活，反映了高度发达的科学和建筑技术，包括青铜铸造和历法体系。
Description.en: Situated on both banks of the Huanhe River to the northwest of the nationally famous historic and cultural city Anyang, in Henan Province of central China, the archaeological remains of Yin Xu dated from 1,300 BCE and comprise two sites: the Palace and Royal Ancestral Shrines Area and the Royal Tombs Area covering a total 414 hectares with an enclosing buffer zone of 720 hectares. Yin Xu has been confirmed by historic documents, oracle bone inscriptions and archaeological excavations as the first site of a capital in Chinese history. The twentieth king of the Shang Dynasty Pan Geng, moved his capital from Yan to Yin (the area around Xiaotun Village of present Anyang) around 1,300 BC, and established a lasting and stable capital. It spanned 255 years with 12 kings and 8 generations and created the splendid and brilliant Yin-Shang Civilization, which is of priceless value in terms of history, art and science.Yin Xu was the earliest site to possess the elements of civilization, including more than 80 house foundations of rammed earth with remains of timber structures, ancestral shrines and altars enclosed within a defensive ditch which also functioned as a flood-control system. Numerous pits within the Palace area contained inscribed oracle bones considered to carry the earliest evidence of the Chinese written language. The Royal Tombs area on higher ground includes sacrificial pits containing chariots and human remains considered to have been sacrificial victims. Burial goods included decorated bronze ritual vessels, jade and bone carvings and ceramics.Being one of the most important capital sites in early China, its planning and layout had an important influence on the construction and development of subsequent capitals of China. The Royal Tomb Area of Yin Xu is the earliest large-scale royal graveyard in China and the source of China’s system of royal and imperial mausoleums;oracle bone inscriptions are the earliest known mature writing in China and constitute evidence for the history of the Shang Dynasty in China, helping to track recorded Chinese history nearly one thousand years earlier, and the Site of Yin Xu conveys the social life of the late Shang Dynasty, reflecting highly developed science and architectural technology including bronze casting and a calendar system.

Dynast.en: The Northern and Southern Dynasties period (420-589)

History_background.cn: 北魏时期皇室下令开凿
History_background.en: The imperial court ordered the excavation during the Northern Wei Dynasty.

Main_function.cn: 佛教石窟艺术展示与信仰
Main_function.en: Buddhist Grotto Art Display and Belief

BUilding_use.cn: 佛像雕刻与宗教活动场所
BUilding_use.en: Buddhist statues and religious activity sites

Brief_intro.cn: 始建于5世纪中叶至6世纪初，拥有252个洞窟和51000尊佛像，是中国佛教石窟艺术的巅峰之作，具有重要历史和艺术价值。
Brief_intro.en: Constructed from the mid-5th century to the early 6th century, the Yungang Grottoes contain 252 caves and 51,000 Buddhist statues, representing the pinnacle of Chinese Buddhist grotto art and possessing immense historical and artistic significance.

Standard.cn: 云冈石窟的雕像群是中国早期佛教石窟艺术的杰作。
Standard.en: The sculptures in the Yungang Grottoes are masterpieces of early Chinese Buddhist grotto art.

Standard.cn: 云冈石窟艺术代表了南亚和中亚佛教宗教象征艺术与中国文化传统的成功融合，始于公元5世纪，在皇室的赞助下。
Standard.en: The Yungang Grottoes art represents a successful fusion of South Asian and Central Asian Buddhist religious symbolism with Chinese cultural traditions, beginning in the 5th century AD under the patronage of the royal family.

Standard.cn: 云冈石窟生动地说明了佛教信仰在中国的强大力量和持久性。
Standard.en: The Yungang Grottoes vividly illustrate the powerful influence and enduring nature of Buddhism in China.

Standard.cn: 佛教宗教石窟艺术传统在云冈石窟首次产生重大影响，并发展出自己独特的风格和艺术力量。
Standard.en: The Buddhist religious grotto art tradition first had a significant impact on the Yungang Grottoes, and developed its own unique style and artistic power.

Description.cn: 云冈石窟规模宏大，开凿于公元5世纪中叶至6世纪初。石窟占地18000平方米，共有252个洞窟和龛位，佛像51000尊，是中国佛教石窟艺术的巅峰之作。谭尧开凿的五窟是中国艺术早期巅峰的经典之作，布局和设计严谨统一。云冈石窟是北魏时期，由皇室下令开凿，体现了当时中国佛教信仰中的国家意志。云冈石窟虽然受到南亚和中亚佛教石窟艺术的影响，但也融入了鲜明的中国特色和地域精神。因此，云冈石窟在早期东方佛教石窟中占据着举足轻重的地位，对中国乃至东亚的佛教石窟艺术产生了深远的影响。
Description.en: The massive Yungang Buddhist grottoes were cut from the mid-5th Century to early-6th Century AD.  Comprising 252 caves and niches and 51,000 statues within a carved area of 18,000 square meters, the Yungang Grottoes represent the outstanding achievement of Buddhist cave art in China. The Five Caves created by Tan Yao are a classical masterpiece of the first peak of Chinese art, with a strict unity of layout and design. The will of the State is reflected in Buddhist belief in China during the Northern Wei Dynasty since the Grottoes were built with Imperial instructions. While influenced by Buddhist cave art from South and Central Asia, Yungang Grottoes have also interpreted the Buddhist cave art with distinctive Chinese character and local spirit. As a result, Yungang Grottoes have played a vitally important role among early Oriental Buddhist grottoes and had a far-reaching impact on Buddhist cave art in China and East Asia.

Name.cn: 左江花山岩画文化景观
Name.en: Zuojiang Huashan Rock Art Cultural Landscape

Dynast.cn: 周朝(公元前1046年 - 公元前256年)

History_background.cn: 公元前5世纪至公元2世纪青铜鼓文化
History_background.en: Bronze Drum Culture (5th century BC to 2nd century AD)

Main_function.cn: 描绘仪式和生活的岩画遗址
Main_function.en: Rock painting sites depicting rituals and daily life

Brief_intro.cn: 这些岩画位于陡峭悬崖上，反映了青铜鼓文化的仪式与生活。
Brief_intro.en: Located on sheer cliff faces, these rock art paintings reflect the rituals and way of life of the bronze drum culture.

Standard.cn: 左江华山岩画文化景观以其独特的景观与岩画组合，生动地展现了公元前5世纪至公元2世纪生活在左江沿岸的洛月族人蓬勃的精神和社会生活，是这一传统如今唯一的见证。
Standard.en: The Zuojiang Huashan Rock Art Cultural Landscape, with its unique combination of landscape and rock art, vividly showcases the vibrant spirit and social life of the Luoyue people who lived along the Zuojiang River from the 5th century BC to the 2nd century AD. It is the only remaining witness to this tradition.

Standard.cn: 左江华山壁画中描绘的鼓及相关元素，是与曾经在该地区广泛传播的青铜鼓文化直接相关的象征性记录。如今，青铜鼓在中国南方仍然被视为权力的象征。
Standard.en: The drums and related elements depicted in the Zuojiang Huashan murals are symbolic records directly related to the bronze drum culture that was once widespread in the region. Today, bronze drums are still regarded as a symbol of power in southern China.

Description.cn: 这些岩画遗址的历史可追溯至公元前5世纪至公元2世纪，共38处，其所在的喀斯特地貌、河岸景观和台地景观描绘了各种仪式，这些仪式被认为是曾经盛行于中国南方的青铜鼓文化的体现。这些岩画位于蜿蜒的左江及其支流明江切割喀斯特地貌的陡峭悬崖上，由洛月人创作，描绘了他们的生活和仪式。
Description.en: Dating from around the 5th century BCE to the 2nd century CE, 38 sites of rock art and their associated karst, riverine and tableland landscape depict ceremonies that have been interpreted as portraying the bronze drum culture once prevalent across southern China. Located on steep cliffs cut through the karst landscape by the meandering Zuojiang River and its tributary Mingjiang River, the pictographs were created by the Luoyue people illustrating their life and rituals.

Name.cn: 巴丹吉林沙漠——沙山湖泊群
Name.en: Badain Jaran Desert - Towers of Sand and Lakes

City.cn: 内蒙古自治区阿拉善盟
City.en: Alxa League, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region

History_background.cn: 受气候变化和青藏高原隆升影响
History_background.en: Affected by climate change and the uplift of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau

Main_function.cn: 自然遗产保护与科研
Main_function.en: Natural Heritage Conservation and Scientific Research

Brief_intro.cn: 中国第三大沙漠，拥有世界最高的稳定沙丘、丰富的湖泊和独特的生物群落，是重要的自然遗产地。
Brief_intro.en: China's third largest desert, home to the world's tallest stationary sand dunes, abundant lakes, and unique biological communities, this is an outstanding natural heritage site.

Standard.cn: 巴丹吉兰沙漠——沙丘与湖泊展现了温带极度干旱气候下沙漠景观和地貌的壮观地质和地貌特征。这些特征造就了非凡的美学价值，体现在密集的、稳定的、线性的、平行的巨型沙丘，以及众多沙丘间湖泊和各种类型的小型沙丘之间。144个沙丘间湖泊呈现出万千色彩，这是由不同的盐度和微生物群落造成的。这里还拥有大片被称为“鸣沙”（指风吹动干燥松散的沙子时产生的共鸣）的沙丘，呈现出非凡的声景。风蚀地貌、绿洲、波纹效应以及世界最高巨型沙丘（相对高度达460米）的雄伟气势，共同构成了一幅令人叹为观止的自然美景。沙丘的动态变化营造出不断变化的视觉环境。
Standard.en: The Badain Jaran Desert—with its dunes and lakes—showcases spectacular geological and geomorphological features characteristic of desert landscapes and landforms in an extremely arid temperate climate. These features create extraordinary aesthetic value, manifested in the dense, stable, linear, parallel giant dunes, numerous inter-dune lakes, and various types of smaller dunes. The 144 inter-dune lakes display a myriad of colors, created by varying salinity and microbial communities. The area also boasts vast expanses of dunes known as "singing sands" (referring to the resonance produced when wind blows through dry, loose sand), creating a remarkable soundscape. Wind-eroded landforms, oases, ripple effects, and the majestic presence of the world's tallest giant dune (reaching a relative height of 460 meters) combine to create a breathtaking natural landscape. The dynamic changes in the dunes create an ever-changing visual environment.

Standard.cn: 该遗产地位于中国三大沙质区域的交界处，是温带和极度干旱气候下沙漠景观和地貌持续演化的杰出范例。它记录并展现了极其丰富的风成地貌和沙漠地貌特征，例如线状和平行的稳定巨型沙丘以及相关的沙丘间湖泊。该遗产地在全球范围内极为罕见，它反映了区域构造运动和与气候演化相关的水文地质变化共同作用下地貌的演化过程。该遗产地线状巨型沙丘的卓越稳定性以及丰富的沙丘间湖泊也使其脱颖而出。它拥有全球最密集的稳定巨型沙丘群，其中包括地球上最高的沙丘之一以及沙丘间湖泊密度最高的地区。该遗产地拥有144个沙丘间湖泊和种类繁多的沙丘地貌，展现出非凡的地质多样性。世界自然保护联盟 (IUCN) 2011 年关于沙漠景观的专题研究和 2021 年关于标准 (viii) 应用的研究都强调，该遗产地是目前尚未列入世界遗产名录的最重要的沙漠景观和地貌遗址之一。
Standard.en: Located at the intersection of three major sandy regions in China, this heritage site is an outstanding example of the continuous evolution of desert landscapes and landforms under temperate and extremely arid climates. It records and showcases an exceptionally rich array of aeolian and desert landforms, such as linear and parallel stable mega-dus dunes and associated interdune lakes. This site is extremely rare globally, reflecting the evolution of landforms under the combined influence of regional tectonic movements and climate-related hydrogeological changes. The remarkable stability of its linear mega-dus dunes and the abundance of interdune lakes further distinguish it. It boasts the world's densest concentration of stable mega-dus dunes, including some of the tallest dunes on Earth and the highest density of interdune lakes. With 144 interdune lakes and a diverse range of dune landforms, the site demonstrates remarkable geological diversity. Both the IUCN 2011 thematic study on desert landscapes and the 2021 study on the application of criterion (viii) emphasize that this site is one of the most important desert landscape and landform sites not yet inscribed on the World Heritage List.

Description.cn: 该遗产地面积726,291.41公顷，缓冲区面积891,114.36公顷。巴丹吉林沙漠位于中国西北部极度干旱的温带沙漠地区阿拉善高原，是中国第三大沙漠，拥有不可替代的湖泊和沙丘沙漠地貌自然遗产。其显著特征是巨型沙丘密度极高，其中包括世界上最高的稳定沙丘、无数的沙丘间湖泊以及各种风成地貌。巨型沙丘构成起伏的地形，其中最高的沙丘相对高度达460米。尽管是沙漠和沙海，巴丹吉林却拥有丰富的植物资源和以夜行性动物为主的生物群落。湖泊大多为咸水湖，颜色多样，为蠕虫、软体动物、甲壳类动物和一些鱼类提供了理想的栖息地。由于其地理位置和地质背景，该遗址深受气候变化和青藏高原持续隆升的影响。其沙漠化过程仍在继续，因此该遗址及其遗迹为了解长期气候变化和沙漠化过程提供了重要线索。遗址的规模和完整性对​​于理解其持续演变至关重要。该地拥有杰出的美学价值，这得益于其大量的巨型沙丘、多样化的风成景观以及独特的湖泊。
Description.en: The property covers an area of 726,291.41 ha, with a buffer zone of 891,114.36 ha. Badain Jaran Desert, located in the Alashan Plateau in the hyper-arid and temperate desert region of northwestern China, is the third largest desert in China and hosts an irreplaceable natural heritage of lake and dune desert features. It stands out with its high density of mega-dunes, including the tallest stabilized sand dunes in the world, a myriad of interdunal lakes, and a range of aeolian landform features. The mega-dunes form an undulating landscape, among which the tallest sand dune achieves a relative height of 460 m. For a sandy desert and sand sea, Badain Jaran is home to abundant plant life and mostly nocturnal animal life. The lakes are mostly saline and diversely coloured, providing a favourable habitat for thriving worms, molluscs, crustacea and some fish.Due to its geographical location and geological background, the property is strongly influenced by climate change and the continuing tectonic uplift of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. Its desert-forming process is continuing, so that the site and its relics offer insights into long-term climatic changes and desert forming processes. The size and integrity of the site is important in understanding its ongoing evolution.The property holds outstanding aesthetic values thanks to the significant abundance of mega-dunes, aeolian landscape diversity and to the uniqueness of its lakes.

History_background.cn: 自新近纪至今在红色沉积层序中持续发育
History_background.en: Continuously developed in red sedimentary sequences from the Neogene to the present.

Main_function.cn: 展示地貌类型及其形成过程
Main_function.en: Showcasing landform types and their formation processes

Brief_intro.cn: 分布于中国东南部，因内外力共同作用于红色沉积岩层，形成壮观的红色悬崖及多样侵蚀地貌。
Brief_intro.en: Distributed across southeastern China, these landscapes have been shaped by both internal and external geological forces acting on red sedimentary rock layers, producing spectacular red cliffs and a diverse array of erosional landforms.

Standard.cn: 中国丹霞地貌是一处令人印象深刻且独一无二的自然景观。构成这片非凡自然美景的红色砾岩和砂岩，被雕琢成壮观的山峰、石柱、峭壁和深邃的峡谷。与交相辉映的森林、蜿蜒的河流和雄伟的瀑布相得益彰，中国丹霞地貌呈现出重要的自然奇观。
Standard.en: China's Danxia landforms are an impressive and unique natural landscape. The red conglomerate and sandstone that make up this extraordinary natural beauty have been sculpted into spectacular peaks, pillars, cliffs, and deep canyons. Complemented by interwoven forests, winding rivers, and majestic waterfalls, China's Danxia landforms present a significant natural wonder.

Standard.cn: 中国丹霞地貌包含多种发育良好的红色地貌，例如山峰、塔状地貌、台地、陡坡、悬崖、山谷、洞穴和拱门。丹霞地貌受内力（包括隆升）和外力（包括风化和侵蚀）的共同作用，展现了在温暖湿润的季风气候下，由陆相红色砾岩和砂岩发育而成的各种地貌特征，体现了地貌多样性及其形成过程。各组成部分代表了从“侵蚀程度最低”到“侵蚀程度最高”的丹霞地貌的最佳范例，呈现出从“年轻”到“成熟”再到“衰老”的清晰地貌演化序列，每个组成部分都展现了特定阶段的特征地貌特征。
Standard.en: China's Danxia landforms encompass a variety of well-developed red landforms, such as peaks, tower-like formations, plateaus, steep slopes, cliffs, valleys, caves, and arches. Driven by both internal forces (including uplift) and external forces (including weathering and erosion), Danxia landforms exhibit diverse geomorphic features developed from terrestrial red conglomerate and sandstone under warm and humid monsoon climates, reflecting landform diversity and its formation process. Each component represents a prime example of Danxia landforms, ranging from "least eroded" to "most eroded," showcasing a clear geomorphic evolution sequence from "young" to "mature" and then to "aged," with each component displaying characteristic geomorphic features of a specific stage.

Description.cn: 中国丹霞地貌是一个系列地貌，由六个组成部分（赤水、泰宁、狼山、丹霞山、龙虎山和江狼山）组成，位于中国东南部的亚热带地区，呈新月形，西起贵州省，东至浙江省，绵延约 1700 公里。中国丹霞地貌是指在中国境内，由内力（包括隆升）和外力（包括风化和侵蚀）共同作用，在大陆红色陆源沉积岩层上发育而成的地貌。其特征是壮观的红色悬崖和一系列侵蚀地貌，包括气势磅礴的天然石柱、石塔、沟壑、山谷和瀑布。丹霞地貌的形成过程受特定岩层序列、构造背景、气候条件、侵蚀过程和地貌特征的影响，本文提出了一个初步的丹霞地貌形成模型。由于内力（构造隆升）和外力（气候、侵蚀、风化）等多种因素的共同作用，丹霞地貌自新近纪至今在红色沉积层序中持续发育。这六个组成部分代表了从“侵蚀程度最低”到“侵蚀程度最高”的丹霞地貌的典型代表，展现了该现象的不同方面，并阐明了地貌类型及其形成过程中的各种作用力和过程，以及与之相关的景观类型。
Description.en: China Danxia is a serial property comprising six component parts (Chishui, Taining, Langshan, Danxiashan, Longhushan, and Jianglangshan) found in the sub-tropical zone of south-eastern China within approximately 1700 km crescent shaped arc from Guizhou Province in the west to Zhejiang Province in the east.China Danxia is the name given in China to landscapes developed on continental red terrigenous sedimentary beds influenced by endogenous forces (including uplift) and exogenous forces (including weathering and erosion). It is characterised by spectacular red cliffs and a range of erosional landforms, including dramatic natural pillars, towers, ravines, valleys and waterfalls. The process of its development is characterised by a particular rock sequence, tectonic background, climatic conditions, erosional processes and landforms and these processes have been presented as an interim model.Due to the combined endogenic (tectonic uplift) and exogenic (climatic, erosion, weathering) forces, and other factors, the Danxia landforms have been developed in red sedimentary sequences continuously from the Neogene until the present.  The six component parts represent the most important examples of 'least eroded' to 'most eroded' Danxia landforms, providing a range of different aspects of the phenomenon, and illustrate both the range of landforms in relation to the forces and processes that formed them, together with a range of associated landscapes.

History_background.cn: 孕育众多第三纪孑遗物种
History_background.en: Nurturing numerous Tertiary relict species

Main_function.cn: 生物多样性保护
Main_function.en: Biodiversity conservation

Brief_intro.cn: 重要的水源地和生物多样性保护区，拥有众多特有和濒危动植物物种，是贵州高原生态系统的重要组成部分。
Brief_intro.en: An important water source and biodiversity reserve, Fanjingshan harbors numerous endemic and endangered species of flora and fauna, and is an integral component of the Guizhou Plateau ecosystem.

Standard.cn: 梵净山以其丰富的苔藓植物资源而著称，共有791种，其中74种为中国特有种。该遗产地还拥有世界上最为丰富的裸子植物资源之一，共有36种。遗产地内分布着大量特有物种，包括46种地方特有植物和1010种中国特有植物，以及4种地方特有脊椎动物。其中最引人注目的是濒危物种贵州仰鼻猴，它仅分布于梵净山，世界其他任何地方均无分布。另一个重要的特有物种是梵净山杉，也仅分布于该遗产地。
Standard.en: Fanjingshan is renowned for its rich bryophyte resources, boasting 791 species, 74 of which are endemic to China. The heritage site also possesses one of the world's richest gymnosperm resources, with 36 species. Numerous endemic species are distributed within the site, including 46 local endemic plant species and 1010 species endemic to China, as well as 4 endemic vertebrate species. Among the most notable are the endangered Guizhou snub-nosed monkey, found only in Fanjingshan and nowhere else in the world. Another important endemic species is the Fanjingshan cedar, also found only within this heritage site.

Description.cn: 梵净山世界遗产地位于中国西南地区，总面积40275公顷，四周环绕着37239公顷的缓冲区。梵净山地处季风气候区，是周边地区乃至更远地区的重要水源地，约有20条河流溪流汇入乌江和沱江水系，最终都注入长江。该遗产地由两部分组成，分别是建南亚热带常绿林生态区（64%）和贵州高原阔叶混交林生态区（36%）。最高峰凤凰山海拔2570米，遗产地海拔落差超过2000米。由此形成的植被垂直分层可分为三个主要海拔植被带：常绿阔叶林（海拔<1300米）、常绿阔叶混交林（海拔1300-2200米）和落叶阔叶、针叶混交灌丛林（海拔>2200米）。梵净山是喀斯特海域中一座由变质岩构成的岛屿，孕育着众多起源于第三纪（距今6500万至200万年前）的古老孑遗动植物物种。该地独特的地理和气候特征造就了其岛屿般的植物群落，使其呈现出高度的特有性。目前已知的特有植物有46种，特有脊椎动物有4种，特有无脊椎动物有245种。其中最突出的特有物种是梵净山杉（Abies fanjingshanensis - EN）和贵州仰鼻猴（Rhinopithecus brelichi - EN），这两种物种均仅分布于梵净山。此外，山毛榉属（Fagus）的三种树种（长柄山毛榉F. longipetiolata、亮叶山毛榉F. lucida和恩氏山毛榉F. engleriana）构成了该地区目前所知的最大的原始山毛榉林。该保护区已记录到3724种植物，占中国植物总数的13%，令人瞩目。保护区以苔藓植物的丰富度著称，同时也是中国裸子植物的重要分布中心之一。无脊椎动物的多样性也十分丰富，共有2317种。此外，保护区内还发现了450种脊椎动物。梵净山是梵净山杉和贵州金丝猴在世界上的唯一栖息地，同时也是64种植物和38种动物的栖息地，这些物种被列为全球濒危物种，其中包括中华大鲵（濒危）、中华鲵（极危）、森林麝（濒危）、白雉（易危）和西藏黑熊（易危）。
Description.en: The Fanjingshan World Heritage property is located in South-West China, covering a total area of 40,275 ha, fully enclosed by a buffer zone of 37,239 ha. Fanjingshan is located in a monsoonal climatic context and is an important source of water for the surrounding landscapes and beyond, with some 20 rivers and streams feeding the Wujiang and Yuanjiang River systems, both of which ultimately drain into the Yangtze River.The property consists of two parts, namely the Jian Nan subtropical evergreen forests ecoregion (64%) and the Guizhou Plateau broadleaf and mixed forests ecoregion (36%). The highest peak, Mt Fenghuangshan, has an elevation of 2,570 m above sea level (masl) and the property covers and an altitudinal range of more than 2,000 m. The resulting vertical stratification of vegetation falls within three major altitudinal vegetation zones: evergreen broadleaf forest (<1,300 masl), mixed evergreen and deciduous broadleaf forest (1,300-2,200 masl) and mixed deciduous broadleaf and conifer and scrub forest (>2,200 masl).Fanjingshan is an island of metamorphic rock in a sea of karst and is home to many ancient and relict plant and animal species which originated in the Tertiary period, between 65 million and 2 million years ago. The property’s geologic and climatic characteristics have shaped its flora which behaves as if it were on an island. This has led to a high degree of endemism, with a total of 46 locally endemic plant species, 4 endemic vertebrate species and 245 endemic invertebrate species. The most prominent endemic species are Fanjingshan Fir (Abies fanjingshanensis - EN) and Guizhou Snub-nosed Monkey (Rhinopithecus brelichi - EN), both of which are entirely restricted to the property. Three species of Fagus (F. longipetiolata, F. lucida, and F. engleriana) are the dominant species of what is understood to be the largest primary beech forest in the subtropical region.A total of 3,724 plant species have been recorded in the property, an impressive 13% of China’s total flora. The property is characterized by an exceptionally high richness in bryophytes as well as one of the distribution centres for gymnosperms in China. The diversity of invertebrates is also very high with 2,317 species. A total of 450 vertebrate species are found inside the property. Fanjingshan being the only habitat in the world for Fanjingshan Fir and Guizhou Snub-nosed Monkey, as well as 64 plant and 38 animal species that are listed as globally threatened, including the tree Bretschneidera sinensis (EN), Chinese Giant Salamander (Andrias davidianus - CR), Forest Musk Deer (Moschus berezovskii - EN), Reeves’s Pheasant (Syrmaticus reevesii - VU), and Asiatic Black Bear (Ursus thibetanus - VU).

Name.en: Huanglong Scenic and Historic Interest Area

City.cn: 四川省阿坝藏族羌族自治州
City.en: Aba Tibetan and Qiang Autonomous Prefecture, Sichuan Province

History_background.cn: none
History_background.en: none

Main_function.cn: 自然景观旅游
Main_function.en: Natural Landscape Tourism

Brief_intro.cn: 以石灰华湖泊、瀑布、森林和山景闻名，是众多野生动植物的栖息地。
Brief_intro.en: Renowned for its travertine lakes, waterfalls, forests, and mountain scenery, the Huanglong area provides vital habitat for a rich variety of wildlife.

Standard.cn: 黄龙以其秀丽的山地风光而闻名，拥有相对未受破坏且高度多样化的森林生态系统，以及更为壮观的局部喀斯特地貌，例如石灰华池、瀑布和石灰岩浅滩。其石灰华梯田和湖泊在亚洲独一无二，位列世界三大杰出代表之列
Standard.en: Huanglong is renowned for its stunning mountain scenery, boasting a relatively unspoiled and highly diverse forest ecosystem, as well as spectacular local karst landforms such as travertine pools, waterfalls, and limestone shoals. Its travertine terraces and lakes are unique in Asia and rank among the world's three most outstanding examples.

Description.cn: 黄龙谷位于四川省西北部，拥有连绵不断的石灰华湖泊、瀑布、森林和壮丽的山景，是一处绝佳的自然景观。谷内山峰常年积雪，海拔从1700米到5588米不等，其中包括中国最东端的冰川。这片位于岷山山脉的6万公顷区域，还拥有壮观的石灰岩地貌和温泉。其多样化的森林生态系统为众多濒危动植物提供了栖息地，其中包括大熊猫和川金丝猴。
Description.en: Situated in the north-west of Sichuan Province, the Huanglong valley with its series of travertine lakes, waterfalls, forests and mountain scenery is a superlative natural property. Topped by permanently snow-capped peaks rising from a base of 1,700 m up to 5,588 m, these include the easternmost glacier in China. Covering 60,000 ha, this area located within the Minshan Mountains also includes spectacular limestone formations and hot springs. Its diverse forest ecosystems provide the home for a number of endangered plants and animals, including the giant panda and Sichuan golden snub-nosed monkey.

History_background.cn: 曾是19至20世纪植物考察地
History_background.en: It was once a site for botanical research in the 19th and 20th centuries.

Main_function.cn: 生物多样性保护与科学研究
Main_function.en: Biodiversity conservation and scientific research

Brief_intro.cn: 中国三大特有植物物种中心之一，拥有丰富的动植物资源和多样的生态系统，是重要的生物多样性保护区和科研基地。
Brief_intro.en: One of China's three major centers of endemic plant species, Shennongjia possesses abundant flora and fauna, diverse ecosystems, and serves as a major biodiversity reserve and scientific research base.

Standard.cn: 湖北神农架保护着华中地区最大的原始森林，也是中国三大特有植物物种中心之一。该遗产地包含11种植被类型，并完整地保留了六个海拔梯度上的植被类型，包括常绿阔叶林、常绿落叶阔叶混交林、落叶阔叶林、针阔混交林、针叶林和灌丛/草甸。该遗产地拥有874种落叶木本植物，隶属于260个属，其树种和属的丰富度在世界范围内的落叶阔叶林类型中首屈一指。在北半球的常绿落叶阔叶混交林中，湖北神农架拥有世界上最完整的海拔自然带。湖北神农架位于大巴山常绿林生态区和西南温带森林优先生态区内，这两个区域均尚未被列入世界遗产名录。它还保护着神农架植物多样性区域中心，该中心已被认定为世界遗产名录的空白区域。除了丰富的植物多样性外，该遗产地还保护着众多珍稀濒危动物物种的关键生态系统。
Standard.en: Shennongjia in Hubei Province protects the largest primeval forest in Central China and is one of China's three major centers for endemic plant species. The heritage site encompasses 11 vegetation types and preserves vegetation types across six altitudinal gradients, including evergreen broad-leaved forests, evergreen-deciduous broad-leaved mixed forests, deciduous broad-leaved forests, coniferous-broad-leaved mixed forests, coniferous forests, and shrub/meadow. With 874 species of deciduous woody plants belonging to 260 genera, its species and genera richness is unparalleled among deciduous broad-leaved forest types worldwide. Among evergreen-deciduous broad-leaved mixed forests in the Northern Hemisphere, Shennongjia boasts the world's most complete altitudinal natural zones. Located within the Dabashan Evergreen Forest Ecoregion and the Southwest Temperate Forest Priority Ecoregion, both areas are not yet listed as World Heritage Sites. It also protects the Shennongjia Regional Centre for Plant Diversity, which has been identified as a World Heritage Blank Area. In addition to its rich plant diversity, the heritage site also safeguards key ecosystems for numerous rare and endangered animal species.

Standard.cn: 湖北神农架独特的地形和气候受冰川作用影响较小，因此成为众多珍稀濒危特有物种以及许多世界落叶木本植物的栖息地。该遗产地物种丰富度极高，尤其以维管植物最为丰富，其温带植物属的种类占中国总数的63%以上，而中国是生物多样性极其丰富的国家，拥有世界上最多的温带植物属。该遗产地拥有全国12.9%的维管植物物种。山地地形也为多种旗舰动物物种提供了重要的栖息地。遗产地内记录到1550只金丝猴（又称川金丝猴）。神农架的金丝猴是中国3个亚种中最濒危的，且仅分布于该遗产地。其他重要物种包括云豹、豹、金猫、豺、黑熊、灵猫、麝、中华鬣羚、中华鬣羚、金雕、白雉以及世界上最大的两栖动物——中国大鲵。该保护区生物多样性极其丰富，拥有大量模式种，并栖息着许多已被引入世界各地园艺栽培的珍稀物种。在国际上，神农架在植物系统学和园艺学研究领域占有特殊地位。
Standard.en: The unique topography and climate of Shennongjia in Hubei Province, less affected by glacial activity, have made it a habitat for numerous rare, endangered, and endemic species, as well as many deciduous woody plants. The site boasts exceptional biodiversity, particularly in vascular plants, with over 63% of China's temperate plant genera. China is an extremely biodiverse country, possessing the world's largest number of temperate plant genera. This site is home to 12.9% of China's vascular plant species. The mountainous terrain also provides important habitats for several flagship animal species. 1,550 golden snub-nosed monkeys (also known as Sichuan golden snub-nosed monkeys) have been recorded within the site. The Shennongjia golden snub-nosed monkey is the most endangered of China's three subspecies and is found only within this site. Other important species include clouded leopards, leopards, golden cats, dholes, Asiatic black bears, civets, musk deer, Chinese serows, golden eagles, white pheasants, and the world's largest amphibian—the Chinese giant salamander. The reserve is extremely biodiverse, possessing numerous type species and home to many rare species that have been introduced into horticulture cultivation worldwide. Internationally, Shennongjia holds a special position in the fields of plant systematics and horticulture research.

Description.cn: 湖北神农架位于中国湖北省神农架林区和巴东县境内。神农架地处中国东部平原和丘陵地区与中部山区之间的生态交汇处，也是气候由亚热带向暖温带过渡的地带，南北冷暖气团在此交汇，并受副热带环​​流控制。该遗产地面积79,624公顷，由西部较大的神农顶/巴东区域和东部较小的老君山区域组成。遗产地周围环绕着45,390公顷的缓冲区。湖北神农架拥有11种植被类型，其特征是海拔梯度多样性。神农架地区被认为是中国三大特有植物物种中心之一，这反映了其地理过渡位置塑造了该地区的生物多样性、生态系统和生物演化。湖北神农架的物种丰富度和特有性在全球范围内都令人瞩目，尤其是在植物区系方面，已记录到3,767种维管植物，其中包括590个温带植物属。此外，有205种植物和2个属是该遗产地的特有种，1,793种植物是中国特有种。该保护区已记录到600多种脊椎动物，其中包括92种哺乳动物、399种鸟类、55种鱼类、53种爬行动物和37种两栖动物。此外，还鉴定出4365种昆虫。保护区内栖息着众多珍稀濒危物种，例如金丝猴（又称四川金丝猴）、云豹、豹、金猫、豺、黑熊、灵猫、麝、中华鬣羚、中华鬣羚、金雕、白腹锦鸡以及世界上最大的两栖动物——中华大鲵。神农架一直以来都是重要的科学研究地点，其山脉在植物学研究史上占有举足轻重的地位。该地区在植物学领域具有特殊的地位，曾是19世纪和20世纪众多国际植物采集考察队的目标。1884年至1889年间，该地区记录到500多个新物种。神农架也是许多物种的全球模式产地。
Description.en: Hubei Shennongjia is located in the Shennongjia Forestry District and Badong County in China’s Hubei Province. Shennongjia is on the ecotone from the plains and foothill regions of eastern China to the mountainous region of central China. It is also situated along a zone of climate transition, where the climate shifts from the subtropical zone to warm temperate zone, and where warm and cold air masses from north and south meet and are controlled by the Subtropical Gyre.The property covers 79,624 ha and consists of two components, the larger Shennongding/Badong component in the west and the smaller Laojunshan component to the east. A buffer zone of 45,390 ha surrounds the property. Hubei Shennongjia includes 11 types of vegetation which are characterized by a diversity of altitudinal gradients. The Shennongjia region is considered to be one of three centres of endemic plant species in China, a reflection of its geographical transitional position which has shaped its biodiversity, ecosystems and biological evolution. Hubei Shennongjia exhibits globally impressive levels of species richness and endemism especially within its flora, 3,767 vascular plant species have been recorded including a remarkable 590 temperate plant genera. In addition, 205 plant species and 2 genera are endemic to the property, and 1,793 species endemic to China. Among the fauna, more than 600 vertebrate species have been recorded including 92 mammal, 399 bird, 55 fish, 53 reptile and 37 amphibian species. 4,365 insect species have been identified. The property includes numerous rare and endangered species such as the Golden or Sichuan Snub-nosed Monkey, Clouded Leopard, Common Leopard, Asian Golden Cat, Dhole, Asian Black Bear, Indian Civet, Musk Deer, Chinese Goral and Chinese Serow, Golden Eagle, Reeve’s Pheasant and the world’s largest amphibian the Chinese Giant Salamander.Shennongjia has been a place of significant scientific interest and its mountains have featured prominently in the history of botanical inquiry. The site has a special status for botany and has been the object of celebrated international plant collecting expeditions conducted in the 19th and 20th centuries. From 1884 to 1889 more than 500 new species were recorded from the area. Shennongjia is also the global type location for many species.

Name.en: Jiuzhaigou Valley Scenic and Historic Interest Area

City.cn: 四川省阿坝藏族羌族自治州
City.en: Aba Tibetan and Qiang Autonomous Prefecture, Sichuan Province

History_background.cn: none
History_background.en: none

Main_function.cn: 自然风光保护与观赏
Main_function.en: Natural landscape protection and appreciation

Brief_intro.cn: 以高山、湖泊、瀑布等秀丽的景色和风光的自然景观著称，是珍稀动植物的重要栖息地。
Brief_intro.en: Celebrated for its spectacular natural scenery of high mountains, multi-hued lakes, and cascading waterfalls, Jiuzhaigou Valley is an important habitat for rare and endangered flora and fauna.

Standard.cn: 九寨沟以其秀丽的景色和壮丽的风景而闻名。众多湖泊、瀑布和石灰岩梯田构成了如梦似幻的景观，清澈见底、富含矿物质的湖水，坐落在壮丽的高山之中，拥有高度多样化的森林生态系统，展现出非凡的自然美景。
Standard.en: Jiuzhaigou is renowned for its stunning scenery and majestic landscapes. Numerous lakes, waterfalls, and limestone terraces create a dreamlike landscape. The crystal-clear, mineral-rich lakes, nestled amidst magnificent mountains, boast a highly diverse forest ecosystem, showcasing extraordinary natural beauty.

Description.cn: 九寨沟风景名胜区是一处自然风光绝美的保护区，拥有壮丽的锯齿状高山，耸立于针叶林之上，环绕着如梦似幻的仙境般景色：清澈见底、色彩斑斓的蓝、绿、紫水潭、湖泊、瀑布、石灰岩梯田、溶洞等众多美景尽收眼底。这里喀斯特地貌丰富多样，堪称高山喀斯特水文研究的“天然 博物馆” 。九寨沟位于四川省北部，占地7.2万公顷，保存着一系列重要的森林生态系统，包括为大熊猫、羚牛等众多濒危动植物提供重要栖息地的原始森林。九寨沟南麓岷山山脉最高峰达4752米，还拥有大量保存完好的第四纪冰川遗迹，极具观赏价值。
Description.en: The Jiuzhaigou Valley Scenic and Historic Interest Area is a reserve of exceptional natural beauty with spectacular jagged alpine mountains soaring above coniferous forest around a fairyland landscape of crystal clear, strange-coloured blue, green and purplish pools, lakes, waterfalls, limestone terraces, caves and other beautiful features. These include a number of karst formations; indeed the area is a 'natural museum' for alpine karst hydrology and research. Covering 72,000 ha in the northern part of Sichuan Province, Jiuzhaigou preserves a series of important forest ecosystems including old-growth forests which provide important habitat for numerous threatened species of plants and animals, including the giant panda and takin. Attaining heights of 4,752 m in the southern Minshan Mountains, Jiuzhaigou also contains an important number of well-preserved quaternary glacial remnants with great scenic value.

Name.cn: 中国黄（渤）海候鸟栖息地（第二期）
Name.en: Migratory Bird Sanctuaries along the Coast of Yellow Sea-Bohai Gulf of China

History_background.cn: 2019年和2024年列入世界遗产名录
History_background.en: Inscribed on the World Heritage List in 2019 and 2024.

Main_function.cn: 为迁徙候鸟提供栖息地
Main_function.en: Provide habitat for migratory birds

Brief_intro.cn: 世界最大潮间带湿地系统之一，是东亚-澳大利亚迁徙路线候鸟的重要停歇地和枢纽。
Brief_intro.en: One of the world's largest intertidal wetland systems, this site is a critical stopover and staging area for migratory birds on the East Asian-Australasian Flyway.

Standard.cn: 中国黄海-渤海湾沿岸的候鸟保护区栖息着400多种鸟类。该保护区的潮滩对世界候鸟的保护具有极其重要的意义，为众多具有国际重要性的候鸟物种（包括全球濒危物种）提供了栖息地。仅江苏盐城南部和北部的候鸟栖息地就对超过10%的东亚-澳大利亚迁徙路线种群至关重要，并为世界上两种最稀有的候鸟——勺嘴鹬和诺氏鹬——提供了关键栖息地，这两种鸟类的生存都依赖于潮滩。中国渤海湾和黄海沿岸候鸟保护区内的湿地发挥着独特的生态功能，它们是候鸟迁徙途中不可或缺的停歇地和中转站，为候鸟提供必要的食物资源，确保它们在南北迁徙过程中补充脂肪，为后续飞行做好准备。如果没有这些重要的枢纽，候鸟的迁徙、繁殖和种群维持都将无法实现。除了为候鸟提供停歇栖息地外，这些湿地还为至少45种濒危鸟类（包括滨鸟、水禽和猛禽）提供越冬地和繁殖地。
Standard.en: The migratory bird reserves along the Yellow Sea and Bohai Bay coast of China are home to more than 400 bird species. The tidal flats of these reserves are of paramount importance for the conservation of migratory birds worldwide, providing habitat for numerous internationally important migratory bird species, including globally endangered ones. The migratory bird habitats in southern and northern Yancheng, Jiangsu Province alone are crucial to more than 10% of the populations along the East Asian-Australasian Flyway and provide critical habitat for two of the world's rarest migratory birds—the Spoon-billed Sandpiper and the Northwestern Sandpiper—both of which depend on the tidal flats for survival. The wetlands within the migratory bird reserves along the Bohai Bay and Yellow Sea coasts of China play a unique ecological role, serving as indispensable stopover and transit points for migratory birds, providing them with essential food resources to replenish their fat reserves during their north-south migrations and prepare them for subsequent flights. Without these vital hubs, migratory bird migration, breeding, and population maintenance would be impossible. In addition to providing stopover habitats for migratory birds, these wetlands also provide wintering and breeding grounds for at least 45 endangered bird species, including shorebirds, waterfowl, and birds of prey.

Description.cn: 位于中国黄海-渤海湾沿岸的候鸟保护区，通过分阶段提名程序的第一阶段（2019年）和第二阶段（2024年）列入世界遗产名录，坐落于世界上最大的潮间带湿地系统，也是生物多样性最丰富的湿地系统之一。该保护区位于黄海生态区，为沿东亚-澳大利亚迁徙路线迁徙的候鸟提供至关重要的栖息地，其湿地在候鸟南北迁徙过程中发挥着独特的生态功能，是不可或缺的停歇地和中转站。黄海和渤海湾是数百万候鸟迁徙的瓶颈，占东亚-澳大利亚迁徙路线候鸟总数的10%以上。因此，该遗产地是沿东亚-澳大利亚迁徙路线迁徙的鸟类不可替代且不可或缺的枢纽。这条迁徙路线不仅横跨黄海内的中国、朝鲜和韩国，还延伸至横跨两半球的约22个国家，从北极到东南亚和大洋洲。更广阔的沿海地区具有重要的全球意义，这一点可以从多个拉姆萨尔湿地名录中得到印证，其中一些湿地与该遗产地的部分区域完全或部分重叠。因此，该遗产地是候鸟所体现的全球共享自然遗产的典范。该遗产地由十二个组成部分构成，位于中国黄海沿岸，包括渤海湾，总面积为289,710.94公顷，另有117,502.10公顷的缓冲区。鉴于人类活动已改变该地区许多潮汐湿地，因此需要采取有效措施遏制主要威胁，恢复重要的候鸟栖息地，并进一步进行国家和跨国系列提名和/或扩展，以加强遗产地的完整性。
Description.en: The Migratory Bird Sanctuaries along the Coast of the Yellow Sea-Bohai Gulf of China, inscribed through Phase I (2019) and Phase II (2024) of a phased nomination process, are situated in the largest intertidal wetland system in the world and one of the most biologically diverse. The property is located in the Yellow Sea Ecoregion, and supports crucial habitats for birds migrating along the East Asian-Australasian Flyway, its wetlands serving a unique ecological function as indispensable stopover and staging sites during northward/southward migration. The Yellow Sea and the Gulf of Bohai are a bottleneck for many millions of migratory waterbirds – more than 10% of the total migration along the East Asian-Australasian Flyway. The property is thus an irreplaceable and indispensable hub for birds migrating along the East Asian-Australasian Flyway, which spans not only China, Democratic People’s Republic of Korea and the Republic of Korea, within the Yellow Sea, but also some 22 countries across two hemispheres from the Arctic to South-East Asia and Australasia. The global importance of the wider coastal area is evidenced by several Ramsar sites, some of which fully or partially overlap with component parts of the property. Thus, this property is a globally significant example of the shared natural heritage embodied in migratory birds.The twelve component parts of the property are located along the Yellow Sea coast of China, including the Bohai Gulf, with a total area of 289,710.94 ha, and a buffer zone of 117,502.10 ha. In light of the fact that human activity has transformed many of the region’s tidal wetlands, there is a need for effective measures to halt major threats and restore key migratory bird habitats, and for further national and transnational serial nominations, and/or extensions to strengthen the integrity of the property.

History_background.cn: none
History_background.en: none

Main_function.cn: 自然景观保护与展示
Main_function.en: Natural landscape protection and display

Brief_intro.cn: 以奇特的花岗岩地貌和茂密森林为特色，展现壮丽景观。
Brief_intro.en: Distinguished by its extraordinary granite landforms and dense forests, Mount Sanqingshan National Park presents a landscape of remarkable grandeur.

Standard.cn: 卓越的自然现象或自然美景：三青山奇特的花岗岩地貌与多样的森林、近景和远景以及引人注目的气象作用相结合，造就了风景秀丽的景观。其中最引人注目的是形态各异的石柱和山峰的密集分布。三青山的自然美景也源于花岗岩地貌与山地植被的交相辉映，以及气象条件的造化，共同营造出变幻莫测、引人入胜的景观。公园内架设的悬空步道使游客能够欣赏到公园的壮丽景色，并享受其宁静祥和的氛围。
Standard.en: Exceptional natural phenomena and scenery: The unique granite landforms of Sanqingshan, combined with diverse forests, foreground and background views, and remarkable meteorological effects, create a stunning landscape. Among the most striking features are the dense distribution of stone pillars and peaks of various shapes. The natural beauty of Sanqingshan also stems from the interplay between the granite landforms and mountain vegetation, as well as the influence of meteorological conditions, all contributing to a constantly changing and captivating landscape. Suspended walkways within the park allow visitors to appreciate its magnificent scenery and enjoy its tranquil atmosphere.

Description.cn: 三青山国家公园在相对较小的区域内，集中展现了形态奇特、森林茂密的岩石柱和山峰，构成了一幅独特的画卷。巍峨险峻、错综复杂的岩石地貌与葱郁的森林交相辉映，再加上变幻莫测的气候，共同造就了令人叹为观止的壮丽景观。
Description.en: Mount Sanqingshan National Park displays a unique array of forested, fantastically shaped granite pillars and peaks concentrated in a relatively small area. The looming, intricate rock formations intermixed with delicate forest cover and combined with ever-shifting weather patterns create a landscape of arresting beauty.

City.cn: 青海省玉树藏族自治州
City.en: Yushu Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Qinghai Province

History_background.cn: 地质演化形成高原与盆地
History_background.en: Geological evolution formed plateaus and basins

Main_function.cn: 自然保护区，保护生物多样性
Main_function.en: Nature reserves protect biodiversity.

Brief_intro.cn: 世界第三极，拥有丰富的高原湖泊、草甸和独特生态系统，是藏羚羊等特有动物的重要栖息地。
Brief_intro.en: Known as the world's third pole, the Hoh Xil plateau is home to abundant alpine lakes, meadows, and unique ecosystems, providing critical habitat for the Tibetan antelope and other endemic species.

Standard.cn: 青海可可西里位于世界最大、最高、最年轻的青藏高原上。这里景色壮丽，令人叹为观止，人类的感知空间被远远超越，感官体验也因此得到极大的提升。尺度对比是可可西里反复出现的主题：高原生态系统在宏大的尺度上不受阻碍地运转，野生动植物与广袤无垠的无树背景形成鲜明对比，矮小的垫状植物与巍峨的雪山交相辉映。夏季，这些矮小的垫状植物汇聚成一片绿海，盛开时更是色彩斑斓，波光粼粼。在雪山脚下的温泉周围，尘土、火山灰和硫磺的气味与来自冰川的凛冽寒风交织在一起。冰川融水形成无数条辫状河，这些河流交织成巨大的湿地系统，造就了数万个色彩斑斓、形状各异的湖泊。湖盆地地势平坦开阔，拥有青藏高原保存最完好的夷平面，以及数量空前的湖泊群。这些湖泊展现了完整的演替阶段，构成了长江源头的重要集水区，并造就了壮丽的景观。湖盆地也是藏羚羊的主要产仔地。每年初夏，数万只雌性藏羚羊从西部的羌塘、北部的阿尔金山脉和东部的三江源越冬地迁徙数百公里，来到可可西里湖盆地产仔。该保护区保护了三江源至可可西里之间的完整藏羚羊迁徙路线，保障了藏羚羊——青藏高原特有的濒危大型哺乳动物之一——的畅通迁徙。
Standard.en: Located on the world's largest, highest, and youngest Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, Hoh Xil in Qinghai Province boasts breathtaking scenery that transcends human perception, greatly enhancing the sensory experience. Scale contrast is a recurring theme in Hoh Xil: the plateau ecosystem operates unhindered on a grand scale, with wild flora and fauna contrasting sharply against the vast, treeless backdrop, and low-lying cushion plants complementing the majestic snow-capped mountains. In summer, these low-lying cushion plants converge into a green sea, bursting with vibrant colors and shimmering light when in full bloom. Around the hot springs at the foot of the snow-capped mountains, the smells of dust, volcanic ash, and sulfur mingle with the biting winds from the glaciers. Glacial meltwater forms countless braided rivers, which intertwine to create a vast wetland system, giving rise to tens of thousands of colorful and uniquely shaped lakes. The lake basins are flat and expansive, possessing the best-preserved peneplains on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and an unprecedented number of lakes. These lakes showcase complete successional stages, forming an important catchment area at the source of the Yangtze River and creating a magnificent landscape. The lake basin is also a major calving ground for Tibetan antelopes. Every early summer, tens of thousands of female Tibetan antelopes migrate hundreds of kilometers from their wintering grounds in the Qiangtang region to the west, the Altun Mountains to the north, and the Three Rivers Source Region to the east, arriving in the Hoh Xil lake basin to give birth. This reserve protects the complete Tibetan antelope migration route between the Three Rivers Source Region and Hoh Xil, ensuring the smooth migration of the Tibetan antelope—one of the endangered large mammals unique to the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau.

Standard.cn: 该保护区植物区系中高度的特有性与高海拔和寒冷气候相关，并促成了动物区系中同样高度的特有性。高山草甸占保护区总植被的45%，以紫针茅（Stipa purpurea）为主。其他植被类型包括高山草甸和高山碎石坡。保护区内超过三分之一的高等植物为青藏高原特有种，所有以这些植物为食的草食性哺乳动物也均为青藏高原特有种。可可西里保护区共有74种脊椎动物，包括19种哺乳动物、48种鸟类、6种鱼类和1种爬行动物（非洲鬣蜥）。保护区内栖息着藏羚羊、牦牛、藏野驴、藏瞪羚、狼和棕熊，这些动物均较为常见。大量野生有蹄类动物依赖于这片保护区，其中包括全球近40%的藏羚羊和高达50%的野生牦牛。可可西里保护区保护着藏羚羊完整生命周期的栖息地和自然过程，包括雌性藏羚羊长途迁徙后聚集产仔的现象。可可西里的产仔地每​​年可容纳多达3万头藏羚羊，几乎占整个藏羚羊分布范围内已确定产仔聚集区的80%。冬季，约有4万头藏羚羊留在保护区内，占全球藏羚羊总数的20%至40%。
Standard.en: The high degree of endemicity in the flora of this reserve is associated with high altitude and a cold climate, contributing to a similarly high degree of endemicity in its fauna. Alpine meadows comprise 45% of the reserve's total vegetation, dominated by *Stipa purpurea*. Other vegetation types include alpine meadows and alpine scree slopes. More than one-third of the higher plants in the reserve are endemic to the Tibetan Plateau, and all herbivorous mammals that feed on these plants are also endemic to the Tibetan Plateau. The Hoh Xil Nature Reserve is home to 74 vertebrate species, including 19 mammal species, 48 ​​bird species, 6 fish species, and 1 reptile species (African iguana). Tibetan antelope, yak, Tibetan wild ass, Tibetan gazelle, wolf, and brown bear are common in the reserve. A large number of wild ungulates depend on this reserve, including nearly 40% of the world's Tibetan antelope and up to 50% of the world's wild yak. The Hoh Xil Nature Reserve protects the habitat and natural processes of the Tibetan antelope throughout its entire life cycle, including the phenomenon of females gathering to give birth after their long migrations. The calving grounds in Hoh Xil can accommodate up to 30,000 Tibetan antelopes annually, accounting for almost 80% of the identified calving areas within the entire Tibetan antelope distribution range. During the winter, approximately 40,000 Tibetan antelopes remain in the reserve, representing 20% ​​to 40% of the global Tibetan antelope population.

Description.cn: 青海可可西里位于广袤的青藏高原东北角，青藏高原是世界上面积最大、海拔最高、最年轻的高原。该矿区占地3,735,632公顷，另有2,290,904公顷的缓冲区，涵盖了海拔4,500米以上的大片高山和草原地带。可可西里有时被称为世界“第三极”，拥有严寒的高原气候，全年平均气温低于零度，最低气温有时可达零下45摄氏度。随着地质构造的不断演化，该矿区在青藏高原上形成了一片广阔的夷平面和盆地。这里是高原上湖泊最密集的区域，展现出高海拔地区极其丰富的湖盆和内陆湖泊景观。壮丽的景色和震撼的视觉冲击力，使这片荒凉而人烟稀少的自然景观仿佛时间在此凝固。然而，这里却展现了不断变化的地貌和生态系统。该保护区独特的地理构造和气候条件孕育了同样独特的生物多样性。超过三分之一的植物物种以及所有依赖这些植物的草食性哺乳动物均为青藏高原特有种，而哺乳动物物种总数的60%也是青藏高原特有种。环绕可可西里湖盆的寒冷高寒草甸是来自青藏高原各地的藏羚羊的主要产仔地，并支撑着重要的迁徙路线。该保护区包含了一条从三江源到可可西的完整迁徙路线。尽管这条路线穿越青藏公路和铁路，面临诸多挑战，但它仍然是目前已知的所有藏羚羊迁徙路线中保护最为完善的。由于交通不便和气候恶劣，这片土地免受现代人类活动和开发的影响，同时也维持着一种与自然保护相辅相成的悠久传统放牧制度。然而，这片被誉为“世界第三极”的土地似乎正遭受全球气候变化的影响，气温异常升高，降水模式也发生了改变。这里的生态系统和地理景观对这种变化极其敏感，必须控制外部威胁，才能使生态系统适应环境变化。
Description.en: Qinghai Hoh Xil is located in the northeast corner of the vast Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau, the largest, highest and youngest plateau in the world. The property covers 3,735,632 ha with a 2,290,904 ha buffer zone and encompasses an extensive area of alpine mountains and steppe systems at elevations of over 4,500 m above sea level. Sometimes referred to as the world’s “Third Pole”, Hoh Xil has a frigid plateau climate, with sub-zero average year-round temperatures and the lowest temperature occasionally reaching -45°C. With its ongoing processes of geological formation, the property includes a large planation surface and basin on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. It is the area with the highest concentration of lakes on the Plateau, exhibiting an exceptional diversity of lake basins and inland lacustrine landscapes at high altitude. With its sweeping vistas and stunning visual impact, this harsh and uninhabited wild landscape seems like a place frozen in time. Yet it is a place that illustrates continually changing geomorphological and ecological systems.The unique geographical formation and climatic conditions of the property nurture a similarly unique biodiversity. More than one third of the plant species, and all the herbivorous mammals dependent on them are endemic to the plateau, and 60% of the mammal species as a whole are plateau endemics. The frigid alpine grasslands and meadows surrounding Hoh Xil's lake basins are the main calving grounds for populations of Tibetan antelope from across the plateau and support critical migration patterns. The property includes a complete migration route from Sanjiangyuan to Hoh Xii. This route, despite being challenged by crossing the Qinghai-Tibet Highway and Railway, is the best protected among all migration routes of Tibetan antelope known today.Inaccessibility and the harsh climate have combined to keep the property free from modern human influences and development while at the same time supporting a long-standing traditional grazing regime that coexists with the conservation of nature. Nevertheless, this 'Third Pole' of the world appears to be suffering from the impact of global climate change with disproportionally warming temperatures and changing precipitation patterns. The ecosystems and geographic landscapes are extremely sensitive to such a change and external threats need to be controlled to allow ecosystems to adapt to environmental change.

Name.en: Sichuan Giant Panda Sanctuaries - Wolong, Mt Siguniang and Jiajin Mountains

History_background.cn: 因大熊猫保护的重要性而闻名
History_background.en: Renowned for the importance of giant panda conservation

Main_function.cn: 大熊猫及珍稀物种保护
Main_function.en: Giant panda and rare species protection

BUilding_use.cn: 自然保护区和风景名胜区

Brief_intro.cn: 全球最大且最重要的大熊猫栖息地，拥有丰富的动植物多样性，是许多濒危和特有物种的重要保护地。
Brief_intro.en: The largest and most important giant panda habitat in the world, these sanctuaries harbor exceptional biodiversity and serve as a vital refuge for numerous endangered and endemic species.

Standard.cn: 四川大熊猫保护区拥有全球超过30%的大熊猫种群，是目前世界上面积最大、最重要的连片大熊猫栖息地。它是建立圈养繁殖种群最重要的种源地。该保护区也是温带地区乃至热带雨林以外地区植物种类最丰富的地区之一。其卓越价值在于保护了多样的地形、地质以及动植物物种。该保护区对生物多样性保护具有非凡价值，并能展示生态系统管理系统如何在国家和省级保护区之间有效运作。
Standard.en: The Sichuan Giant Panda Nature Reserve is home to over 30% of the world's giant panda population and is currently the world's largest and most important contiguous giant panda habitat. It is a crucial source area for establishing captive breeding populations. The reserve also boasts one of the richest plant species diversity outside of temperate zones and even tropical rainforests. Its exceptional value lies in protecting diverse topography, geology, and flora and fauna. The reserve holds extraordinary value for biodiversity conservation and demonstrates how ecosystem management systems can effectively operate between national and provincial protected areas.

Description.cn: 四川大熊猫保护区——卧龙、四姑娘山和嘉金山——因其对大熊猫保护的重要性而闻名遐迩，被誉为中国的“国宝”和全球大熊猫保护的旗舰。该保护区是中国乃至全世界现存最大、最重要的连片大熊猫栖息地，也是建立圈养繁殖种群最重要的种源地。除了大熊猫之外，该保护区还拥有大量特有和濒危动植物物种，包括其他标志性哺乳动物，例如小熊猫、雪豹和云豹，已记录的哺乳动物种类达109种（占中国哺乳动物总数的20%以上）。该保护区是某些鸟类特有种的重要中心，已记录到365种鸟类，其中300种在当地繁殖。然而，该保护区对植物而言尤为重要，是世界上温带地区植物种类最丰富的地区之一，已记录到约5000至6000种植物。许多物种是孑遗物种，例如鸽子树，而且在木兰、竹子、杜鹃花和兰花等类群中也存在着显著的多样性。该保护区是数百种传统药用植物的重要来源和基因库，其中许多植物目前正面临威胁。该遗产地位于中国东南部的四川省，地处成都高原和青藏高原之间的邛崃山和嘉金山地带，包括四个地级市的七个自然保护区和十一个风景名胜区，总面积达924,500公顷，另有527,100公顷的缓冲区。
Description.en: Sichuan Giant Panda Sanctuaries - Wolong, Mt Siguniang and Jiajin Mountains is principally renowned for its importance for the conservation of the giant panda, recognized as a “National Treasure” in China and as a flagship for global conservation efforts. The property is the largest and most significant remaining contiguous area of panda habitat in China and thus the world. It is also the most important source of giant panda for establishing the captive breeding population of the species.In addition to the giant panda, the property features a great number of endemic and threatened species of plants and animals, including other iconic mammal species such as the red panda, snow leopard and clouded leopard among the 109 species of mammals recorded (more than 20% of all Chinese mammals). The property is an important centre of endemism for some bird taxa with 365 bird species recorded, 300 of which breed locally. However the property is particularly important for flora, being one of the botanically richest sites of any temperate region in the world with some 5,000 – 6,000 species recorded. Many species are relicts, such as the dove tree, and there is significant diversity in groups such as magnolias, bamboos, rhododendrons, and orchids. The property is a major source and gene pool for hundreds of traditional medicinal plants, many now under threat.Located in China’s southeast province of Sichuan in the Qionglai and Jiajin Mountains between the Chengdu Plateau and the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau, the property includes seven nature reserves and eleven scenic parks in four prefectures or cities. It covers a total area of 924,500 ha surrounded by a buffer zone of 527,100 ha.

History_background.cn: 分两期列入世界遗产名录
History_background.en: Inscribed on the World Heritage List in two phases

Main_function.cn: 保护典型喀斯特地貌遗产
Main_function.en: Protect typical karst landform heritage

Brief_intro.cn: 世界上最壮观的湿润热带至亚热带喀斯特地貌之一，包含了多种重要的喀斯特地貌类型以及其他壮观的特征如天然桥梁、峡谷和大型洞穴系统，横跨四省，形成了独特而美丽的景观。
Brief_intro.en: One of the world's most spectacular examples of humid tropical to subtropical karst terrain, spanning four provinces, the South China Karst encompasses diverse karst landform types as well as dramatic natural bridges, gorges, and extensive cave systems, forming a landscape of exceptional beauty.

Standard.cn: 华南喀斯特世界遗产地包含壮观的喀斯特地貌特征和景观，这些特征和景观既是罕见的自然现象，又具有卓越的美学价值。其中包括石林石林，以及由白云石灰岩构成的奈古石林和湖泊中形成的苏依山石林等杰出的自然奇观；荔波的峰丛和峰林喀斯特地貌；以及武隆喀斯特，其特征包括被称为天坑的巨大塌陷洼地，洼地之间架设着异常高耸的天然桥梁，以及绵延的深邃无顶洞穴。
Standard.en: The South China Karst World Heritage Site encompasses spectacular karst landforms and landscapes that are both rare natural phenomena and possess exceptional aesthetic value. These include the Stone Forest, the Naigu Stone Forest composed of dolomite limestone, and the Suyishan Stone Forest formed in a lake, among other outstanding natural wonders; the peak clusters and peak forests of Libo; and the Wulong Karst, characterized by massive sinkholes known as tiankengs (sinkholes) with exceptionally high natural bridges connecting them, as well as sprawling, deep, roofless caves.

Standard.cn: 华南喀斯特世界遗产地展现了世界上最杰出的景观之一——喀斯特地貌复杂演化的历史。石林和荔波是喀斯特地貌特征的全球标杆区域。石林的石林历经2.7亿年，跨越了从二叠纪至今的四个主要地质时期，展现了喀斯特地貌演化的阶段性特征。荔波拥有不同年代的碳酸盐岩露头，经数百万年的侵蚀作用，形成了壮观的风丛和风林喀斯特地貌。荔波还包含众多高耸的喀斯特山峰、深邃的落水洞、沉陷的溪流和绵长的河洞。武隆代表了经历了显著隆升的内陆高地喀斯特高原，拥有巨大的落水洞和桥状地貌。武隆的地貌蕴含着世界著名河流系统之一——长江及其支流的历史遗迹。环江喀斯特是荔波喀斯特的延伸部分。这两个遗址共同构成了峰丛喀斯特地貌的杰出范例，并保存和展示了丰富多样的地表和地下喀斯特地貌特征。
Standard.en: The South China Karst World Heritage Site showcases one of the world's most outstanding landscapes—the complex evolutionary history of karst landforms. Shilin and Libo are global benchmark areas for karst landform characteristics. Shilin's stone forest, spanning 270 million years and four major geological periods from the Permian to the present, demonstrates the phased characteristics of karst landform evolution. Libo boasts outcrops of carbonate rocks from different eras, sculpted over millions of years by erosion into spectacular wind-blown forests and aeolian karst landforms. Libo also contains numerous towering karst peaks, deep sinkholes, submerged streams, and long river caves. Wulong represents a significantly uplifted inland karst plateau, featuring enormous sinkholes and bridge-like landforms. Wulong's landforms contain historical relics of one of the world's most famous river systems—the Yangtze River and its tributaries. Huanjiang Karst is an extension of Libo Karst. These two sites together constitute an outstanding example of peak-cluster karst landforms, and preserve and display a rich variety of surface and underground karst landform features.

Description.cn: 华南喀斯特地貌区面积约55万平方公​​里。该区域喀斯特地貌呈现出明显的地貌过渡特征，从西部的云贵高原（平均海拔2100米）到东部的广西盆地（平均海拔110米），地势在700公里内逐渐下降约2000米。该地区被公认为是世界湿润热带和亚热带喀斯特地貌发育的典型代表区。 华南喀斯特世界遗产地是一系列遗产，包括横跨四个省份的七个喀斯特地貌群：石林喀斯特、荔波喀斯特、武隆喀斯特、桂林喀斯特、石兵喀斯特、金佛山喀斯特和环江喀斯特。总面积97125公顷，缓冲区面积176228公顷。该遗产地分两期列入世界遗产名录。 第一期于2007年列入世界遗产名录，包括三个区域群，总面积47,588公顷，缓冲区总面积98,428公顷。石林喀斯特地貌位于云南省，拥有石林和雕刻般的尖峰状岩柱，被认为是世界尖峰喀斯特地貌的标杆地貌。石林喀斯特地貌由两个核心区和一片公共缓冲区组成，面积12,070公顷，缓冲区面积22,930公顷。缓冲区已被指定为联合国教科文组织地质公园。荔波喀斯特地貌位于贵州省，拥有高耸的锥形喀斯特山峰、其间深邃的封闭洼地（洞窟）、下沉溪流和漫长的地下洞穴。该地貌被认为是世界锥形喀斯特地貌的标杆地貌。该地貌由两个核心区和一片公共缓冲区组成。该区域总面积为29,518公顷，缓冲区面积为43,498公顷。其中一个组成部分是国家级自然保护区。武隆喀斯特部分位于重庆市，由地势较高的内陆喀斯特高原组成，经历了显著的地壳抬升。其巨大的落水洞和天坑桥是华南地区典型的天坑地貌，为世界著名河流系统之一——长江及其支流的历史提供了佐证。武隆喀斯特部分由三个核心区组成，每个核心区都设有独立的缓冲区。核心区总面积为6,000公顷，缓冲区总面积为32,000公顷。 2014年列入名录的第二期桂林喀斯特地貌单元包括四个区域，总面积49,537公顷，缓冲区总面积77,800公顷。桂林喀斯特单元位于广西丽江国家公园内，包含峰林和峰丛喀斯特地貌。桂林喀斯特分为葡萄段和丽江段。葡萄段面积2,840公顷，缓冲区面积21,610公顷；丽江段面积22,544公顷，缓冲区面积23,070公顷。石兵喀斯特单元位于贵州武阳河国家公园内，包含白云岩喀斯特地貌。石兵喀斯特面积10,280公顷，缓冲区面积18,015公顷。金佛山喀斯特地貌单元是一座独特的喀斯特台地山，四周环绕着高耸的悬崖峭壁。金佛山喀斯特地貌单元位于重庆市，地处金佛山国家级自然保护区和金佛山国家公园的范围内。金佛山单元面积为6744公顷，缓冲区面积为10675公顷。环江喀斯特地貌单元是一座锥形喀斯特地貌，位于广西壮族自治区木伦国家级自然保护区的范围内。环江单元面积为7129公顷，缓冲区面积为4430公顷。 华南喀斯特世界遗产地保护着一系列壮观且极具代表性的大陆喀斯特地貌，包括塔状喀斯特（峰林）、石林喀斯特（石林）和锥状喀斯特（峰丛），以及其他喀斯特地貌，例如天坑喀斯特（巨型落水洞）、桌山和峡谷。该遗产地还包含许多大型洞穴系统，其中蕴藏着丰富的洞穴沉积物。华南喀斯特的喀斯特地貌特征和地貌多样性被公认为世界最佳之一。该地区可被视为三种喀斯特地貌类型的全球典型代表：峰林（塔状喀斯特）、峰丛（锥状喀斯特）和石林（石林或石林）。此外，该地区还保留了大部分自然植被，使其呈现出季节性变化，并增添了其卓越的美学价值。 该遗产地囊括了华南地区从内陆高原到低地平原最壮观、最具科学意义和代表性的喀斯特地貌系列，是世界上湿润热带至亚热带喀斯特地貌的典范，也是地球上最伟大的景观之一。它与邻国（包括越南）的喀斯特地貌相得益彰，越南的多处世界遗产也展现了喀斯特地貌。
Description.en: The huge karst area of South China is about 550,000 km2 in extent. The karst terrain displays a geomorphic transition as the terrain gradually descends about 2000 meters over 700 kilometers from the western Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau (averaging 2100 meters elevation) to the eastern Guangxi Basin (averaging 110 meters elevation). The region is recognized as the world’s type area for karst landform development in the humid tropics and subtropics. The World Heritage Property of South China Karst is a serial property that includes seven karst clusters in four Provinces: Shilin Karst, Libo Karst, Wulong Karst, Guilin Karst, Shibing Karst, Jinfoshan Karst, and Huanjiang Karst. The total area is 97,125 hectares, with a buffer zone of 176,228 hectares. The property was inscribed in two phases. Phase I inscribed in 2007, include three clusters totalling 47,588 hectares, with buffer zones totalling 98,428 hectares. The Shilin Karst component is in Yunnan province and contains stone forests with sculpted pinnacle columns and is considered the world reference site for pinnacle karst. Shilin Karst consists of two core areas surrounded by a common buffer zone. The area is 12,070 hectares with a buffer zone of 22,930 hectares. The buffer zone is designated as a UNESCO Geopark. The Libo Karst component is in Guizhou province and includes high conical karst peaks, intervening deep enclosed depressions (cockpits), sinking streams and long underground caves. The area is considered a world reference site for cone karst. The property consists of two core areas surrounded by a common buffer. The area is 29,518 hectares with a buffer zone of 43,498 hectares. One of the components is a national nature reserve. The Wulong Karst component is in Chongqing province and consists of high inland karst plateaux that have experienced considerable uplift. Its giant dolines and bridges are representative of South China’s tiankeng (giant collapse depression) landscapes, and provide the evidence for the history of one of the world’s great river systems, the Yangtze and its tributaries. The Wulong Karst component is a cluster of three core zones, each with a separate buffer zone. The areas total 6,000 hectares with buffer zones of 32,000 hectares. Phase II inscribed in 2014 includes four clusters totaling 49,537 hectares, and buffer zones totaling 77,800 hectares. The Guilin Karst component in Guangxi province is located within Lijiang National Park and contains fenglin (tower) and fengcong (cone) karst formations. Guilin Karst is divided into two sections: the Putao Section with an area of 2,840 hectares and a buffer zone of 21,610 hectares and the Lijiang Section with an area of 22,544 hectares and a buffer zone of 23,070 hectares. The Shibing Karst component in Guizhou province includes dolomitic karst formations and is located within Wuyanghe National Park. Shibing Karst has an area of 10,280 hectares and a buffer zone of 18,015 hectares. The Jinfoshan Karst component is a unique karst table mountain surrounded by towering cliffs. Jinfoshan Karst is located in Chongqing province within the boundaries of the Jinfoshan National Nature Reserve and Jinfoshan National Park. The Jinfoshan component has an area of 6,744 hectares and a buffer zone of 10,675 hectares. The Huanjiang Karst component is a cone karst area located in Guangxi Province within the boundaries of the Mulun National Nature Reserve. The Huanjiang Component has an area of 7,129 hectares and a buffer zone of 4,430 hectares. The South China Karst World Heritage property protects a diversity of spectacular and iconic continental karst landscapes, including tower karst (fenglin), pinnacle karst (shilin) and cone karst (fengcong), as well as other karst phenomena such as Tiankeng karst (giant dolines), table mountains and gorges. The property also includes many large cave systems with rich speleothem deposits. The karst features and geomorphological diversity of the South China Karst are widely recognized as among the best in the world. The region can be considered the global type-site for three karst landform styles: fenglin (tower karst), fengcong (cone karst), and shilin (stone forest or pinnacle karst).The landscape also retains most of its natural vegetation, which results in seasonal variations and adds to the outstanding aesthetic value of the area. The property contains the most spectacular, scientifically significant and representative series of karst landforms and landscapes of South China from interior high plateau to lowland plains and constitutes the world’s premier example of humid tropical to subtropical karst: one of our planet’s great landscapes. It complements sites that are also present in neighbouring countries, including Viet Nam, where several World Heritage properties also exhibit karst formations.

Name.en: Three Parallel Rivers of Yunnan Protected Areas

History_background.cn: none
History_background.en: none

Main_function.cn: 自然遗产保护
Main_function.en: Natural Heritage Protection

Brief_intro.cn: 是中国生物多样性最丰富的地区, 涵盖了三大河流上游，拥有丰富地貌和生物多样性，是重要的自然遗产地。
Brief_intro.en: The most biologically diverse region in China, this protected area encompasses the upper reaches of three major rivers, featuring rich and varied landforms and extraordinary biodiversity, making it an outstanding natural heritage site.

Standard.cn: 金沙江、澜沧江和怒江三条河流的深邃平行峡谷是该遗产地最突出的自然特征；虽然这三条河流的大部分河段位于遗产地边界之外，但河谷景观仍然是该区域的主要景观元素。高山遍布，梅里雪山、白马雪山和哈巴雪山的冰川覆盖山峰构成了壮丽的天际线。明勇桥冰川是一处著名的自然奇观，它从川岳峰（海拔6740米）延伸至海拔2700米处，据称是北半球低纬度地区（北纬28°）下降到最低海拔的冰川。其他突出的景观地貌包括高山喀斯特地貌（特别是怒江峡上方月亮山风景区的“石月”）和高山丹霞的“龟甲”状风化地貌。
Standard.en: The deep, parallel canyons of the Jinsha, Lancang, and Nujiang rivers are the most prominent natural feature of this heritage site; although most of these rivers lie outside the site's boundaries, the valley landscape remains a dominant element of the area's scenery. High mountains abound, with glaciers covering the Meili, Baima, and Haba Snow Mountains creating a magnificent skyline. The Mingyongqiao Glacier, a renowned natural wonder, extends from Chuanyue Peak (6740 meters) to 2700 meters, reportedly the lowest-altitude glacier in the low latitudes of the Northern Hemisphere (28°N). Other prominent landforms include alpine karst topography (particularly the "Stone Moon" in the Moon Mountain scenic area above the Nujiang Gorge) and the "tortoise shell" weathered landforms of alpine Danxia landforms.

Standard.cn: 该地块具有卓越的价值，展现了过去五千万年来与印度板块与欧亚板块碰撞、古特提斯海闭合以及喜马拉雅山脉和青藏高原隆升相关的地质历史。这些是亚洲地表演化过程中的重大地质事件，并且至今仍在持续。地块内多种多样的岩石类型记录了这段历史，此外，高山带的喀斯特地貌、花岗岩巨石和丹霞砂岩地貌也堪称世界山地地貌中的佼佼者。
Standard.en: This block is of exceptional value, showcasing the geological history of the past 50 million years related to the collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates, the closure of the Paleo-Tethys Sea, and the uplift of the Himalayas and the Tibetan Plateau. These are major geological events in the evolution of Asia, and their effects continue to this day. The diverse rock types within the block record this history; furthermore, its alpine karst landforms, granite megaliths, and Danxia sandstone formations are among the best in the world.

Standard.cn: 三条平行河流区域生态过程的显著表现是地质、气候和地形等多种因素共同作用的结果。首先，该区域位于活跃的地形带内，因此拥有丰富的岩石基质，从火成岩（四种类型）到各种沉积岩，包括石灰岩、砂岩和砾岩。该区域地处板块碰撞点，因此地形特征极其多样，从峡谷到喀斯特地貌再到冰川覆盖的山峰，应有尽有。此外，该区域曾是更新世的避难所，并且位于生物地理汇聚带（即温带和热带气候特征交汇），所有这些因素共同造就了其生物多样性高度丰富的演化基础。除了地形地貌多样性（垂直落差近 6000 米）之外，季风气候影响着该地区的大部分区域，并提供了另一种有利的生态刺激，使得温带古北界生物群落得以全面发展。
Standard.en: The remarkable ecological processes in the region, characterized by three parallel rivers, are the result of the combined effects of multiple factors, including geology, climate, and topography. Firstly, the region lies within an active topographic zone, thus possessing a rich rock matrix, ranging from igneous rocks (four types) to various sedimentary rocks, including limestone, sandstone, and conglomerate. Located at a plate collision point, the region exhibits extremely diverse topographic features, from canyons to karst landforms to glacier-covered peaks. Furthermore, the region served as a Pleistocene refuge and lies within a biogeographical convergence zone (where temperate and tropical climate characteristics meet), all of which contribute to its highly biodiverse evolutionary foundation. In addition to the diverse topography (a vertical drop of nearly 6000 meters), the monsoon climate influences much of the region, providing another favorable ecological stimulus that allowed the temperate Palearctic biomes to flourish.

Standard.cn: 云南西北部是中国生物多样性最丰富的地区，也可能是地球上生物多样性最丰富的温带地区。该遗产地涵盖了横断山脉的大部分自然栖息地，而横断山脉是世界上现存最重要的生物多样性保护区域之一。遗产地地形和气候的显著多样性，以及其位于东亚、东南亚和青藏高原生物地理区域的交汇处，并作为动植物迁徙的南北走廊（尤其是在冰河时期），使其成为真正独特的景观，尽管经历了数千年的人类活动，仍然保留了高度的自然特征。作为众多珍稀濒危动植物最后的栖息地，该遗产地具有突出的普遍价值。
Standard.en: Northwestern Yunnan is one of the most biodiverse regions in China, and possibly the most biodiverse temperate region on Earth. This heritage site encompasses much of the natural habitat of the Hengduan Mountains, one of the world's most important surviving biodiversity conservation areas. The site's remarkable topographical and climatic diversity, its location at the crossroads of East Asian, Southeast Asian, and Tibetan Plateau biogeographical regions, and its role as a north-south corridor for flora and fauna migration (especially during the Ice Age), make it a truly unique landscape that has retained a high degree of natural character despite thousands of years of human activity. As the last refuge for numerous rare and endangered plants and animals, this heritage site possesses outstanding universal value.

Description.cn: 云南三江并流保护区位于中国云南省西北山区，是一个由15个保护区组成的自然序列遗产，分为8个保护区群。该遗产地拥有极其丰富的地貌景观，包括深邃的河谷、茂密的森林、巍峨的雪山、冰川、高山喀斯特地貌、红色的砂岩地貌（丹霞地貌）、以及绵延的湖泊和草甸。这片占地170万公顷的区域涵盖了亚洲三大河流——长江（金沙江）、湄公河和萨尔温江的上游部分河段，这三条河流大致平行，自北向南流淌，穿过陡峭的峡谷，部分河段深达3000米，两侧是海拔超过6000米的冰川覆盖的山峰。遗产地横跨横断山脉的大部分区域，横断山脉是从喜马拉雅山脉东端延伸至印度支那的主要弧形山脉。由于地处世界三大生物地理区域的交汇处，该遗产地位于中国生物多样性的中心地带，也可能蕴藏着丰富的生物多样性。世界温带地区生物多样性最丰富的地区。
Description.en: Located in the mountainous north-west of Yunnan Province in China, the Three Parallel Rivers of Yunnan Protected Areas is a natural serial property consisting of 15 protected areas, grouped into eight clusters. The Property contains an outstanding diversity of landscapes, such as deep-incised river gorges, luxuriant forests, towering snow-clad mountains, glaciers, and alpine karst, reddish sandstone landforms (Danxia）, lakes and meadows over vast vistas.
