The 1.7 million hectare site features sections of the upper reaches of three of the great rivers of Asia: the Yangtze (Jinsha), Mekong and Salween which run approximately parallel, north to south, through steep gorges which, in places, are 3,000 m deep and are bordered by glaciated peaks more than 6,000 m high. The property spans a large portion of the Hengduan Mountains, which is the major arc curving into Indochina from the eastern end of the Himalayas. Being located in the convergent regions of the three world's major biogeographic realms, the property is in an epicentre of Chinese biodiversity. It may also harbour the richest biodiversity among the temperate areas of the world.

Name.en: Wulingyuan Scenic and Historic Interest Area

History_background.cn: none
History_background.en: none

Main_function.cn: 自然保护与旅游观光
Main_function.en: Nature conservation and tourism

Brief_intro.cn: 拥有数量和样貌壮观的石英砂岩柱、天然桥、洞穴及丰富动植物，是重要的自然景区。
Brief_intro.en: Home to a spectacular array of quartzite sandstone pillars, natural bridges, caves, and diverse flora and fauna, Wulingyuan is an area of outstanding natural significance.

Standard.cn: 数量庞大的砂岩柱和山峰——超过3000座——蔚为壮观。这些山峰与天然桥梁、峡谷、瀑布、溪流、水潭和洞穴等其他地貌以及茂密的阔叶林交相辉映，构成了一幅美轮美奂的景观，而经常笼罩此地的薄雾和云雾更增添了它的魅力。这里有40多个洞穴和两座巨大的天然石桥，其中一座桥高出谷底357米。
Standard.en: The sheer number of sandstone pillars and peaks—over 3,000—is spectacular. These peaks, along with natural bridges, canyons, waterfalls, streams, pools, caves, and other landforms, as well as dense broad-leaved forests, create a breathtaking landscape, often shrouded in mist and clouds, adding to its allure. There are over 40 caves and two enormous natural stone bridges, one of which rises 357 meters above the valley floor.

Description.cn: 武陵源是人口稠密的农业区中的一片自然绿洲。这片位于中国湖南省的壮丽区域占地约26400公顷，以3000多根狭窄的石英砂岩柱为主，其中许多高达200多米。在这些巍峨的山峰之间，沟壑纵横，溪流潺潺，水潭飞流，瀑布飞流，还有两座巨大的天然桥和约40个洞穴。这些洞穴中令人叹为观止的方解石沉积是一大特色。除了令人叹为观止的自然景观，包括壮观的嶙峋山峰、茂盛的植被和清澈的湖泊溪流之外，该地区还是许多濒危动植物的家园
Description.en: Wulingyuan is an island of nature within a heavily populated agricultural region. A spectacular area stretching some 26,400ha in China’s Hunan Province, the site is dominated by more than 3,000 narrow quartz sandstone pillars, many over 200m high. Nestled within its towering peaks lie ravines and gorges with streams, pools and waterfalls, two large natural bridges, and some 40 caves. Impressive calcite deposits are a notable feature within these caves. In addition to the striking beauty of the landscape, including spectacular jagged stone peaks, luxuriant vegetation cover and clear lakes and streams, the region is also home to a number of endangered plant and animal species.

History_background.cn: none
History_background.en: none

Main_function.cn: 自然遗产保护与展示
Main_function.en: Natural Heritage Protection and Display

Brief_intro.cn: 是温带干旱区生物和生态演化过程的杰出范例，拥有丰富的自然景观和生物多样性，是温带干旱区生态演化的重要代表。
Brief_intro.en: An outstanding example of biological and ecological evolutionary processes in temperate arid regions, Xinjiang Tianshan possesses rich natural landscapes and biodiversity, and is a significant representative of ecological evolution in temperate dry-land environments.

Standard.cn: 天山是中亚一条绵延约2500公里的大型山脉，是世界温带干旱区最大的山脉，也是全球最大的孤立东西向山脉。新疆天山东西走向绵延1760公里，是一条自然风光秀丽的山脉。新疆天山西端以天山最高峰吐木尔峰（海拔7443米）为界，东端以博格达峰（海拔5445米）为界。该山脉位于中亚两大沙漠之间，北部是准噶尔沙漠，南部是塔里木沙漠。新疆天山的魅力不仅在于其壮丽的雪山和冰川覆盖的山峰、秀丽的森林和草甸、清澈的河流和湖泊以及红色的河床峡谷，更在于山地元素与广袤沙漠的交相辉映。南坡裸露的岩石与北坡茂密的森林和草地形成了鲜明的对比，造就了炎热与寒冷、干燥与潮湿、荒凉与繁茂的环境的鲜明视觉对比，也造就了非凡的美丽。
Standard.en: The Tian Shan Mountains are a large mountain range in Central Asia, stretching approximately 2,500 kilometers. It is the largest mountain range in the world's temperate arid zone and the world's largest isolated east-west mountain range. The Xinjiang Tian Shan range extends 1,760 kilometers east-west, a mountain range renowned for its stunning natural scenery. The western boundary of the Tian Shan is marked by its highest peak, Tumur Peak (7,443 meters), while the eastern boundary is marked by Bogda Peak (5,445 meters). This mountain range lies between two major deserts in Central Asia: the Junggar Desert to the north and the Tarim Desert to the south. The charm of the Xinjiang Tian Shan lies not only in its magnificent snow-capped mountains and glaciers, its beautiful forests and meadows, its clear rivers and lakes, and its red riverbed canyons, but also in the striking contrast between mountainous elements and the vast desert. The exposed rocks on the southern slopes contrast sharply with the dense forests and grasslands on the northern slopes, creating a striking visual contrast between heat and cold, dryness and humidity, barrenness and lushness, resulting in extraordinary beauty.

Standard.cn: 新疆天山是温带干旱区生物和生态演化过程的杰出范例。由于天山地处两大沙漠之间，且属于中亚干旱大陆性气候，其地貌和生态系统自上新世以来得以保存，这在世界山地生态系统中独树一帜。新疆天山具备温带干旱区所有典型的山地海拔带特征，反映了不同海拔、坡度和梯度上的水分和热量变化。该遗产地是研究全球气候变化背景下干旱区山地生态系统生物群落演替的杰出范例。新疆天山也是帕米尔-天山高原生物和生态演化的杰出代表。植被的海拔分布、南北坡的显著差异以及植物多样性，都体现了帕米尔-天山高原的生物和生态演化。该遗产地也是孑遗物种、众多珍稀濒危物种以及特有物种的重要栖息地。它代表了原本温暖潮湿的植物群落逐渐被现代干旱地中海植物群落所取代的过程。
Standard.en: The Tianshan Mountains in Xinjiang are an outstanding example of biological and ecological evolution in temperate arid regions. Located between two major deserts and situated in a Central Asian arid continental climate zone, the Tianshan's landforms and ecosystems have been preserved since the Pliocene, a unique feature among global mountain ecosystems. The Tianshan exhibits all the typical altitudinal characteristics of temperate arid mountains, reflecting variations in moisture and heat at different altitudes, slopes, and gradients. This heritage site is an outstanding example for studying the succession of biological communities in arid mountain ecosystems under the background of global climate change. The Tianshan is also a prominent representative of the biological and ecological evolution of the Pamir-Tianshan Plateau. The altitudinal distribution of vegetation, the significant differences between the north and south slopes, and plant diversity all reflect the biological and ecological evolution of the Pamir-Tianshan Plateau. This heritage site is also an important habitat for relict species, numerous rare and endangered species, and endemic species. It represents the process by which a originally warm and humid plant community was gradually replaced by a modern arid Mediterranean plant community.

Description.cn: 新疆天山是一个系列遗产地，由四个组成部分构成，总面积606,833公顷，缓冲区总面积491,103公顷，位于中华人民共和国新疆天山山脉东部。这四个组成部分沿新疆天山山脉绵延1,760公里，地处温带干旱区，周围环绕着中亚沙漠。该遗产地因其卓越的自然美景和优良的自然特征，以及涵盖多种生物和生态过程，符合世界遗产名录标准（vii）和（ix）。该遗产地拥有卓越的风景价值和众多绝佳的自然景观——从红色的峡谷到巍峨的山峰和冰川，再到美丽的湿地、草甸和草原。山区与广袤的中亚沙漠之间，以及干燥的南坡与湿润的北坡之间形成鲜明对比，更凸显了这些景观的视觉冲击力。新疆天山也是温带干旱地区生物和生态演化过程的杰出范例。植被的垂直分布、南北坡的显著差异以及植物群落的多样性，都展现了帕米尔-天山高原的生物和生态演化历程。新疆天山生物多样性丰富，是孑遗物种、众多珍稀濒危物种以及特有物种的重要栖息地。它完美地诠释了原始的温暖湿润植物群落如何逐渐被现代的耐旱地中海植物群落所取代。
Description.en: Xinjiang Tianshan is a serial property consisting of four components totaling 606,833 hectares, with buffer zones totaling 491,103 hectares located in the People’s Republic of China in the Xinjiang Tianshan, the eastern portion of the Tianshan mountain range. The four components are located along the 1,760 kilometers of the Xinjiang Tianshan, a temperate arid zone surrounded by Central Asian deserts. The property was nominated under criterion (vii) for its outstanding beauty and superlative natural features and criterion (ix) for capturing a range of biological and ecological processes.The property has outstanding scenic values and many superlative natural features – from red bed canyons to high peaks and glaciers to beautiful wetlands, meadows and steppe. The visual impact of these features is magnified by the stark contrasts between the mountain areas and vast Central Asian deserts, and between the dry south slopes and the much wetter north slope. Xinjiang Tianshan is also an outstanding example of ongoing biological and ecological evolutionary process in a temperate arid zone. Altitudinal vegetation distributions, significant differences between north and south slopes, and diversity of flora, all illustrate the biological and ecological evolution of the Pamir-Tian Shan Highlands. Xinjiang Tianshan has outstanding biodiversity and is important habitat for relic species, and numerous rare and endangered species, as well as endemic species. It provides an excellent example of the gradual replacement of the original warm and wet flora by modern xeric Mediterranean flora.

Name.en: Mount Emei Scenic Area, including Leshan Giant Buddha Scenic Area

History_background.cn: 佛教最早在中国扎根地之一
History_background.en: One of the earliest places where Buddhism took root in China

Main_function.cn: 佛教圣地与文化景观
Main_function.en: Buddhist holy sites and cultural landscapes

BUilding_use.en: Buddhist temples, Buddha statues and cultural relics

Brief_intro.cn: 中国佛教四大圣地之一，佛教在中国境内最早扎根的地方，也是佛教向东方广泛传播的源头。第一座寺庙修建于此
Brief_intro.en: One of the four sacred Buddhist mountains of China, Mount Emei is one of the earliest places where Buddhism took root in China and a source from which Buddhism spread widely to the East. The first Buddhist temple in China was built here.

Standard.cn: 峨眉山共有三十余座寺庙，其中十座规模宏大且历史悠久；这些寺庙风格传统，大多依山而建，充分利用了地形优势。从选址、设计到建造，它们都展现出极高的原创性和匠心独运。其先进的建筑技艺堪称中国寺庙建筑的精髓。
Standard.en: Mount Emei boasts over thirty temples, ten of which are grand in scale and steeped in history. These temples, built in traditional styles, are mostly nestled against the mountainside, making full use of the terrain. From site selection and design to construction, they all demonstrate exceptional originality and ingenuity. Their advanced architectural techniques represent the essence of Chinese temple architecture.

Standard.cn: 峨眉山最突出的特点是物质与非物质、自然与文化的联系。峨眉山是中国佛教四大圣地之一，具有重要的历史意义。佛教于公元1世纪经丝绸之路从印度传入中国，并在峨眉山上建造了中国第一座佛教寺庙。
Standard.en: The most prominent feature of Mount Emei is the connection between the material and the intangible, nature and culture. Mount Emei is one of the four sacred Buddhist sites in China and holds significant historical importance. Buddhism was introduced to China from India via the Silk Road in the 1st century AD, and the first Buddhist temple in China was built on Mount Emei.

Standard.cn: 峨眉山因其极高的植物多样性，在自然保护和科学研究方面具有特殊意义。该地区的生物多样性极其丰富：已记录到242科约3200种植物，其中31种为国家级保护植物，100多种为特有种。这得益于其位于四川盆地边缘和喜马拉雅山脉东麓的过渡地带。在其海拔2600米的范围内，分布着多种多样的植被带，包括亚热带常绿阔叶林、常绿阔叶混交林、阔叶针叶混交林和亚高山针叶林。除了这些独特的植物群落外，峨眉山的动物物种也十分丰富，已记录到约2300种动物，其中包括一些全球濒危物种。
Standard.en: Mount Emei holds special significance for nature conservation and scientific research due to its exceptionally high plant diversity. The region boasts incredibly rich biodiversity: approximately 3,200 plant species from 242 families have been recorded, including 31 nationally protected species and over 100 endemic species. This is thanks to its location in the transitional zone between the edge of the Sichuan Basin and the eastern foothills of the Himalayas. Within its 2,600-meter elevation range, diverse vegetation zones exist, including subtropical evergreen broad-leaved forests, evergreen broad-leaved mixed forests, broad-leaved and coniferous mixed forests, and subalpine coniferous forests. In addition to these unique plant communities, Mount Emei is also rich in animal species, with approximately 2,300 species recorded, including some globally endangered species.

Description.cn: 峨眉山具有极其重要的文化意义，它是佛教在中国境内最早扎根的地方，也是佛教向东方广泛传播的源头。中国第一座佛教寺庙建于公元1世纪，即广祥寺，并于1614年正式更名为华藏寺。此后，又陆续兴建了30多座寺庙，其中包括建于4世纪的万年寺（寺内供奉着10世纪的普贤铜佛，高7.85米）、清阴阁（由亭台楼阁组成，始建于6世纪初）、17世纪初的宝国寺以及梨沟园（伏虎寺）。这些建筑群使峨眉山成为佛教最神圣的圣地之一。其中最引人注目的便是高达71米的乐山大佛。这座大佛雕刻于公元8世纪，位于西觉峰山坡上，俯瞰三江交汇处，是世界上最大的佛教雕塑。一块碑文记载了大佛的建造过程。周边古迹包括建于9世纪的灵宝塔和清初的大佛寺。五予寺内有两尊重要的佛像：一尊建于9世纪的大石铜佛，以及一尊建于11世纪的阿弥陀佛铁鎏金像。玛昊岩上分布着五百多座公元1至4世纪的汉代墓葬，这些墓葬以其精美的雕刻和书法题记而闻名。峨眉山风景秀丽，令人叹为观止。同时，由于其在佛教传入中国过程中发挥了重要作用，峨眉山也具有重要的精神和文化意义。众多文化古迹，特别是传统建筑，与自然环境的巧妙融合，使其成为一处极具文化底蕴的景观。峨眉山以其极其丰富的植被而闻名，从亚热带常绿林到亚高山松林，种类繁多。该景区占地15400公顷，分为峨眉山和乐山大佛风景区两大区域，将自然美景与人文元素巧妙融合。
Description.en: Mount Emei (Emeishan) is an area of exceptional cultural significance as it is the place where Buddhism first became established on Chinese territory and from where it spread widely through the East. The first Buddhist temple in China was built on the summit of Mount Emei in the 1st century CE. It became the Guangxiang Temple, receiving its present royal name of Huazang in 1614. The addition of more than 30 other temples including the Wannian Temple founded in the 4th century containing the 7.85m high Puxian bronze Buddha of the 10th century, and garden temples including the Qingyin Pavilion complex of pavilions, towers and platforms dating from the early 6th century; the early 17th century Baoguo Temple and the Ligou Garden (Fuhu Temple) turned the mountain into one of Buddhism's holiest sites. The most remarkable manifestation of this is the 71 meter tall Giant Buddha of Leshan. Carved in the 8th century CE on the hillside of Xijuo Peak overlooking the confluence of three rivers, it is the largest Buddhist sculpture in the world. A contemporary account of the creation of the Giant Buddha is preserved in the form of an inscribed tablet. Associated monuments include the 9th century Lingbao Pagoda and the Dafo (Giant Buddha) Temple dating from the early Qing Dynasty. The Wuyu Temple contains two important statues: the 9th century Dashi bronze Buddha and the 11th century Amithabha statue group, cast in iron and gilded. Over five hundred Han Dynasty tombs of the 1st to 4th centuries, notable for their fine carvings and calligraphic inscriptions are located on Mahao Crag.Mount Emei is an area of striking scenic beauty. It is also of great spiritual and cultural importance because of its role in the introduction of Buddhism into China. The conscious siting of so many of the cultural monuments, particularly of traditional architecture, within the natural environment makes it a cultural landscape of very high order.Mount Emei is also notable for its exceptionally rich vegetation, ranging from subtropical evergreen forests to subalpine pine forests. Covering an area of 15,400 ha in two discrete areas – the Mount Emei and the Leshan Giant Buddha Scenic Areas – the property is an area of natural beauty into which the human element has been integrated with skill and subtlety.

History_background.cn: 唐代以来在中国艺术文学史上重要
History_background.en: Important in the history of Chinese art and literature since the Tang Dynasty

Main_function.cn: 自然风光观赏与植物保护
Main_function.en: Natural scenery appreciation and plant protection

Brief_intro.cn: 传说将其描述为发现长生不老药的地方，因壮丽山景和丰富植物著称，自唐代以来有重要历史地位，是中国著名旅游和艺术胜地。
Brief_intro.en: Described in legend as the place where the elixir of immortality was discovered, Huangshan is celebrated for its magnificent mountain scenery and diverse flora. Holding a distinguished place in history since the Tang dynasty, it has long been a celebrated destination for tourism and artistic inspiration in China.

Standard.cn: 黄山风景的文化价值最早于唐代进入中国人的视野，并一直备受推崇。公元747年，黄山被皇帝下令命名为黄山，此后吸引了众多游客，包括隐士、诗人、画家等，他们用绘画和诗歌赞颂黄山的壮丽景色，创造了具有世界意义的丰富艺术和文学作品。元代（1271-1368年）在黄山上修建了64座寺庙。1606年，僧人普门来到黄山，建造了法海禅寺。到了明代（约16世纪），黄山的景色已成为中国山水画家喜爱的题材，并由此形成了影响深远的山水画派。在如此秀丽的环境中展现人与自然的互动，激发了一代又一代中国艺术家和作家的创作灵感。
Standard.en: The cultural value of Huangshan's scenery first entered the Chinese consciousness during the Tang Dynasty and has remained highly regarded ever since. In 747 AD, the emperor officially named Huangshan, attracting numerous tourists, including hermits, poets, and painters who praised its magnificent scenery through paintings and poems, creating a wealth of artistic and literary works of global significance. During the Yuan Dynasty (1271-1368), 64 temples were built on Huangshan. In 1606, the monk Pumen arrived at Huangshan and built the Fahai Temple. By the Ming Dynasty (around the 16th century), Huangshan's scenery had become a favorite subject for Chinese landscape painters, leading to the formation of a far-reaching school of landscape painting. The interaction between humanity and nature within such a beautiful environment has inspired generations of Chinese artists and writers.

Standard.cn: 黄山以其壮丽的自然景观而闻名，其中包括巨大的花岗岩巨石和古老的松树，云雾缭绕更添其雄伟气势。这片壮丽的景观还包括天然石柱、奇形怪状的岩石、瀑布、溶洞、湖泊和温泉等，这些都是其复杂地质历史的产物。黄山拥有众多巍峨的山峰，其中77座海拔超过1000米，最高峰莲花峰海拔高达1864米。
Standard.en: Huangshan is renowned for its magnificent natural scenery, including massive granite boulders and ancient pine trees, all shrouded in mist and clouds, adding to its majestic grandeur. This magnificent landscape also includes natural stone pillars, strangely shaped rocks, waterfalls, caves, lakes, and hot springs—all products of its complex geological history. Huangshan boasts numerous towering peaks, 77 of which exceed 1000 meters in altitude, with the highest peak, Lotus Peak, reaching 1864 meters.

Standard.cn: 黄山为众多地方或国家特有植物物种提供了栖息地，其中一些物种在全球范围内受到威胁。其极其丰富的植物区系包含了中国三分之一的苔藓植物（包括藓类和地钱）和超过一半的蕨类植物。黄山特有物种包括13种蕨类植物和6种高等植物，此外还有许多其他物种是该地区或中国的特有物种。除了这些独特的植物区系外，黄山还拥有超过300种重要的脊椎动物，包括48种哺乳动物、170种鸟类、38种爬行动物、20种两栖动物和24种鱼类。共有13种物种受到国家级保护，包括云豹（ Neofelis nebulosa，易危物种）和东方鹳（ Ciconia boyciana，濒危物种）。
Standard.en: Huangshan provides habitat for numerous endemic and national plant species, some of which are threatened globally. Its extremely rich flora includes one-third of China's bryophytes (including mosses and liverworts) and more than half of its ferns. Huangshan is endemic to 13 fern species and 6 higher plant species, in addition to many other species endemic to the region or China. Besides these unique flora, Huangshan is home to over 300 important vertebrate species, including 48 mammal species, 170 bird species, 38 reptile species, 20 amphibian species, and 24 fish species. Thirteen species are under national protection, including the clouded leopard (Neofelis nebulosa, vulnerable) and the oriental stork (Ciconia boyciana, endangered).

Description.cn: 黄山常被誉为“中国最美的山”，自公元8世纪左右的唐代以来，它在中国艺术和文学史上扮演着重要的角色。公元747年，一个传说将黄山描述为发现长生不老药的地方。这个传说赋予了黄山“黄山”之名，也奠定了它在中国历史上的地位。黄山吸引了众多隐士、诗人以及山水画家，他们为这里壮丽的山峦景色所倾倒：无数花岗岩山峰耸立于云海之上，其中许多超过1000米。到了16世纪左右的明代，黄山的景色，以及众多奇形怪状的岩石和古树，激发了影响深远的山水画派的创作灵感，为世界想象和艺术中东方山水的形象奠定了基础。该遗产地位于中国安徽省亚热带季风湿润气候区，占地16060公顷，缓冲区达49000公顷，因其丰富的植物种类和对许多地方或国家特有植物物种的保护而具有突出的重要性，其中一些物种正面临灭绝的威胁
Description.en: Mount Huangshan, often described as the “loveliest mountain of China”, has played an important role in the history of art and literature in China since the Tang Dynasty around the 8th century, when a legend dated from the year 747 described the mountain as the place of discovery of the long-sought elixir of immortality.  This legend gave Mount Huangshan its name and assured its place in Chinese history.  Mount Huangshan became a magnet for hermits, poets and landscape artists, fascinated by its dramatic mountainous landscape consisting of numerous granitic peaks, many over 1,000 m high, emerging through a perpetual  sea of clouds.  During the Ming Dynasty from around the 16th century, this landscape and its numerous grotesquely-shaped rocks and ancient, gnarled trees inspired the influential Shanshui (“Mountain and Water”) school of landscape painting, providing a fundamental representation of the oriental landscape in the world’s imagination and art.The property, located in the humid subtropical monsoon climate zone of China’s Anhui Province and covering an area of 16,060 ha with a buffer zone of 49,000 ha, is also of outstanding importance for its botanical richness and for the conservation of a number of locally or nationally endemic plant species, some of which are threatened with extinction.

History_background.cn: 新石器时代有人类定居，三千年受崇拜
History_background.en: Humans settled there during the Neolithic period, and it was worshipped for three thousand years.

Main_function.cn: 文化遗产与自然景观游览
Main_function.en: Cultural Heritage and Natural Landscape Tours

BUilding_use.en: Sacrificing to Heaven and Earth and Preserving Cultural Relics

Brief_intro.cn: 中国著名圣山，具有非凡的历史、文化、美学和科学价值。早在新石器时代就有人类在此定居，是东方文化的重要发源地。
Brief_intro.en: China's most revered sacred mountain, Mount Taishan possesses exceptional historical, cultural, aesthetic, and scientific significance. Human settlement here dates back to the Neolithic period, making it an important cradle of Eastern cultural tradition.

Standard.cn: 泰山作为中国传统五岳之一，其景观是一项独特的艺术成就。沿着6660级台阶蜿蜒而上，点缀着11座山门、14座牌坊、14座亭台和4座阁楼，这些建筑不仅体现了人类的匠心独运，更是对这处壮丽自然景观的锦上添花。历经两千年演变，其规模之宏大，足以跻身人类历史上最伟大的成就之列。
Standard.en: Mount Tai, one of China's Five Sacred Mountains, boasts a landscape that is a unique artistic achievement. Winding its way up the 6,660 steps, one encounters 11 mountain gates, 14 memorial archways, 14 pavilions, and 4 towers. These structures not only showcase human ingenuity but also enhance the magnificent natural scenery. Having evolved over two millennia, its sheer scale places it among the greatest achievements in human history.

Standard.cn: 泰山是中国最受尊崇的山峰，两千年来对艺术发展产生了深远而广泛的影响。泰山上的泰山神庙和供奉其女老母的青云庙，都是泰山上的建筑原型，并在帝制时期被广泛借鉴，成为中国各地建筑的典范。山峦承载着人类活动的痕迹，优美的建筑——桥梁、城门或亭台楼阁——与幽暗的松林或险峻的峭壁形成鲜明对比，这种山峦的概念模型只能源于对泰山的借鉴。
Standard.en: Mount Tai, China's most revered mountain, has profoundly and extensively influenced the development of art for two millennia. The Temple of Mount Tai and the Qingyun Temple, dedicated to its goddess Nülaomu, are architectural prototypes of Mount Tai, widely referenced during the imperial period and becoming models for architecture throughout China. Mountains bear the marks of human activity; the elegant architecture—bridges, city gates, or pavilions—contrastes sharply with the dark pine forests or precipitous cliffs. This conceptual model of mountains could only have originated from the inspiration of Mount Tai.

Standard.cn: 泰山是古代中国文明遗迹的独特见证，尤其体现在其宗教、艺术和文学方面。两千年来，泰山一直是皇帝祭祀天地、举行丰山祭祀的主要场所之一，祭祀仪式由天子亲自主持。自汉代以来，泰山便与五行学说一起，成为象征天国的五座山峰之一，五行学说是中国思想的基本前提。
Standard.en: Mount Tai is a unique testament to ancient Chinese civilization, particularly in its religious, artistic, and literary aspects. For two thousand years, Mount Tai has been one of the main sites for emperors to worship Heaven and Earth and to hold the Fengshan Sacrifice, with the sacrificial ceremonies personally presided over by the emperor. Since the Han Dynasty, Mount Tai, along with the Five Elements theory, has been one of the five mountains symbolizing the Heavenly Kingdom, a fundamental premise of Chinese thought.

Standard.cn: 泰山是神圣山岳的杰出典范。位于泰山神庙内的天福宫（公元1008年）是中国现存三大宫殿之一。同样建于宋代的青云寺，其庭院和建筑布局体现了典型的山岳建筑群特征；而神石寺及其千佛殿则是规模宏大的寺庙建筑群的杰出完整范例。它们共同展现了唐宋时期的文化和宗教风貌。
Standard.en: Mount Tai is an outstanding example of a sacred mountain. The Tianfu Palace (built in 1008 AD) within the Taishan Temple is one of the three major palaces still existing in China. Qingyun Temple, also built in the Song Dynasty, embodies typical characteristics of mountain architecture in its courtyards and building layout; while Shenshi Temple and its Thousand Buddha Hall are outstanding examples of large-scale and complete temple complexes. Together, they showcase the cultural and religious landscape of the Tang and Song Dynasties.

Standard.cn: 泰山自然与文化整体包括新石器时代（大汶口）以来以祭祀中心形式存在的传统人类聚落，在游客增多和旅游业带来的不可逆转的变化的影响下，已成为传统文化的杰出代表。
Standard.en: Mount Tai's natural and cultural landscape encompasses traditional human settlements that have existed as sacrificial centers since the Neolithic Age (Dawenkou). Under the influence of increasing tourists and the irreversible changes brought about by the tourism industry, it has become an outstanding representative of traditional culture.

Standard.cn: 泰山与世界历史上一些重要性不容忽视的事件有着直接且具体的联系。这些事件包括儒家思想的兴起、中国的统一以及中国文字和文学的出现。
Standard.en: Mount Tai has direct and specific connections to some significant events in world history. These events include the rise of Confucianism, the unification of China, and the emergence of Chinese writing and literature.

Standard.cn: 泰山历经近30亿年的自然演化，通过复杂的地质和生物过程形成，最终成为一座覆盖着茂密植被、巍峨耸立于周围高原之上的巨大岩体。这座气势磅礴、雄伟壮丽的山峰，完美融合了秀丽的自然景观与数千年来人类活动的文化影响。
Standard.en: Mount Tai, formed over nearly 3 billion years through complex geological and biological processes, has become a massive rock formation covered in lush vegetation, towering majestically above the surrounding plateau. This imposing and magnificent mountain perfectly blends stunning natural scenery with the cultural influence of thousands of years of human activity.

Description.cn: 泰山是中国最著名的圣山，具有非凡的历史、文化、美学和科学价值。早在新石器时代就有人类在此定居（附近有一处大汶口遗址），三千多年来，泰山一直受到人们的崇拜。泰山是一座雄伟壮丽的岩石山体，占地25000公顷，海拔1545米，耸立于周围高原之上，被誉为中国最美丽的风景名胜之一，自古以来就是东方东亚文化的重要发源地。早在公元前219年，泰山就已成为山岳崇拜的重要对象。当时，秦始皇在凤山祭祀中向泰山献祭，以告知神明他统一天下的胜利。泰山上有12处有历史记载的祭祀天地的皇家仪式遗址，约1800块石碑和碑文，以及22座寺庙，这些共同使泰山成为中国最重要的古迹，举世闻名的历史文化宝库。泰山神庙是泰山最重要的古迹，庙内藏有公元1009年的道教名画《泰山神行图》。碑文包括汉代张骞、恒芳、金孙夫人的碑刻；北齐时期的佛经谷碑刻；唐玄宗的《泰山颂》；以及唐代的平行碑刻。此外，这里还生长着许多古树，包括六棵2100年前栽种的汉代柏树；1300年前栽种的唐代槐树；以及500年前栽种的迎宾松和五官松。所有这些建筑元素、绘画、雕塑、石刻和古树都与泰山的自然景观融为一体。
Description.en: Mount Taishan is the most famous sacred mountain of China, with exceptional historic, cultural, aesthetic and scientific value.  Settled by humans as early as the Neolithic (a Dawenkou site is nearby), the mountain has been worshipped continuously throughout the last three millennia.  A large and impressive rock mass covering 25,000 ha and rising to 1,545 m above the surrounding plateau, Mount Taishan is considered one of the most beautiful scenic spots in China and was an important cradle of oriental East Asian culture since the earliest times. The mountain was an important object of the cult worship of mountains even before 219 BCE, when the Qin Emperor, Huang Di, paid tribute to the mountain in the Fengshan sacrifices to inform the gods of his success in unifying all of China. On the mountain there are 12 historically recorded imperial ceremonies in homage to Heaven and Earth, about 1,800 stone tablets and inscriptions, and 22 temples, which together make Mount Taishan the most important monument in China, a world-renowned treasure house of history and culture.The key monument, the Temple to the God of Taishan, contains the Taoist masterpiece painting of 1,009 CE “The God of Taishan Making a Journey”. Inscriptions include the Han Dynasty stelae of Zhang Qian, Heng Fang and Madam Jin Sun; the Valley of Inscribed Buddhist Scriptures inscribed in the Northern Qi Dynasty; the Eulogium on Taishan by Tang Xuanzong, and the Parallel Stelae of the Tang Dynasty. There is also a number of ancient and significant trees, including six cypresses of the Han Dynasty planted 2,100 years ago; Sophora japonica of the Tang Dynasty planted 1,300 years ago, and the Guest-Greeting Pine and the Five-Bureaucrat Pine, both of which were planted some 500 years ago.  All the architectural elements, paintings, in situ sculptures, stone inscriptions and ancient trees are integrated into the landscape of Mount Taishan.

History_background.cn: 新儒学传播地，历史可追溯至商代
History_background.en: The history of the spread of Neo-Confucianism can be traced back to the Shang Dynasty.

Main_function.cn: 生物多样性保护与文化遗产展示
Main_function.en: Biodiversity conservation and cultural heritage display

BUilding_use.cn: 寺庙、书院和遗址供学术与宗教活动
BUilding_use.en: Temples, academies, and ruins served for academic and religious activities.

Brief_intro.cn: 世界上最杰出的亚热带森林之一，拥有丰富生物多样性和众多历史文化遗址，同时也是新儒家思想的发源地。
Brief_intro.en: One of the world's most outstanding subtropical forests, Mount Wuyi harbors exceptional biodiversity and numerous historic cultural sites, and is also the birthplace of Neo-Confucian thought.

Standard.cn: 武夷山是一处风景秀丽的自然景观，已受到一千二百多年的保护。山上分布着一系列杰出的考古遗址，包括公元前1世纪建立的汉城，以及与公元11世纪新儒学诞生相关的众多寺庙和学堂。
Standard.en: Wuyi Mountain is a scenic natural landscape that has been protected for over 1,200 years. The mountain is dotted with a series of outstanding archaeological sites, including a Han city built in the 1st century BC, and numerous temples and schools associated with the birth of Neo-Confucianism in the 11th century AD.

Standard.cn: 武夷山是新儒家思想的发源地，这种学说在东亚和东南亚国家占据主导地位长达数个世纪，并影响了世界大部分地区的哲学和政治。
Standard.en: Wuyi Mountain is the birthplace of Neo-Confucianism, a doctrine that dominated East and Southeast Asian countries for centuries and influenced philosophy and politics in much of the world.

Standard.cn: 九曲溪（下峡谷）东部风景区地貌壮丽，景色绝佳，耸立着众多由当地红色砂岩构成的孤立陡峭巨石。这些巨石在长达10公里的蜿蜒河段中占据主导地位，高出河床200至400米，最终汇入清澈深邃的溪流。古老的崖道是该景区的重要组成部分，游客可由此俯瞰河流全景。
Standard.en: The eastern scenic area of Jiuxi River (Lower Canyon) boasts magnificent landforms and stunning scenery, featuring numerous isolated, steep boulders composed of local red sandstone. These boulders dominate the 10-kilometer-long winding river section, rising 200 to 400 meters above the riverbed before finally flowing into the clear, deep stream. Ancient cliff paths are an important part of the scenic area, offering visitors panoramic views of the river.

Standard.cn: 武夷山是世界上最杰出的亚热带森林之一。它是中国亚热带森林和华南雨林中保存最完好的森林之一，也是最具代表性的大型森林，植物多样性极高。这里栖息着大量古老孑遗植物，其中许多是中国特有种，在国内其他地区也极为罕见。武夷山的动物多样性也十分丰富，尤其以爬行动物、两栖动物和昆虫种类最为突出。
Standard.en: Wuyishan is one of the world's most outstanding subtropical forests. It is one of the best-preserved subtropical forests and rainforests in China, and also one of the most representative large forests, boasting extremely high plant diversity. It is home to a large number of ancient relict plants, many of which are endemic to China and extremely rare in other parts of the country. Wuyishan also possesses rich animal diversity, particularly in reptiles, amphibians, and insects.

Description.cn: 武夷山位于中国东南部的福建省，是保存最完好的中国亚热带森林和华南雨林中生物多样性最丰富、最具代表性的森林之一。该遗产地对生物多样性保护具有极其重要的意义，是众多古老孑遗植物物种的避难所，其中许多是中国特有物种。此外，武夷山还拥有极其丰富的动植物资源，包括大量的爬行动物、两栖动物和昆虫。九曲河峡谷风光旖旎，景色壮丽，平缓的岩壁与清澈深邃的河水交相辉映，构成一幅绝美的画卷。沿河分布着众多寺庙和修道院，其中许多如今已成废墟。这些遗址曾是新儒学发展和传播的沃土。自11世纪以来，新儒学作为一种政治哲学，对东亚文化产生了深远的影响。尤其值得一提的是，这里至少有35座古代儒学书院，其历史可追溯至北宋至清代（公元10至19世纪）。此外，该地区还拥有可追溯至商代（公元前2世纪）的墓葬、碑刻和石窟，石窟内有木舟棺。同时，这里也保存着60多座道教寺庙和修道院的遗址。公元前1世纪，汉代统治者在附近的城村建造了一座大型行政都城。其高大的城墙环绕着一处具有重要意义的考古遗址。 该遗产地由四个保护区组成：西部的武夷山国家级自然保护区、中部的九曲溪生态保护区和东部的武夷山国家风景名胜区彼此相连，而位于东南约15公里处的汉代遗址保护区则是一个独立的区域。遗产地总面积107,044公顷，周围环绕着40,170公顷的缓冲区，并因其文化、风景和生物多样性价值而被列入世界遗产名录。
Description.en: Mount Wuyi, located in China’s south-east province of Fujian, contains the largest, most representative example of a largely intact forest encompassing the diversity of the Chinese Subtropical Forest and the South Chinese Rainforest.  Of enormous importance for biodiversity conservation, the property acts as a refuge for an important number of ancient, relict plant species, many of them endemic to China, and contains an extremely rich flora and fauna, including significant numbers of reptile, amphibian and insect species.The serene beauty of the dramatic gorges of the Nine-Bend River is of exceptional scenic quality in its juxtaposition of smooth rock cliffs with clear, deep water. Situated along this river are numerous temples and monasteries, many now in ruins, which provided the setting for the development and spread of Neo-Confucianism, a political philosophy which has been very influential in the cultures of East Asia since the 11th century. In particular there are no fewer than 35 ancient Confucian academies dating from the Northern Song to Qing Dynasties (10th to 19th centuries CE). In addition the area contains tombs, inscriptions and rock shelters with wooden boat coffins dating back to the Shang Dynasty (2nd century BCE), and the remains of more than 60 Taoist temples and monasteries.In the 1st century BCE a large administrative capital was built at nearby Chengcun by the Han Dynasty rulers.  Its massive walls enclose an archaeological site of great significance. The property consists of four protected areas: Wuyishan National Nature Reserve in the west, Nine-Bend Stream Ecological Protection Area in the centre and Wuyishan National Scenic Area in the east are contiguous, and the Protection Area for the Remains of Ancient Han Dynasty is a separate area, about 15km to the south-east. Totalling 107,044 ha, the property is surrounded by a buffer zone of 40,170 ha and has been inscribed for cultural as well as scenic and biodiversity values.
